nodes.name: Branching random walk
nodes.statement: A \emph{branching random walk} (\textsc{brw}\xspace{}) models a population of individuals that evolves in discrete time and in space. Start with a single individual at generation 0. Afterwards, at every generation, each individual reproduces independently of the others and then dies, giving birth to a random number of offsprings. Each offspring inherits the position of its parent, plus some random displacement.
nodes.statement_short: A BRW: individuals reproduce independently each generation; offspring inherit parent's position plus a random displacement.

nodes.name: Subcritical, critical and supercritical BRW
nodes.statement: The \textsc{brw}\xspace is \emph{subcritical} if $m<1$, \emph{critical} if $m=1$, and \emph{supercritical} if $m>1$.

nodes.name: Centered BRW
nodes.statement: In the subcritical and critical case, the \emph{drift}, i.e. the expected mean displacement of the offsprings of a particle, also matters; we say that the \textsc{brw}\xspace is \emph{centered} if this drift is zero.

nodes.name: Maximum displacement
nodes.statement: The \emph{maximum displacement} is the maximal position attained by an individual across all generations.

nodes.name: Lalley–Shao tail for stable branching Lévy process
nodes.statement: Offspring distributions having finite variance are found in \cite{lalley2016maximalstable}, which works on a critical branching Lévy process with binary branching where the displacement follows a symmetric stable process with index $\alpha$. They obtain an asymptotic of the tail on the maximum displacement in $\P(M \geq t) \sim (2/\alpha)^{1/2} t^{-\alpha/2}$, see also \cite{profeta2021extreme} when the displacement is a critical or subcritical $\alpha$-stable Lévy process with positive jumps, and \cite{profeta2024maximal} for spectrally negative Lévy processes---more on that later.
nodes.statement_short: For critical binary branching symmetric alpha-stable Lévy process, P(M>=t) ~ (2/alpha)^{1/2} t^{-alpha/2}.

nodes.name: Exponential tail for subcritical BRW (Neuman–Zheng)
nodes.statement: \cite{neuman2017maximal} consider a subcritical \textsc{brw}\xspace where the offspring distribution has finite third moment and the distribution of the displacements has an exponential moment, and shows that the maximum displacement has an exponential tail; the exponential moment on the displacements is crucial.

nodes.name: Lalley–Shao r^{-2} tail of the maximum displacement
nodes.statement: While the distribution of the maximum displacement of a critical \textsc{brw}\xspace depends on the \emph{reproduction scheme}, i.e. the joint distribution of the displacements of offsprings, and is not universal, the tail is: \cite{lalley2015maximal} established that the probability that the maximum displacement exceeds $r$ behaves like a constant times $r^{-2}$ as $r\to\infty$, where the constant depends on the reproduction scheme\xspace.
nodes.statement_short: For critical BRW the probability that the maximum displacement exceeds r is asymptotically a constant times r^{-2}.

nodes.name: Ulam–Harris tree
nodes.statement: Define $\UU := \cup_{n\geq 0} \N_*^n$ the infinite Ulam--Harris tree of finite sequences of natural numbers, where $\N_*^0 = \{\emptyset\}$, $\N_* = \{1, 2, \dots\}$ and $\N = \N_* \cup \{0\}$.

nodes.name: Concatenation and length
nodes.statement: If $u,v \in \UU$, denote $uv$ their concatenation and $|u|$ the length of $u$.

nodes.name: Ancestor and parent
nodes.statement: We say that $u$ is an ancestor of $v$ if and only if there exists $w\in\UU$ such that $v = uw$; if $|w|=1$ then $u$ is the parent of $v$, denoted by $p(v)$.

nodes.name: Ancestral line
nodes.statement: For every $u\in \UU$, the ancestral line of $u$ is the sequence $(u_0 = \emptyset, u_1, \dots, u_{|u|} = u)$ where for every $0\leq j \leq |u|$, $u_j$ is the only ancestor of $u$ with $|u_j|=j$.

nodes.name: Tree (planar)
nodes.statement: A tree $T \subset \UU$ is a subset of $\UU$ such that $\emptyset \in T$, and for every $u = p(u)k$ with $k\in \N_*$, $p(u) \in T$ and $p(u) j \in T$ for every $0\leq j \leq k$.

nodes.name: Offspring numbers k_v
nodes.statement: Let $k_v$ be i.i.d. $\N$-valued random variables with common distribution $\mu$.

nodes.name: Bienaymé–Galton–Watson tree
nodes.statement: The Bienaymé--Galton--Watson tree with offspring distribution $\mu$ is the tree $T$ such that $\emptyset \in T$, and for every $u\in \UU$, $u \in T$ if and only if $p(u)\in T$ and $u = p(u)j$ with $1\leq j \leq k_{p(u)}$.

nodes.name: Bienaymé–Galton–Watson process
nodes.statement: The number of vertices in $T$ at generation $n$, $N_n := \#\{ v \in \N_*^n, v\in T\}$ follows a Bienaymé--Galton--Watson process.

nodes.name: Critical BGW tree
nodes.statement: If $\sum_{n\geq 0} n \mu(n) = 1$ we say that the Bienaymé--Galton--Watson tree (resp. process) is critical.

nodes.name: Extinction of critical BGW process
nodes.statement: Assuming $\mu(1) < 1$, the process goes extinct almost surely, i.e. $N_n \to 0$ almost surely as $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Point process
nodes.statement: A (real-valued) point process is a random variable with values in the set $\M$ of all counting measures over $\R$, i.e. the set of all measures $\mu$ such that $\mu(A) \in \N \cup \{\infty\}$ for every Borel set $A$, equipped with the sigma-algebra generated by the collection of $\mu \mapsto \mu(A)$ over all Borel sets $A$.

nodes.name: Supremum of a measure
nodes.statement: We let $\sup \mu$ be the supremum of the support of $\mu$, with $\sup\mu = -\infty$ if $\mu = 0$.

nodes.name: Finite point process
nodes.statement: A point process $\chi$ is finite if $\chi(\R)<\infty$ almost surely; in this case there exists a measurable enumeration $(X_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)}$ of the atoms of $\chi$, i.e. a family of random variables such that $\chi = \sum_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)} \delta_{X_i}$ with $\delta_x$ the Dirac mass at $x$ --- for example, we can enumerate the atoms in increasing order.

nodes.name: Mean measure
nodes.statement: The mean measure of a point process $\chi$ is the measure $M : A \mapsto \E[\chi(A)]$ for every Borel set $A$.

nodes.name: Campbell measure C
nodes.statement: Following \cite{baccelli2009stochastic}, define the measure $C$ on $\R\times \M$ by \[ C(A \times \Gamma) = \E\left[ \int_A \ind{\chi - \delta_x \in \Gamma} \d \chi(x) \right] . \]

nodes.name: Reduced Palm distribution
nodes.statement: Since $C(\cdot , \Gamma)$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $M$ for every $\Gamma$, we have \[ C(A\times \Gamma) = \int_A P_x(\Gamma) \d M(x) . \] When $M$ is locally finite, the function $(x,\Gamma) \mapsto P_x(\Gamma)$ can be made into a stochastic kernel; we call $P_x$ the reduced Palm distribution of $\chi$ at $x$.

nodes.name: Reduced Campbell–Little–Mecke formula
nodes.statement: We then have the reduced Campbell--Little--Mecke formula: for every positive and measurable, resp. bounded and measurable $f$, \begin{equation} \E\left[\int f(x, \chi-\delta_x) \d \chi(x) \right] = \int f(x, \phi) \d P_x(\phi) \d M(x) . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Reduced Campbell–Little–Mecke formula (1)
nodes.statement: \E\left[\int f(x, \chi-\delta_x) \d \chi(x) \right] = \int f(x, \phi) \d P_x(\phi) \d M(x) .
nodes.label: eq:Campbell-Little-Mecke

nodes.name: Mean measure of the Palm distribution M_x
nodes.statement: A point process distributed under $P_x$ has itself a mean measure, which we denote by $M_x$.

nodes.name: Campbell–Little–Mecke formula for the Palm mean measure
nodes.statement: For every positive and measurable, resp. bounded and measurable $f$, \begin{equation} \E\left[\int \left(\int f(x,y) \d(\chi-\delta_x)(y)\right) \d\chi(x) \right] = \int \left( \int f(x, y) \d M_x(y) \right) \d M(x) . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (2)
nodes.statement: \E\left[\int \left(\int f(x,y) \d(\chi-\delta_x)(y)\right) \d\chi(x) \right] = \int \left( \int f(x, y) \d M_x(y) \right) \d M(x) .
nodes.label: eq:Campbell-Little-Mecke-mean

nodes.name: Reproduction scheme
nodes.statement: Let $\BB := (\chi, \Lambda, D, (X_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)})$, where $\chi$ is a point process, $\Lambda\geq 0$ a random variable with $\Lambda\geq \sup\chi$ a.s., $D\geq 0$, and $(X_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)}$ is a measurable enumeration of the atoms of $\chi$.

nodes.name: Decorated branching random walk
nodes.statement: We define the decorated \textsc{brw}\xspace $(T, (D_v)_{v\in T}, (X_v)_{v\in T}, (\Lambda_v)_{v\in T})$ with \emph{reproduction scheme} $\BB$ as follows. Let $(\chi_u, \Lambda^{(u)}, D_u, (X^{(u)}_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi_u(\R)})_{u\in\UU}$ be i.i.d. copies of $\BB$. For every $u\in\UU$, let $k_u := \chi_u(\R)$, and let $T$ be the tree constructed from the $(k_u)_u$ (it is a Bienaymé--Galton--Watson tree). Define $X_\emptyset = 0$, $\Lambda_\emptyset = \Lambda^{(\emptyset)}$, and for every $u = p(u) j \in T$, define $X_u = X_{p(u)} + X^{(p(u))}_j$ and $\Lambda_u = X_u + \Lambda^{(u)}$. The joint process $(T, (D_u)_{u\in T}, (X_u)_{u\in T}, (\Lambda_u)_{u\in T})$ defines the decorated \textsc{brw}\xspace with reproduction scheme\xspace $\BB$.
nodes.statement_short: Decorated BRW built from i.i.d. copies of the reproduction scheme on the Ulam–Harris tree: positions X_u, decorations Λ_u, weights D_u.

nodes.name: Generation-n point process G_n
nodes.statement: We write $G_n := \sum_{u\in T, |u|=n} \delta_{X_u}$ for the point process of its vertices at generation $n$.

nodes.name: Assumptions (critical, centered, finite variance, o(r^{-4}) decoration tail)
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item the \textsc{brw}\xspace is critical: $\E[\chi(\R)] = M(\R) = 1$, \item the \textsc{brw}\xspace is centered: $\E\left[ \int x \d\chi(x)\right] = \int x \d M(x) = 0$, \item $\E[\chi(\R)^2] = \sigma^2 + 1 \in (1, \infty)$, \item $\E\left[\int x^2 \d\chi(x)\right] = \int x^2 \d M(x) = \eta^2 \in (0, \infty)$, \item $\P(\Lambda>r) = o(r^{-4})$ as $r\to\infty$, \item $\E[D] = 1$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Critical, centered BRW with finite offspring variance sigma^2, finite displacement variance eta^2, P(Lambda>r)=o(r^{-4}), E[D]=1.
nodes.label: assum

nodes.name: Remark on Assumptions
nodes.statement: Note that 3. and 4. imply that the reproduction scheme\xspace is non-degenerate, i.e. that $\P(\chi(\R) = 1) < 1$ and $M(\{0\}) < 1$. Point 5. holds if $\E[\Lambda^4]<\infty$, see Lemma \ref{lem:refined-Markov}. Point 6. is here to simplify notations and could be replaced by ``$D$ is an integrable, non-negative and not a.s. zero random variable'' up to an extra constant in the statements of Theorems \ref{th:main-volume-smaller} and \ref{th:main-condition-vol}.

nodes.name: Tail of the maximum decoration
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{assum}, asymptotically as $r\to\infty$, \[ \P\left(\sup_{v\in T} \Lambda_v > r\right) \sim \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2 r^2} . \]
nodes.statement_short: P(sup of decorations > r) ~ 6 eta^2/(sigma^2 r^2) as r -> infinity.
nodes.label: th:main-tail

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary (maximum displacement tail)
nodes.statement: Taking $\Lambda = \sup(0, \sup\chi)$, we get the immediate corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Specialize Theorem 1 to Lambda = max(0, sup chi).

nodes.name: Tail of the maximum displacement
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{assum}, asymptotically as $r\to\infty$, \[ \P\left(\sup_{v\in T} X_v > r\right) \sim \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2 r^2} . \]
conclusions: asymptotically as $r\to\infty$, \[ \P\left(\sup_{v\in T} X_v > r\right) \sim \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2 r^2} . \]
nodes.statement_short: P(maximum displacement > r) ~ 6 eta^2/(sigma^2 r^2).
nodes.label: cor:main-tail

nodes.name: Generalization of Lalley–Shao
nodes.statement: This corollary is a generalization of \cite[Theorem 1]{lalley2015maximal}, which is established for the specific reproduction scheme\xspace $\chi = L \delta_X$ with $X$ in $L^{4+\varepsilon}(\Z)$, $\E[X]=0$, $\E[L^3]<\infty$ and $\E[L]=1$ (and which can be extended to $X\in L^4$ and $L\in L^2$ with minimal effort). We extend it to very general reproduction schemes\xspace, with a \textsc{brw}\xspace that is not necessarily in $\Z$, and with minimal moment assumptions.

nodes.name: Maximum span
nodes.statement: The maximum span of a random variable is the largest $d$ such that there exists $x$ such that the support of the random variable is contained in $x+d\Z$.

nodes.name: Point probability of the maximum decoration
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{assum}, if $M$ is supported on $\Z$ and has maximal span $1$ and if $\Lambda$ is $\N$-valued, then asymptotically as $r\to\infty$ with $r\in \N$, \[ \P\left(\sup_{v\in T} \Lambda_v = r\right) \sim \frac{12 \eta^2}{\sigma^2 r^3} . \]
assumptions: $M$ is supported on $\Z$ and has maximal span $1$
nodes.statement_short: For lattice BRW, P(max decoration = r) ~ 12 eta^2/(sigma^2 r^3).
nodes.label: th:main-condition

nodes.name: Remark on densities
nodes.statement: It is likely that such an asymptotic could be established for displacements that have a density with respect to the Lebesgue measure, but we chose not to investigate this.

nodes.name: Laplace transform of the total weight conditioned on the maximum
nodes.statement: Let $\psi$ be the unique positive solution of \[ \psi'' = \psi^2 + \psi \] with $\psi(x)\to\infty$ as $x\to 0$ and $\psi(x)\to 0$ as $x\to\infty$. For every $\alpha>0$, define \[\RR(\alpha) = \frac{6 \eta^2}{\sigma^2} \left(\frac{2\alpha}{\sigma^2} \psi\left( \sqrt{\frac{12\alpha}{\sigma^2}}\right) - 1 + \frac{\alpha}{\sigma^2} \right).\] Then $\RR$ can be extended to $0$ by continuity with a series expansion as $\alpha\searrow 0$ \[ \frac{\sigma^2}{6\eta^2} \RR(\alpha) = \frac{3}{5}\left(\frac{\alpha}{\sigma^2}\right)^2 - \frac{2}{7}\left(\frac{\alpha}{\sigma^2}\right)^3 + \frac{3}{25}\left(\frac{\alpha}{\sigma^2}\right)^4 + \dots \] and under Assumptions \ref{assum}, if $t(r,\alpha) = \frac{\alpha^2}{2\sigma^2} \left(\frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2 r^2}\right)^2$, \[ r^2\left( 1 - \E\left[ \e^{-t(r,\alpha)\sum_{v\in T} D_v} \, | \, \sup_v \Lambda_v \leq r \right]\right) \ulim r \infty \RR(\alpha) \] and \[ \E\left[ \e^{-t(r,\alpha)\sum_{v\in T} D_v} \, | \, \sup_v \Lambda_v > r \right] \ulim r \infty \frac{2\alpha}{\sigma^2}\psi\left( \sqrt{\frac{12\alpha}{\sigma^2}} \right) . \]
conclusions: Then $\RR$ can be extended to $0$ by continuity with a series expansion as $\alpha\searrow 0$
nodes.statement_short: With t = alpha^2/(2 sigma^2) w(r)^2, the Laplace transform of the total weight conditioned on max<=r or >r converges to explicit limits via the ODE psi''=psi^2+psi.
nodes.label: th:main-volume-smaller

nodes.name: Laplace transform of the total weight conditioned on max = r
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{assum}, if $M$ is supported on $\Z$ and has maximal span $1$ and if $\Lambda$ is $\N$-valued, then \[ \E\left[ \e^{-t(r,\alpha)\sum_{v\in T} D_v} \, | \, \sup_v \Lambda_v = r \right] \ulim r \infty \frac{2\alpha}{\sigma^2}\psi\left( \sqrt{\frac{12\alpha}{\sigma^2}} \right) . \]
assumptions: $M$ is supported on $\Z$ and has maximal span $1$
nodes.statement_short: Conditioned on the maximum decoration equal to r, the weight Laplace transform has the same limit as conditioning on > r.
nodes.label: th:main-condition-vol

nodes.name: Lalley–Shao counterexample without fourth moment
nodes.statement: As already observed in \cite{lalley2015maximal} in the case $\chi = N \delta_X$ with $N$ and $X$ independent, there are counter-examples when $X \notin L^4$.
nodes.section: 2.3 On the minimality of our hypotheses

nodes.name: Behaviour with non-zero drift
nodes.statement: When $\E[\int x \d\chi(x)] \neq 0$ we also expect a different behavior, namely: if it is positive, then the probability in Theorem \ref{th:main-tail} should behave like $r^{-1}$, and if it is negative then the tail should be much lighter.
nodes.section: 2.3 On the minimality of our hypotheses
conclusions: if it is positive, then the probability in Theorem \ref{th:main-tail} should behave like $r^{-1}$
if it is negative then the tail should be much lighter

nodes.name: Miermont: multitype BRW converges to the Brownian snake
nodes.statement: Theorem 3 in \cite{miermont2008invarianceGW} establishes the convergence of the multitype \textsc{brw}\xspace towards the Brownian snake. The assumption requires exponential moments on the offspring distribution (in our monotype setting, this is the distribution of $\chi(\R)$) and ---roughly speaking--- moments of order $8+\varepsilon$ on the displacement for some $\varepsilon>0$ (in our monotype setting this would mean $\E[\int x^{8+\varepsilon} \d\chi(x)]<\infty$).

nodes.name: Miermont's moment conjecture
nodes.statement: The authors conjectured in the remark after \cite[Theorem 4]{miermont2008invarianceGW} that this assumption could be reduced to a moment of order $4+\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Multitype planar tree
nodes.statement: A multitype planar tree is a tree $T\subset \UU$ together with a type function $\bs:T\to \kX$, where $\kX$ is a set of types (in our case finite).

nodes.name: Multitype offspring point processes
nodes.statement: Assume that for every $x\in\kX$ we have a point process $\chi^{(x)}$ on $\R\times\kX$, together with a measurable numbering $(X^{(x)}_i, s^{(x)}_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi^{(x)}(\R\times\kX)}$ of its atoms. For every $y\in\kX$, the point process $\chi^{(x)}(\cdot \times \{y\})$ represents the point process of offsprings that are of type $y$, and for every $1\leq i \leq \chi^{(x)}(\R\times\kX)$, $X^{(x)}_i$ is the displacement the $i$-th child respective to its parent, and $s^{(x)}_i$ is its type.

nodes.name: Multitype decorated branching random walk
nodes.statement: Given a multitype reproduction scheme\xspace $\BB := (\chi^{(x)}, \Lambda^{(x)}, D^{(x)}, (X^{(x)}_i, s^{(x)}_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi^{(x)}(\R\times\kX)})_{x\in\kX}$, where $D^{(x)}\geq 0$, $\Lambda^{(x)}\geq \sup\chi^{(x)}$ a.s. for every $x\in\kX$ and $(X^{(x)}_i, s^{(x)}_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi^{(x)}(\R\times\kX)}$ is a measurable numbering of $\chi^{(x)}$, we define the multitype decorated \textsc{brw}\xspace $(T, \bs, (D_v)_{v\in T}, (X_v)_{v\in T}, (\Lambda_v)_{v\in T})$ with reproduction scheme\xspace $\BB$, where $T\subset \UU$, $\bs:T\to\kX$, $D_v\geq 0$, and $X_v, \Lambda_v \in \R$ for every $v\in T$, and the probabilities $(\P_{x})_{x\in\kX}$ with associated expectations $(\E_x)_{x\in\kX}$, by induction as follows. For every $s_\emptyset\in\kX$, under $\P_{s_\emptyset}$, let $\left((\chi^{(x)}_u, \Lambda^{(x)}_u, (X^{(x)}_{u,i}, s^{(x)}_{u,i})_{1\leq i \leq \chi^{(x)}_u(\R\times\kX)})_{x\in\kX}\right)_{u\in \UU}$ be an i.i.d. family with common distribution the same as $\BB$. Then $\emptyset \in T$, $\bs(\emptyset) = s_\emptyset$, and $X_\emptyset = 0$, and for every $n\geq 1$ and $u\in\UU$ with $|u|=n$ and $u = vw$ with $v=p(u)$, \begin{itemize} \item $u\in T$ if and only if $1\leq w \leq \chi^{(\bs(v))}_v(\R\times\kX)$, \item $\bs(u) = s^{(\bs(v))}_{v, w}$, \item $X_u = X_v + X^{(\bs(v))}_{v,w}$. \end{itemize} In addition, for every $u\in T$, we define \begin{itemize} \item $\Lambda_u = X_u + \Lambda^{(\bs(u))}_u$, \item $D_u = D^{(\bs(u))}_u$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Inductive construction of the multitype decorated BRW from i.i.d. per-type reproduction schemes.

nodes.name: Raphaëlis: reduced BRW is critical with finite variance
nodes.statement: This can be provided in part by \cite{miermont2008invarianceGW, raphaelis2017scaling}; for example, Proposition 2 in \cite{raphaelis2017scaling} ensures that the reduced \textsc{brw}\xspace satisfies 1. and 3. in Assumptions \ref{assum}.

nodes.name: Non-degeneracy of the multitype process
nodes.statement: Assume that the process is non-degenerate in the sense of \cite{miermont2008invarianceGW}, i.e. that there exists at least one $x\in\kX$ such that $\P(\chi^{(x)}(\R\times\kX) = 1)<1$.

nodes.name: Mean offspring matrix entries M_{x,y}
nodes.statement: Define for every $x,y\in\kX$ \begin{equation} M_{x,y} = \E\left[\chi^{(x)}(\R \times \{y\}) \right] \end{equation} the average number of type $y$ offspring of a type $x$ vertex, and assume that $M_{x,y} < \infty$ for every $x,y$.

nodes.name: Equation (3)
nodes.statement: M_{x,y} = \E\left[\chi^{(x)}(\R \times \{y\}) \right]
nodes.label: eq:def-M

nodes.name: Mean offspring matrix M
nodes.statement: We see them as the $(x,y)$ entry of matrix $M$, whose iterates we write $M^n = (M^n_{x,y})_{x,y\in\kX}$.

nodes.name: Irreducibility of M
nodes.statement: We suppose that $M$ is irreducible, i.e. for every $x,y$ there exists $n\geq 1$ such that $M^n_{x,y}>0$.

nodes.name: Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue and eigenvectors
nodes.statement: By the Perron-Frobenius theorem $M$ has a largest eigenvalue $\rho$ and a left eigenvector $\ba = (a_x)_{x\in\kX}$ and a right eigenvector $\bb = (b_x)_{x\in\kX}$ associated to this eigenvalue, both unique up to multiplication by a constant and both with positive entries.

nodes.name: Remark on non-irreducible M
nodes.statement: In many cases we can handle a non-irreducible $M$, in particular when there are subsets of the space of of states that are transient (hence not visited if we start from a recurrent $x$). Naturally we can discard any state that cannot be reached from the initial one, i.e. any $y$ with $M^n_{x,y} = 0$ for every $n$. We can also often handle the presence of multiple communicating classes, i.e. subsets $S$ of states such that for every $y,z\in S$ we have $M^n_{y,z}>0$ for some $n$. For every communicating class we can restrict the matrix $M$ to it. The restriction is irreducible. Then $M$ will have maximal eigenvalue $1$ if and only if for at least one of its communicating classes, the restriction of $M$ on this class has maximal eigenvalue $1$ (such a class is ``critical’’); and if the restriction of $M$ on each of its communicating classes has eigenvalue at most $1$ (if it is $<1$ the class is ``subcritical’’). If $M$ has only one critical communicating class then we can incorporate the other classes into the decorations $D$ and $\Lambda$ of the states of the unique critical communicating class, and define a reduced \textsc{brw}\xspace with state space the critical class. In this case it is necessary that the state through which we reduce belongs to the critical class.
nodes.statement_short: Non-irreducible M can often be handled by restricting to the unique critical communicating class and absorbing other classes into decorations.

nodes.name: Ancestor order
nodes.statement: For every $u,v\in\UU$, write $u \preceq v$ if $u$ is an ancestor of $v$ (i.e. if there exists $w\in\UU$ such that $v = uw$) and $u\prec v$ if $u\preceq v$ and $u\neq v$.

nodes.name: Excursion trees T_u and point processes L_u
nodes.statement:
Following the idea of \cite[Definition 1]{raphaelis2017scaling}, for every $u\in\UU$ define random trees \[ \TT_u = \{ v\in T :  orall u \prec w \prec v,  s(w) 
eq x \} \quad , \quad \widetilde\TT_u = \{v\in T:  orall u \preceq w \prec v,  s(w) 
eq x\} , \] subsets \[ \partial\TT_u = \{ v\in \TT_u:  s(v) = x, v
eq u\} \quad , \quad \partial\widetilde\TT_u = \{v\in\widetilde\TT_u :  s(v)=x\} \] ordered in lexicographic order, \[ \TT_u^\circ = \TT_u \setminus \partial\TT_u \quad , \quad \widetilde\TT_u^\circ = \widetilde\TT_u \setminus \partial\widetilde\TT_u , \] and point processes \[ \LL_u = \sum_{v\in\partial\TT_u, v
eq\emptyset} \delta_{X_v} \quad , \quad \widetilde\LL_u = \sum_{v\in\partial\widetilde\TT_u} \delta_{X_v} . \]
nodes.statement_short: Subtrees between consecutive type-x vertices, their boundaries and boundary point processes.

nodes.name: Reduced reproduction scheme
nodes.statement: Define $\BB^r_u = (\LL_u, \sup_{v\in\TT_u^\circ} \Lambda_v, \sum_{v\in\TT_u^\circ} D_v, (X_i)_{i \in \partial\TT_u} )$.

nodes.name: Reduced (monotype) BRW
nodes.statement: In addition, we can define a new tree $\T$, a collection $(\B_u)_{u\in\T}$ and a function $t:\T\to T$ by induction with $\emptyset\in\T$, $t(\emptyset) = \emptyset$, and if $u\in\T$ then $\B_u = \BB^r_{t(u)}$, and letting $(v_1, \dots, v_d)$ be the elements of $\partial\TT_{t(u)}$, we let $ui\in \T$ and $t(ui) = v_i$ for every $1\leq i \leq d$. Then the family $(\B_u)_{u\in\T}$ is i.i.d. conditionally on $\T$, and from $\T$ and the family $(\B_u)_{u\in\T}$ we can construct the reduced (monotype) \textsc{brw}\xspace $(\T, (\D_u)_{u\in\T}, (\X_u)_{u\in\T}, (\Lambda^\T_u)_{u\in\T})$, and we can check that \[ \sum_{u\in\T} \D_u = \sum_{u\in T} D_u \quad , \quad \sup_{u\in\T} \Lambda^\T_u = \sup_{u\in T} \Lambda_u . \]
nodes.statement_short: The type-x vertices form a monotype decorated BRW with the same total weight and maximal decoration.

nodes.name: Matrices tilde M, N, O
nodes.statement: For every $y,z\in\kX$ let \[ \widetilde{M}_{y,z} = \begin{cases} M_{y,z} &\text{ if } y\neq x\\ 0 &\text{ if } y=x \end{cases} \quad , \quad N_{y,z} = \E\left[\int t \ind{s=z} \d\chi^{(y)}(t,s)\right] \quad , \quad O_{y,z} = \E\left[\int t^2 \ind{s=z} \d\chi^{(y)}(t,s)\right] \] and recall that $\bb$ is the right eigenvector of $M$ associated to its largest eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Multitype assumptions
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item the matrix $M$ has maximal eigenvalue $1$, \item $\left\{\left(M(I-\widetilde{M})^{-1} + I\right) N \bb\right\}_x = 0$, \item for every $y\in\kX$, $\E[\chi^{(y)}(\R\times\kX)^2] < \infty$, \item for every $y\in\kX$, $\E\left[\int t^2 \d\chi^{(y)}(t,s) \right] < \infty$, and \[ \eta^2 = \left\{ \left(M (I-\widetilde{M})^{-1} + I\right) \left( O + N(I-\widetilde{M})^{-1} N \right) \bb \right\}_x / b_x \] is non-zero (this is the variance of the displacement of the reduced \textsc{brw}\xspace), \item for every $y\in\kX$, $\P(\Lambda^{(y)}>r) = o(r^{-4})$ as $r\to\infty$, \item for every $y\in\kX$, $\E[D^{(y)}]<\infty$, and there exists one $y\in\kX$ with $\E[D^{(y)}]>0$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Perron eigenvalue 1, reduced centering, finite second moments, nonzero reduced variance eta^2, o(r^{-4}) decoration tails, integrable weights.
nodes.label: assum-multitype

nodes.name: Reduced BRW satisfies the assumptions iff multitype assumptions hold
nodes.statement: The reduced \textsc{brw}\xspace satisfies Assumptions \ref{assum} (replacing 6. by $\E[\D]\in (0,\infty)$), hence the multitype \textsc{brw}\xspace satisfies Theorems \ref{th:main-tail} to \ref{th:main-condition-vol}, if and only if the multitype \textsc{brw}\xspace satisfies Assumptions \ref{assum-multitype}.
conclusions: The reduced \textsc{brw}\xspace satisfies Assumptions \ref{assum} (replacing 6. by $\E[\D]\in (0,\infty)$), hence the multitype \textsc{brw}\xspace satisfies Theorems \ref{th:main-tail} to \ref{th:main-condition-vol}, if and only if the multitype \textsc{brw}\xspace satisfies Assumptions \ref{assum-multitype}.
nodes.label: prop:equiv-assum

nodes.name: Simpler sufficient conditions for multitype assumptions
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item Assumption \ref{assum-multitype}.2 holds if $N_{y,z} = 0$ for every $y,z\in\kX$. \item The condition $\eta^2>0$ in assumption \ref{assum-multitype}.4 holds if for at least one pair $(y,z)\in\kX^2$ the mean measure $A \mapsto \E[\chi^{(y)}(A\times\{z\})]$ is non-zero and not supported on a single point. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: if for at least one pair $(y,z)\in\kX^2$ the mean measure $A \mapsto \E[\chi^{(y)}(A\times\{z\})]$ is non-zero and not supported on a single point
if for at least one pair $(y,z)\in\kX^2$ the mean measure $A \mapsto \E[\chi^{(y)}(A\times\{z\})]$ is non-zero and not supported on a single point

nodes.label: lem:simpler-assum

nodes.name: Planar map
nodes.statement: A planar map is a cellular embedding of a connected finite planar graph on the sphere, considered up to orientation-preserving homeomorphism.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps
nodes.genus: cellular embedding of a connected finite planar graph

nodes.name: Cellular embedding and faces
nodes.statement: By cellular, we mean that the image of edges do not intersect except possibly at their endpoints, and that the connected component of the complement of the union of all edges form a collection of disjoint simply connected open sets, which we call the faces of the map.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Degree of a face or vertex
nodes.statement: The degree of a face, resp. of a vertex is the number of edges incident to that face, resp. that vertex (if both ``sides'' of an edge are incident to the same face, or both ``endpoints'' are the same vertex, the edge is counted twice).
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Bipartite map
nodes.statement: A map is bipartite if all its faces have even degree.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Rooted and pointed map
nodes.statement: A rooted and pointed map $(\bm, e, v)$ is a map $m$ with a distinguished oriented edge $e$, called the root edge, and a distinguished vertex $v$.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Positive bipartite map
nodes.statement: A bipartite map is said to be positive if is oriented towards its endpoint that is closest to $v$ for the graph distance in the map.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Vertex map dagger
nodes.statement: By convention, we allow the map $\dagger$ with a single vertex, no edge, and a single face of degree $0$, and we consider it to be rooted and pointed.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Boltzmann weight w_q
nodes.statement: Given nonnegative numbers $(\bq_k)_{k\geq 1}$ that are not identically zero, define for every map $\bm$ \[ w_\bq(\bm) := \prod_{f\in F(\bm)} \bq_{\deg(f)} , \] where $F(\bm)$ is the set of faces of $\bm$, and with the convention $w_\bq(\dagger) = 1$.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Partition function Z_q
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bq = \sum_{\bm} w_\bq(\bm)$, where the sum is over all positive rooted and pointed bipartite planar maps.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Marckert–Miermont admissibility criterion
nodes.statement: Proposition 1 in \cite{marckert2007invariance}, rephrased in \cite[Section 3.2.2]{curien2019peeling} (we follow this latter reference) gives a condition for $Z_\bq < \infty$ (we say that the sequence $(\bq_k)_{k\geq 1}$ is admissible), namely that the function \[ f_\bq(x) = 1 + \sum_{k\geq 1} \bq_\bk {{2k-1}\choose k} x^k \] is such that $f_\bq(x) = x$ admits a positive solution; $Z_\bq$ is then its smallest positive solution.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps
nodes.statement_short: Z_q is finite iff f_q(x)=x has a positive solution; Z_q is then the smallest such solution.

nodes.name: Critical and generic critical weight sequence
nodes.statement: The weight sequence is critical if $f_\bq'(Z_\bq) = 1$, and generic critical if in addition $f_\bq''(Z_\bq) < \infty$.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Bouttier–Di Francesco–Guitter bijection
nodes.statement: Positive pointed and rooted bipartite maps are in bijection by the Bouttier--Di Francesco--Guitter bijection \cite{bouttier2004planar} with rooted mobiles; when the map is distributed under the Boltzmann distribution, the mobile has the distribution of a two-type (undecorated) \textsc{brw}\xspace.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps
nodes.origin_citation: Bouttier, Di Francesco & Guitter 2004; Marckert & Miermont 2007

nodes.name: Types of mobile vertices
nodes.statement: Let $\kX = \{F,V\}$. Vertices at even generations are of type $V$ while vertices at odd generations are of type $F$. Vertices of type $F$, resp. type $V$, follow a reproduction scheme\xspace $\BB_F$, resp. $\BB_V$ defined as follows.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Offspring laws mu_F and mu_V
nodes.statement: Let $\mu_F(k) = \frac{1}{1-Z_\bq^{-1}} {{2k+1} \choose {k+1}} \bq_{k+1} Z_\bq^{k}$ for every $k\geq 0$, and $\mu_V(k) = Z_\bq^{-1} (1-Z_\bq^{-1})^k$ for every $k\geq 0$; and let $N_F \sim \mu_F$, resp. $N_V \sim \mu_V$.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Reproduction scheme of type V
nodes.statement: First, let $D_V\geq 0$ be any integrable random variable, that may depend on $N_V$, and let \[ \BB_V = ( N_V \delta_{(0,F)} \ , \ 0 \ , \ D_V \ , \ (0,F)_{1\leq n \leq N_V}) . \]
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Uniform bridge b_k
nodes.statement: Conditionally on $N_F$, define $(b_k)_{0\leq k\leq 2N_F+2}$ be a uniform bridge with steps $\pm 1$ with $b_0 = b_{2N_F+2} = 0$ and $b_1 = -1$.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Downstep
nodes.statement: An index $0\leq k < 2N_F+2$ is called a downstep if $b_{k+1} = b_k-1$.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Set of downsteps
nodes.statement: Write $\DD$ for the (random) set of downsteps of $(b_k)_{0\leq k \leq 2N_F+2}$, excluding $0$.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Reproduction scheme of type F
nodes.statement: Then let $D_F\geq 0$ be an integrable random variable, that may depend on $N_F$, $\DD$ and $(b_k)_{k\in\DD}$, and define \[ \BB_F = \left( \sum_{k\in\DD} \delta_{(b_k,V)} \ , \ \max_{k\in\DD} b_k \ , \ D_F \ , \ (b_k,V)_{k\in\DD} \right) . \]
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Mobile BRW satisfies the multitype assumptions
nodes.statement: Assume that $D_V$ and $D_F$ are not both a.s. zero. Then the two-type \textsc{brw}\xspace \[ (T, \bs, (D_v)_{v\in T}, (X_v)_{v\in T}, (\Lambda_v)_{v\in T}) \] satisfies Assumptions \ref{assum-multitype}.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps
assumptions: Assume that $D_V$ and $D_F$ are not both a.s. zero.
nodes.label: prop:mobile

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (mobile) — pointer
nodes.statement: See Appendix \ref{sec:prop-mobile}.
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps
nodes.statement_short: Deferred to the appendix.

nodes.name: Distance and volume of Boltzmann planar maps
nodes.statement: Let $\bm$ be a positive pointed and rooted planar map distributed under the probability distribution $Z_\bq^{-1} w_\bq(\cdot)$ (this is the Boltzmann distribution), and let $\bd$ be the distance between its root vertex and its pointed vertex and $N_V$, resp. $N_F$ and $N_E$ its number of vertices, resp. faces or edges. Then letting $\sigma^2 = Z_\bq^2 f_\bq''(Z_q)$ and $c_V = 1$, $c_E=Z_\bq$ and $c_F = Z_\bq-1$, as $r\to\infty$, \begin{align} \P(\bd > r) &\sim 2 r^{-2} , \\ \P(\bd = r) &\sim 4 r^{-3} , \end{align} and under $\P(\, \cdot \, | \bd = r)$, resp. under $\P(\, \cdot \, | \bd>r)$, we have the convergence in distribution \[ \frac{1}{\sigma^2 r^4} \left(\frac{N_V}{c_V} , \frac{N_F}{c_F}, \frac{N_E}{c_E}\right) \ulimd r \infty (\bn, \bn, \bn) \] where recalling $\psi$ from Theorem \ref{th:main-volume-smaller} \[ \E\left[ \e^{-2\alpha^2 \bn} \right] = \frac{2\alpha}{\sigma^2} \psi\left(\sqrt{\frac{12\alpha}{\sigma^2}}\right) . \]
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps
assumptions: Let $\bm$ be a positive pointed and rooted planar map distributed under the probability distribution $Z_\bq^{-1} w_\bq(\cdot)$
nodes.statement_short: For generic critical Boltzmann maps the root-to-point distance has tail 2r^{-2}, point mass 4r^{-3}, and conditioned volumes rescaled by r^4 converge.
nodes.label: cor:maps

nodes.name: Equation (4)
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Equation (5)
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary (planar maps)
nodes.statement: This follows from the interpretation of the maximum displacement of the mobile as minus one, plus the distance between the root vertex and pointed vertex of $\bm$. To count the number of vertices one takes $D_V = 1$ and $D_F = 0$; to count the number of faces one takes $D_V = 0$ and $D_F = 1$; and recalling Euler's formula, to count the number of edges we takes $D_V = D_F = 1$ (up to an additive constant which does not contribute to the formulas of Corollary \ref{cor:maps} as $r\to\infty$).
nodes.section: 2.5 Mobiles of generic critical pointed and rooted Boltzmann planar maps
nodes.statement_short: Apply the BRW results to the BDG mobile: the max displacement is the distance minus one; choose D_V, D_F to count vertices, faces or edges.

nodes.name: Snake convergence under minimal assumptions
nodes.statement: Still, to the best of our knowledge the state of the art still falls short of our Assumptions \ref{assum}, which we conjecture are sufficient to establish the convergence towards the Brownian snake in the sense that follows.

nodes.name: Janson–Marckert convergence of discrete snakes
nodes.statement: Condition the \textsc{brw}\xspace to have progeny $n$, i.e. $n$ individuals in total across all generations. Let $f:[0,2n] \to T$ be the depth-first enumeration of the vertices of $T$, as defined in \cite[Section 1.3]{janson2005convergence}, let $V_n(t) = |f(t)|$ be the generation of $f(t)$ (its height in the tree) and $R_n(t) = X_{f(t)}$ its label (the discrete head process), defined for integer values and interpolated linearly for non-integer values. These two processes will be enough for our purposes. Then letting $v_n(t) = n^{-1/2} V_n(2nt)$ and $r_n(t) = n^{-1/4} R_n(2nt)$ for every $t\in [0,1]$, by \cite[Theorem 2 and Corollary 1]{janson2005convergence}, as well as the remark in their Section 1.4 for the normalization, we have that $((\sigma/2) v_n, (\sigma/2)^{1/2} \eta^{-1} r_n)\to (v,r)$ in distribution as $n\to\infty$ in $C([0,1])^2$, where $(v,r)$ is the head of the Brownian snake with lifetime process $v$ a normalized Brownian excursion.
nodes.statement_short: Rescaled height and label processes of a BRW conditioned on progeny n converge to the head of the Brownian snake.

nodes.name: Maximum of a BRW with given progeny
nodes.statement: As a consequence of the above convergence, we get that for every $x\in(0,\infty)$, \begin{equation} \P(M\geq x n^{1/4} \ | \ \bV = n) \ulim n \infty \P(r_*\geq (\sigma/2)^{1/2} \eta^{-1} x) . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (6)
nodes.statement: \P(M\geq x n^{1/4} \ | \ \bV = n) \ulim n \infty \P(r_*\geq (\sigma/2)^{1/2} \eta^{-1} x) .
nodes.label: eq:convergence-max-towards-snake

nodes.name: Local limit for total progeny of a critical BGW tree
nodes.statement: It is well-known that as $n\to\infty$ (using e.g. Kemperman's formula and a local limit theorem for the Lukasiewicz walk of the Bienaymé--Galton--Watson tree) \[ \P(\bV = n) \sim \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}} n^{-3/2} . \]

nodes.name: Heuristic recovery of the tail via the Brownian snake
nodes.statement: Combining it with \eqref{eq:convergence-max-towards-snake}, we get that as $r\to\infty$, \begin{align*} \P(M\geq r) &= \sum_{n\geq 1} \P(\bV = n) \P(M\geq r \ | \ \bV=n) \\ &\sim (2\pi\sigma^2)^{-1/2} \sum_{n\geq 1} n^{-3/2} \P(r_* \geq \sigma^{1/2} \eta^{-1} r n^{-1/4}) \\ &\sim (2\pi\sigma^2)^{-1/2} r^{-2} \sum_{n\geq 1} r^{-4} \left( \frac{r^4}{n} \right)^{3/2} \P\left(r_* \geq \frac{\sigma^{1/2}}{\eta \sqrt{2}} \frac{r}{n^{1/4}} \right) \\ &\sim \frac{1}{r^2 \sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}} \int_0^\infty y^{-3/2} \P\left(r_* \geq \frac{\sigma^{1/2}}{\eta\sqrt{2}} \ | \ \zeta = y \right) \d y \\ &\sim \frac{2}{\sigma r^2} \N_0\left( r_* \geq \frac{\sigma^{1/2}}{\eta\sqrt{2}} \right) , \end{align*} where $\N_0$ is the excursion measure of the Brownian snake started from $0$ (see \cite[Section III.5, Section IV.I and Section IV.6]{gall1999spatial}.) Since \[ \N_0(r_* \geq y) = \frac{3}{2y^2} \] we finally get \[ \P(M\geq r) \sim \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2 r^2} , \] recovering our Corollary \ref{cor:main-tail}.
nodes.statement_short: Summing over progeny with the snake excursion measure N_0(r_* >= y) = 3/(2y^2) recovers the 6 eta^2/(sigma^2 r^2) tail.

nodes.name: Heuristic interpretation of the volume limits
nodes.statement: Similarly, we can find that \begin{align*} \E\left[ \e^{-t\bV r^{-4}} \ | \ M\geq r \right] \ulim r \infty \N_0\left[ \e^{-t\zeta} \ | \ r_*\geq \frac{\sigma^{1/2}}{\eta\sqrt{2}} \right] . \end{align*} This gives us an interpretation of the limits in Theorem \ref{th:main-volume-smaller} and \ref{th:main-condition-vol}.

nodes.name: Proof sketch of the tail theorem
nodes.statement: The main idea is to use the Markov property of the \textsc{brw}\xspace to express our object of interest with a martingale: in our case, the function $w(r) = \frac{1}{\P(\sup_{v\in T} \Lambda_v \leq r)}-1 \approx \P(\sup_{v\in T}\Lambda_v > r)$ will be expressed as \begin{equation} w(r) \approx \E\left[ \kW^{(r)}_n w(S_n) \right] \end{equation} where $(S_n)$ is a random walk started at $r$ and $\kW^{(r)}_n$ is a weighting factor that depends on $w$ and on the trajectory of the random walk. This is established in Proposition \ref{prop:almost-martingale}, after first proving the martingale property in Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-equation} and \ref{prop:convolution-w}. Applying the optional stopping theorem at the first time that $S_n$ goes below a certain value $x$ gives us Corollary \ref{cor:Feynman-Kac}: \[ \frac{w(r)}{w(x)} \approx \E\left[ \kW^{(r)}_{\tau_x} \right] , \] from which we deduce a functional equation on the limit of the ratio $w(r)/w(x)$ as $x$ and $r$ go to infinity (Proposition \ref{prop:func-equation-phi}). Solving this equation then allows us to obtain the asymptotics of $w$.
nodes.statement_short: Feynman–Kac representation of w via an almost-martingale, optional stopping, then a functional equation for the ratio limit.

nodes.name: Equation (7)
nodes.statement: w(r) \approx \E\left[ \kW^{(r)}_n w(S_n) \right]
nodes.label: eq:summary-w

nodes.name: Distribution function h of the maximum
nodes.statement: Let $h(r) = \P(\sup_{v\in T} \Lambda_v \leq r)$.
nodes.section: 3.1 The Markov property of the Branching Random Walk

nodes.name: Function w
nodes.statement: We define $w(r) = \frac{1}{h(r)}-1$ for every $r\geq 0$.
nodes.section: 3.1 The Markov property of the Branching Random Walk

nodes.name: Convolution equation for h
nodes.statement: With the convention that $\ln 0 = -\infty$, for every $r\geq 0$ \begin{equation} h(r) = \E\left[ \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \exp\left( \int \ln h(r-x) \d \chi(x) \right) \right] . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.1 The Markov property of the Branching Random Walk
assumptions: With the convention that $\ln 0 = -\infty$, for every $r\geq 0$
nodes.statement_short: Branching (Markov) property: h(r) = E[1{Lambda<=r} exp(int ln h(r-x) dchi(x))].
nodes.label: prop:convolution-equation

nodes.name: Equation (8)
nodes.statement: h(r) = \E\left[ \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \exp\left( \int \ln h(r-x) \d \chi(x) \right) \right] .
nodes.section: 3.1 The Markov property of the Branching Random Walk

nodes.name: Remark: Laplace functional form
nodes.statement: This is the analogue of \cite[Proposition 5]{lalley2015maximal}. If $\Lambda = \sup(0, \sup\chi)$, then defining the Laplace functional $\LL_\chi(f) := \E[\exp(-\int f \d\chi)]$, then we recognize the equation $h(r) = \LL_\chi(-\ln h(r-\cdot))$.
nodes.section: 3.1 The Markov property of the Branching Random Walk

nodes.name: Proof of the convolution equation
nodes.statement: This is a simple application of the Markov property. Let $(\chi, \Lambda, (X_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)}) \sim \BB$ be independent of $(T, (X_v)_{v\in T}, (\Lambda_v)_{v\in T})$, then \begin{align*} h(r) &= \E\left[ \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \prod_{i=1}^{\chi(\R)} \P\left( \sup_{v\in T} \Lambda_v \leq r-X_i \right) \right] = \E\left[ \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \prod_{i=1}^{\chi(\R)} h(r-X_i) \right] \end{align*} from which we recognize the expression of the Proposition.
nodes.section: 3.1 The Markov property of the Branching Random Walk
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Markov property at the root and condition on the first generation.

nodes.name: Continuity of the tail w
nodes.statement: There exists a neighborhood $I$ of $0$ and two non-increasing continuous functions $F_-, F_+$ on $I$ with $F_-(0) = F_+(0) = 1$ such that for every $y\in I$, \begin{align} F_-\left( \frac{\sigma}{\eta} y \right) &\leq \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w\left( r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r)}}\right)}{w(r)} \\ &\leq \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{w\left( r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r)}}\right)}{w(r)} \leq F_+\left( \frac{\sigma}{\eta} y \right) . \end{align} We can take \begin{equation*} F_-(y) = \begin{cases} 1-y\sqrt{\frac{8}{\pi}} \geq 1-2y &\text{if } y\geq 0 \\ 1 &\text{if } y<0 \end{cases} \qquad , \qquad F_+(y) = \begin{cases} 1 &\text{if } y\geq 0 \\ f^{-1}(-y) &\text{if }y<0 \text{ large enough} \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $f: [1,3] \to [0, \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{3\sqrt{6}}] , x\mapsto \frac{1-x^{-1}}{\sqrt{x}}\sqrt{\pi/8}$.
conclusions: There exists a neighborhood $I$ of $0$ and two non-increasing continuous functions $F_-, F_+$ on $I$ with $F_-(0) = F_+(0) = 1$ such that for every $y\in I$
nodes.statement_short: w(r + y/sqrt(w(r)))/w(r) is asymptotically bounded between explicit functions F_-, F_+ of (sigma/eta) y.
nodes.label: lem:continuity-w-broad

nodes.name: Equations (9)–(10)
nodes.statement: F_-\left( \frac{\sigma}{\eta} y \right) &\leq \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w\left( r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r)}}\right)}{w(r)} \\ &\leq \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{w\left( r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r)}}\right)}{w(r)} \leq F_+\left( \frac{\sigma}{\eta} y \right) .
nodes.label: eq:continuity-ratio-right

nodes.name: Asymptotic continuity of w
nodes.statement: A useful consequence is that because $w(r)\to 0$ as $r\to\infty$ and because $w$ is decreasing, we have for every fixed $K>0$ \[ \lim_{r\to\infty} \sup_{|y| \leq K} \left| \frac{w(r+y)}{w(r)} -1\right| = 0 , \] which is the analogue of \cite[Lemma 13]{lalley2015maximal}.
nodes.statement_short: For fixed K, w(r+y)/w(r) -> 1 uniformly over |y|<=K.

nodes.name: Proof of the continuity lemma
nodes.statement: We first prove \eqref{eq:continuity-ratio-right}. The result is immediate if $y\leq 0$. Rewrite Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-equation}: for every $r,u\geq 0$, using that $\ind{\dots}\leq 1$, \[ h(r+u) \leq \E\left[ \prod_{x\in G_1} h(r+u-x) \right] . \] Apply the Markov property $n$ times: \[ h(r+u) \leq \E\left[ \prod_{x\in G_n} h(r+u-x) \right] . \] Let us assume that there exists a decreasing function $0\leq f \leq 1$ such that for every $y>0$ \begin{equation} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w\left(r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r)}}\right)}{w(r)} \geq f(y) . \end{equation} Clearly $f(y) = \ind{y\leq 0}$ works. Bound $h(x) \geq h(x) \wedge h(r)$: \[ h(r+u) \leq \E\left[ \exp\left(\ln h(r) G_n([u,\infty)) + \int_{(-\infty, u]} \ln h(r+u-x) \d G_n(x) \right) \right] . \] Write $X$ for the expression inside the exponential. Since $X<0$ we have $\e^{X} \leq 1 + X + \frac{X^2}{2}$. We then use the many-to-one formula: letting $(U_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a random walk started at $0$ with i.i.d. steps distributed under $M$ the mean measure of $\chi$, \[ \E[X] = (\ln h(r)) \P(U_n\geq u) + \E\left[\ind{U_n<u} \ln h(r+u-U_n)\right] . \] Take $u = y / \sqrt{w(r)} = y \left( \frac{1}{h(r)}-1\right)^{-1/2} \geq y (-\ln h(r))^{-1/2}$ for $y>0$ and $n = \left\lfloor \frac{s}{\eta^2 w(r)} \right\rfloor$ for some $s>0$, so that $\frac{U_n}{\sqrt{n\eta^2}} \ulim r \infty N$ in distribution where $N\sim\NN(0,1)$: \begin{align*} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{-\E[X]}{w(r)} &\geq \liminf_{r\to\infty} \left( \P(U_n\geq u) + \E\left[\ind{U_n<u} \frac{-\ln h(r+u-U_n)}{w(r)} \right] \right) \\ &\geq \P(N\geq y\sqrt{s}) + \liminf_{r\to\infty} \E\left[\ind{U_n\in(-\infty,u)} f\left(y - U_n\sqrt{w(r)}\right) \right] \\ &\geq \P(B_s\geq y) + \E\left[\ind{B_s<y} f\left(y - B_s\right) \right] . \end{align*} where $(B_v)_{v\geq 0}$ is a centered standard Brownian motion. On the other hand, \[ \E[X^2] \leq \E[G_n(\R)^2] (\ln h(r))^2 = (1+n\sigma^2) (\ln h(r))^2 \] so that \[ \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{\E[X^2]}{w(r)} \leq \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{s \sigma^2}{\eta^2 w(r)^2} (\ln h(r))^2 = \frac{s \sigma^2}{\eta^2} . \] We deduce \begin{equation*} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w(r+u)}{w(r)} = \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{1-h(r+u)}{w(r)} \geq \E\left[\ind{B_s\geq y} + \ind{B_s<y} f\left(y - B_s\right) \right] - \frac{s \sigma^2}{2\eta^2} . \end{equation*} Consider the sequence $f_s^{(m)}$ defined by $f_s^{(0)}(y) = \ind{y\leq 0}$ and \[ f_s^{(m+1)}(y) = \E\left[\ind{B_{s}\geq y} + \ind{B_{s}<y}f_s^{(m)}\left(y-B_{s}\right)\right] - \frac{s \sigma^2}{2\eta^2} . \] We just proved that for every $m$ and $s$, \[ \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w(r+u)}{w(r)} \geq f_s^{(m)}(y) . \] We can check by the Markov property that \begin{align*} f_s^{(m)}(y) &= \sum_{k=0}^{m-1} \E\left[\ind{B_0 < y, B_s<y, B_{2s}<y, \dots, B_{ks}<y} \left(\ind{B_{(k+1)s}\geq y} - \frac{s \sigma^2}{2\eta^2} \right) \right] \\ &= \P(\tau_y^{(s)} \leq ms) - \frac{\sigma^2}{2\eta^2} \E\left[ s + \tau_y^{(s)}\ind{\tau_y^{(s)} \leq ms} \right] \end{align*} where $\tau_y^{(s)} = \inf \{k\geq 0\ :\ B_{ks}\geq y \}$. Letting $\tau_y = \inf\{x\geq 0 \ : \ B_x\geq y\}$, taking the limit $s\to 0$ with $ms\to x$, we find that \[ f(y) = \P(\tau_y \leq x) - \frac{\sigma^2}{2\eta^2} \E[\tau_y \ind{\tau_y \leq x}] \] is suitable for the Lemma. Using that $\tau_y$ and $y^2 \tau_1$ have the same distribution, and that $\P(\tau_1>x) \leq 2(2\pi x)^{-1/2}$, hence by the layer-cake formula $\E[\tau_1 \ind{\tau_1\leq x}] = \int_0^x \P(\tau_1>x) \leq (2\pi)^{-1} 4\sqrt{x}$, then taking $x = y^2 \eta^2 / \sigma^2$ \begin{align*} f(y) \geq 1 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\inf_{x>0} \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} + \frac{y^2 \sigma^2 \sqrt{x}}{\eta^2} \right) = 1 - y \frac{\sigma}{\eta}\sqrt{\frac{8}{\pi}} . \end{align*} Note that using the correct asymptotic would give us $f(y)-1 \sim - y \frac{2\sigma}{\eta\sqrt{6}}$ as $y\to 0$, which is compatible with the $f$ above. Let us now deduce \eqref{eq:continuity-ratio-left}. Assume that \eqref{eq:continuity-ratio-right} holds for some constant $c$. The result is immediate if $y\leq 0$. For every $x>0$, define $r_x := \inf\{r\geq 0 : w(r) \leq x \}$; by right continuity of $h$ and thus $w$, we have $w(r_x) \leq x$. On the other hand, by the asymptotic continuity of $w$ given after Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad}, which is a consequence of only \eqref{eq:continuity-ratio-right}, we have that $\limsup_{x\to 0} x^{-1} \lim_{s\nearrow r_x} w(s) = 1$ and $\lim_{x\to 0} x^{-1} w(r_x) = 1$. Since $r_x \to \infty$ as $x\to 0$, we have by \eqref{eq:continuity-ratio-left} that for every $y>0$ \[ \liminf_{x\to 0} \frac{w\left(r_x + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r_x)}}\right)}{w(r_x)} \geq 1 - c\frac{\sigma}{\eta} y . \] Fix $A > 1$ and consider $r_{Aw(r)}$ as $r\to\infty$: for every $y < (1-A^{-1})\frac{\eta}{c\sigma}$, \begin{equation*} \liminf_{r\to \infty} \frac{w\left(r_{Aw(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r_{Aw(r)})}}\right)}{w(r)} = A \liminf_{r\to \infty} \frac{w\left(r_{Aw(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r_{Aw(r)})}}\right)}{w(r_{Aw(r)})} \geq A \left(1 - c\frac{\sigma}{\eta} y\right) > 1 , \end{equation*} so that for every $r$ large enough, $r > r_{Aw(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r_{Aw(r)})}} \geq r_{Aw(r)} + \frac{y/\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{w(r)}}$. Then \[ r_{Aw(r)} \leq r - \frac{y/\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{w(r)}} \implies \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{ w\left( r - \frac{1}{\sqrt{w(r)}} \frac{y}{\sqrt{A}} \right)}{w(r)} \leq \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{ w\left( r_{Aw(r)} \right)}{w(r)} \leq A . \] Write $f(x) = \frac{1-x^{-1}}{c\sqrt{x}}$, defined for $x>1$. This is bijective from $[1, 3]$ to $[0, \frac{2}{3c\sqrt{3}}]$, and is such that for every $A\in(1,3)$ and every $0\leq z < \frac{\eta}{\sigma} f(A)$, \[ \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{ w\left( r - \frac{z}{\sqrt{w(r)}} \right)}{w(r)} \leq A , \] or equivalently, that for every $0<z<\frac{2}{3c\sqrt{3}} \frac{\eta}{\sigma}$, \[ \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{ w\left( r - \frac{z}{\sqrt{w(r)}} \right)}{w(r)} \leq f^{-1}\left(\frac{\sigma}{\eta} z\right) . \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound h(r+u) via n generations, second-order expansion and many-to-one; iterate to a Brownian hitting-time bound. Upper bound deduced by inverting the lower bound through r_x.

nodes.name: Reduce to the lower bound for y>0.
nodes.statement: We first prove \eqref{eq:continuity-ratio-right}. The result is immediate if $y\leq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the lower bound for y>0.

nodes.name: Upper bound h(r+u) by a product over generation n.
nodes.statement: Rewrite Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-equation}: for every $r,u\geq 0$, using that $\ind{\dots}\leq 1$, \[ h(r+u) \leq \E\left[ \prod_{x\in G_1} h(r+u-x) \right] . \] Apply the Markov property $n$ times: \[ h(r+u) \leq \E\left[ \prod_{x\in G_n} h(r+u-x) \right] . \]
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound h(r+u) by a product over generation n.

nodes.name: Assume a provisional lower bound f, to be improved iterative
nodes.statement: Let us assume that there exists a decreasing function $0\leq f \leq 1$ such that for every $y>0$ \begin{equation} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w\left(r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r)}}\right)}{w(r)} \geq f(y) . \end{equation} Clearly $f(y) = \ind{y\leq 0}$ works.
nodes.statement_short: Assume a provisional lower bound f, to be improved iteratively.

nodes.name: Rewrite the bound as E[exp X].
nodes.statement: Bound $h(x) \geq h(x) \wedge h(r)$: \[ h(r+u) \leq \E\left[ \exp\left(\ln h(r) G_n([u,\infty)) + \int_{(-\infty, u]} \ln h(r+u-x) \d G_n(x) \right) \right] . \] Write $X$ for the expression inside the exponential.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the bound as E[exp X].

nodes.name: Many-to-one formula and CLT bound the first moment of X.
nodes.statement: Since $X<0$ we have $\e^{X} \leq 1 + X + \frac{X^2}{2}$. We then use the many-to-one formula: letting $(U_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a random walk started at $0$ with i.i.d. steps distributed under $M$ the mean measure of $\chi$, \[ \E[X] = (\ln h(r)) \P(U_n\geq u) + \E\left[\ind{U_n<u} \ln h(r+u-U_n)\right] . \] Take $u = y / \sqrt{w(r)} = y \left( \frac{1}{h(r)}-1\right)^{-1/2} \geq y (-\ln h(r))^{-1/2}$ for $y>0$ and $n = \left\lfloor \frac{s}{\eta^2 w(r)} \right\rfloor$ for some $s>0$, so that $\frac{U_n}{\sqrt{n\eta^2}} \ulim r \infty N$ in distribution where $N\sim\NN(0,1)$: \begin{align*} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{-\E[X]}{w(r)} &\geq \liminf_{r\to\infty} \left( \P(U_n\geq u) + \E\left[\ind{U_n<u} \frac{-\ln h(r+u-U_n)}{w(r)} \right] \right) \\ &\geq \P(N\geq y\sqrt{s}) + \liminf_{r\to\infty} \E\left[\ind{U_n\in(-\infty,u)} f\left(y - U_n\sqrt{w(r)}\right) \right] \\ &\geq \P(B_s\geq y) + \E\left[\ind{B_s<y} f\left(y - B_s\right) \right] . \end{align*} where $(B_v)_{v\geq 0}$ is a centered standard Brownian motion.
nodes.statement_short: Many-to-one formula and CLT bound the first moment of X.

nodes.name: Bound the second moment of X and deduce a new lower bound.
nodes.statement: On the other hand, \[ \E[X^2] \leq \E[G_n(\R)^2] (\ln h(r))^2 = (1+n\sigma^2) (\ln h(r))^2 \] so that \[ \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{\E[X^2]}{w(r)} \leq \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{s \sigma^2}{\eta^2 w(r)^2} (\ln h(r))^2 = \frac{s \sigma^2}{\eta^2} . \] We deduce \begin{equation*} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w(r+u)}{w(r)} = \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{1-h(r+u)}{w(r)} \geq \E\left[\ind{B_s\geq y} + \ind{B_s<y} f\left(y - B_s\right) \right] - \frac{s \sigma^2}{2\eta^2} . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the second moment of X and deduce a new lower bound.

nodes.name: Iterate the bound to obtain a sequence f_s^(m).
nodes.statement: Consider the sequence $f_s^{(m)}$ defined by $f_s^{(0)}(y) = \ind{y\leq 0}$ and \[ f_s^{(m+1)}(y) = \E\left[\ind{B_{s}\geq y} + \ind{B_{s}<y}f_s^{(m)}\left(y-B_{s}\right)\right] - \frac{s \sigma^2}{2\eta^2} . \] We just proved that for every $m$ and $s$, \[ \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w(r+u)}{w(r)} \geq f_s^{(m)}(y) . \]
nodes.statement_short: Iterate the bound to obtain a sequence f_s^(m).

nodes.name: Express f_s^(m) via a discretized hitting time and pass to t
nodes.statement: We can check by the Markov property that \begin{align*} f_s^{(m)}(y) &= \sum_{k=0}^{m-1} \E\left[\ind{B_0 < y, B_s<y, B_{2s}<y, \dots, B_{ks}<y} \left(\ind{B_{(k+1)s}\geq y} - \frac{s \sigma^2}{2\eta^2} \right) \right] \\ &= \P(\tau_y^{(s)} \leq ms) - \frac{\sigma^2}{2\eta^2} \E\left[ s + \tau_y^{(s)}\ind{\tau_y^{(s)} \leq ms} \right] \end{align*} where $\tau_y^{(s)} = \inf \{k\geq 0\ :\ B_{ks}\geq y \}$. Letting $\tau_y = \inf\{x\geq 0 \ : \ B_x\geq y\}$, taking the limit $s\to 0$ with $ms\to x$, we find that \[ f(y) = \P(\tau_y \leq x) - \frac{\sigma^2}{2\eta^2} \E[\tau_y \ind{\tau_y \leq x}] \] is suitable for the Lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Express f_s^(m) via a discretized hitting time and pass to the Brownian limit.

nodes.name: Scaling and layer-cake give the explicit linear lower bound.
nodes.statement: Using that $\tau_y$ and $y^2 \tau_1$ have the same distribution, and that $\P(\tau_1>x) \leq 2(2\pi x)^{-1/2}$, hence by the layer-cake formula $\E[\tau_1 \ind{\tau_1\leq x}] = \int_0^x \P(\tau_1>x) \leq (2\pi)^{-1} 4\sqrt{x}$, then taking $x = y^2 \eta^2 / \sigma^2$ \begin{align*} f(y) \geq 1 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\inf_{x>0} \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} + \frac{y^2 \sigma^2 \sqrt{x}}{\eta^2} \right) = 1 - y \frac{\sigma}{\eta}\sqrt{\frac{8}{\pi}} . \end{align*} Note that using the correct asymptotic would give us $f(y)-1 \sim - y \frac{2\sigma}{\eta\sqrt{6}}$ as $y\to 0$, which is compatible with the $f$ above.
nodes.statement_short: Scaling and layer-cake give the explicit linear lower bound.

nodes.name: Turn to the upper bound.
nodes.statement: Let us now deduce \eqref{eq:continuity-ratio-left}. Assume that \eqref{eq:continuity-ratio-right} holds for some constant $c$. The result is immediate if $y\leq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Turn to the upper bound.

nodes.name: Introduce the generalized inverse r_x of w.
nodes.statement: For every $x>0$, define $r_x := \inf\{r\geq 0 : w(r) \leq x \}$; by right continuity of $h$ and thus $w$, we have $w(r_x) \leq x$. On the other hand, by the asymptotic continuity of $w$ given after Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad}, which is a consequence of only \eqref{eq:continuity-ratio-right}, we have that $\limsup_{x\to 0} x^{-1} \lim_{s\nearrow r_x} w(s) = 1$ and $\lim_{x\to 0} x^{-1} w(r_x) = 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the generalized inverse r_x of w.

nodes.name: Apply the lower bound at r_{A w(r)} to get an upper bound on
nodes.statement: Since $r_x \to \infty$ as $x\to 0$, we have by \eqref{eq:continuity-ratio-left} that for every $y>0$ \[ \liminf_{x\to 0} \frac{w\left(r_x + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r_x)}}\right)}{w(r_x)} \geq 1 - c\frac{\sigma}{\eta} y . \] Fix $A > 1$ and consider $r_{Aw(r)}$ as $r\to\infty$: for every $y < (1-A^{-1})\frac{\eta}{c\sigma}$, \begin{equation*} \liminf_{r\to \infty} \frac{w\left(r_{Aw(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r_{Aw(r)})}}\right)}{w(r)} = A \liminf_{r\to \infty} \frac{w\left(r_{Aw(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r_{Aw(r)})}}\right)}{w(r_{Aw(r)})} \geq A \left(1 - c\frac{\sigma}{\eta} y\right) > 1 , \end{equation*} so that for every $r$ large enough, $r > r_{Aw(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r_{Aw(r)})}} \geq r_{Aw(r)} + \frac{y/\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{w(r)}}$. Then \[ r_{Aw(r)} \leq r - \frac{y/\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{w(r)}} \implies \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{ w\left( r - \frac{1}{\sqrt{w(r)}} \frac{y}{\sqrt{A}} \right)}{w(r)} \leq \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{ w\left( r_{Aw(r)} \right)}{w(r)} \leq A . \]
nodes.statement_short: Apply the lower bound at r_{A w(r)} to get an upper bound on the ratio.

nodes.name: Invert f to obtain F_+.
nodes.statement: Write $f(x) = \frac{1-x^{-1}}{c\sqrt{x}}$, defined for $x>1$. This is bijective from $[1, 3]$ to $[0, \frac{2}{3c\sqrt{3}}]$, and is such that for every $A\in(1,3)$ and every $0\leq z < \frac{\eta}{\sigma} f(A)$, \[ \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{ w\left( r - \frac{z}{\sqrt{w(r)}} \right)}{w(r)} \leq A , \] or equivalently, that for every $0<z<\frac{2}{3c\sqrt{3}} \frac{\eta}{\sigma}$, \[ \limsup_{r\to\infty} \frac{ w\left( r - \frac{z}{\sqrt{w(r)}} \right)}{w(r)} \leq f^{-1}\left(\frac{\sigma}{\eta} z\right) . \]
nodes.statement_short: Invert f to obtain F_+.

nodes.name: Explicit lower bound on liminf r^2 w(r)
nodes.statement: For example, we can deduce from it that $\liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2 w(r) \geq \frac{\pi \eta^2}{54 \sigma^2} \approx 0.00969 \frac{6 \eta^2}{\sigma^2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of the explicit lower bound
nodes.statement: Indeed, if this was not the case then we could take $z$ such that \eqref{eq:continuity-ratio-left} would fail at the limit $r\to\infty$ because $r-\frac{z}{\sqrt{w(r)}}$ would take negative values and the limsup would thus be unbounded.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction with the upper bound in Lemma (continuity of w).

nodes.name: Lower bound r^2 w(r)
nodes.statement: $\liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2 w(r) > 0 .$
nodes.label: lem:lower-bound-w

nodes.name: Proof of the lower bound on w
nodes.statement: We use the second moment method. By the many-to-one formula, if $(U_n)_{n\geq 0}$ is a random walk with $U_0=0$ and step distribution given by $M$, \[ \E[G_{r^2}([r, \infty))] = \P(U_{r^2} \geq r) \ulim r \infty \P( N \geq \eta^{-1} ) > 0 \] where $N\sim\NN(0,1)$. On the other hand, \[ \E[G_{r^2}(\R)^2] = 1 + r^2\sigma^2 . \] By the Paley--Zygmund inequality, \[ \P(G_{r^2}([r,\infty)) > 0) \geq \frac{\E[G_{r^2}([r, \infty))]^2}{\E[G_{r^2}(\R)^2]} \] thus giving $\liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2(1-h(r)) > 0 $.
nodes.statement_short: Second moment method with many-to-one and the Paley–Zygmund inequality at generation r^2.

nodes.name: First moment of G_{r^2}([r,inf)) via many-to-one.
nodes.statement: We use the second moment method. By the many-to-one formula, if $(U_n)_{n\geq 0}$ is a random walk with $U_0=0$ and step distribution given by $M$, \[ \E[G_{r^2}([r, \infty))] = \P(U_{r^2} \geq r) \ulim r \infty \P( N \geq \eta^{-1} ) > 0 \] where $N\sim\NN(0,1)$.
nodes.statement_short: First moment of G_{r^2}([r,inf)) via many-to-one.

nodes.name: Second moment of the generation size.
nodes.statement: On the other hand, \[ \E[G_{r^2}(\R)^2] = 1 + r^2\sigma^2 . \]
nodes.statement_short: Second moment of the generation size.

nodes.name: Paley–Zygmund gives the lower bound.
nodes.statement: By the Paley--Zygmund inequality, \[ \P(G_{r^2}([r,\infty)) > 0) \geq \frac{\E[G_{r^2}([r, \infty))]^2}{\E[G_{r^2}(\R)^2]} \] thus giving $\liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2(1-h(r)) > 0 $.
nodes.statement_short: Paley–Zygmund gives the lower bound.

nodes.name: Event E(r,R,delta)
nodes.statement: For every $0\leq R \leq r$ and every $\delta>0$, define \begin{equation} E(r,R,\delta) := \left\{\chi(\R)\leq \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)} \right\} \cap \{ \Lambda \leq R \} . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (12)
nodes.statement: E(r,R,\delta) := \left\{\chi(\R)\leq \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)} \right\} \cap \{ \Lambda \leq R \} .
nodes.label: eq:event-E-rRd

nodes.name: Size-biased pair (Z, I)
nodes.statement: Let $(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)})$ be the couple of random variables with values in $\R\times \{0,1\}$ such that for every positive and measurable $f$, \begin{equation} \E\left[ f(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}) \right] = \E\left[ \int f(x,\ind{E(r,R,\delta)}) \d\chi(x) \right] . \end{equation} This does indeed define a random variable because $\E[\chi(\R)]=1$.

nodes.name: Equation (13)
nodes.statement: \E\left[ f(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}) \right] = \E\left[ \int f(x,\ind{E(r,R,\delta)}) \d\chi(x) \right] .
nodes.label: eq:def-ZI

nodes.name: Truncated Palm kernel P^{(r,R,delta)}
nodes.statement: We also define the Markov kernel $((z,i), \Gamma) \mapsto P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,i}(\Gamma)$, where $\Gamma$ is a measurable subset of the set of point measures, $i\in\{0,1\}$ and $z\in\R$, such that for every positive and measurable $g$, if $(X_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)}$ is a measurable numbering of the atoms of $\chi$, \begin{equation} \E\left[ \sum_{i=1}^{\chi(\R)} g\left(X_i , \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}, \chi - \delta_{X_i} \right) \right] = \E\left[ \int g\left(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}, \phi \right) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}}(\phi) \right] . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (14)
nodes.statement: \E\left[ \sum_{i=1}^{\chi(\R)} g\left(X_i , \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}, \chi - \delta_{X_i} \right) \right] = \E\left[ \int g\left(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}, \phi \right) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}}(\phi) \right] .
nodes.label: eq:def-Palm

nodes.name: Mean measure function M_z
nodes.statement: This Markov kernel defines a ``mean measure function'' $M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z}$ such that for every Borel subset $A$ of $\R$, \begin{equation} M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z}(A) = \int \phi(A) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,1}(\phi) . \end{equation} Note that we only define it when $i=1$ in $P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,i}$, since the case $i=0$ will not be of interest to us.

nodes.name: Equation (15)
nodes.statement: M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z}(A) = \int \phi(A) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,1}(\phi) .
nodes.label: eq:def-Palm-mean

nodes.name: Approximate convolution equation for w
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{assum} 1. to 4., there exists $\delta^0>0$ and $r_0>0$ such that for every $\delta \in (0,\delta^0)$, $r_\bullet \geq r_0$, $r\geq 2r_\bullet$ and for every $r_\bullet \leq R \leq r-r_\bullet$, \begin{multline} w(r) = \E\Bigg[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \exp\Big( - w(r-Z) - \frac{1}{2} \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \\ + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right] \Big) \Bigg] + \mathrm{Remainder}(r,R,\delta) , \end{multline} where \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{90}|\mathrm{Remainder}(r,R,\delta)| \leq \P(\Lambda>R) + \P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}\right) + (\sigma^2 + 1) w(r-R)^2 \left( w(r-R) + \delta \right) . \end{equation*}
conclusions: there exists $\delta^0>0$ and $r_0>0$ such that for every $\delta \in (0,\delta^0)$, $r_\bullet \geq r_0$, $r\geq 2r_\bullet$ and for every $r_\bullet \leq R \leq r-r_\bullet$,
nodes.statement_short: w(r) equals an exponentially-weighted size-biased expectation of w(r-Z) up to an explicitly bounded remainder.
nodes.label: prop:convolution-w

nodes.name: Equation (16)
nodes.statement: w(r) = \E\Bigg[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \exp\Big( - w(r-Z) - \frac{1}{2} \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \\ + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right] \Big) \Bigg] + \mathrm{Remainder}(r,R,\delta) ,
nodes.label: eq:convolution-w

nodes.name: Remark on the order of the remainder
nodes.statement: Let us anticipate the final result to see what is the order of magnitude of the remainder. We will typically take $R = \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r)}}$ for some $y>0$, so that $\P(\Lambda>R) = o(w(r)^2)$ by Lemma \ref{lem:refined-Markov}. On the other hand, we will show that for this choice of $R$ then $w(r-R) \leq c w(r)$, hence $\P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}\right) = o(\delta^{-2} w(r-R))$. We may choose $\delta \to 0$ very slowly as $r\to\infty$ so that this, and the remainder as a whole, is $o(w(r)^2)$. This ensures that if we sum $\approx w(r)^{-1}$ occurences of this remainder, this error term will still be asymptotically negligible in front of the expectation, which will be of order $w(r)$.
nodes.statement_short: With R ~ y/sqrt(w(r)) and delta -> 0 slowly the remainder is o(w(r)^2).

nodes.name: Proof of the approximate convolution equation
nodes.statement: The rest of this section is devoted to the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w}. Since stating right now the conditions that $r_0$ and $\delta^0$ must satisfy would detract readability, I choose instead to state the conditions at the point where they appear naturally in the process of the proof. I will then state ``by taking $r_0$ larger if necessary we may assume that some new assertion holds'' (resp. by taking $\delta^0>0$ smaller if necessary) to mean that there exists a choice of $r_0$, resp. of $\delta^0>0$ such that the new assertion holds, in addition to all the assertions that have already been stated before. In everything that follows, we assume that $\delta \in (0,\delta^0)$, $r_\bullet \geq r_0$, $r\geq 2r_\bullet$ and that $r_\bullet \leq R \leq r-r_\bullet$. Let $Y_r = \int -\ln h(r-x)\d\chi(x)$, again using the convention $\ln 0 = -\infty$. Recall \eqref{eq:event-E-rRd} \begin{equation*} E(r,R,\delta) := \left\{\chi(\R)\leq \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)} \right\} \cap \{ \Lambda \leq R \} , \end{equation*} and write $(*) := \P\left( \chi(\R) > \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)} \right)$ and $(**) := \P(\Lambda > R)$. Since $-\ln h$ is decreasing, using that $-\ln h(x) = \ln(1+w(x)) \leq w(x)$ we have on $E(r,R,\delta)$ \[ Y_r \leq (-\ln h(r-R)) \chi(\R) \leq w(r-R) \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)} \leq \delta . \] By Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-equation} \begin{align} h(r) = \E\left[ \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \e^{-Y_r} \right] = \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \e^{-Y_r} \right] + \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)^c} \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \e^{-Y_r}\right] . \end{align} Let $\omega_\e(x) = \e^{-x} - \left(1-x+\frac{x^2}{2}\right)$. Taking $\delta^0>0$ small enough we can ensure that $|\omega_\e(x)| \leq x^3$ for every $0\leq x \leq \delta^0$. Bounding the second term of \eqref{eq:z1} by $\P(E(r,R,\delta)^c) \leq (*) + (**)$ and writing the expansion of $\e^{-Y_r}$ in the first one, we get \begin{equation*} \left| h(r) - 1 + \E[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} Y_r] - \frac{1}{2}\E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} Y_r^2 \right] \right| \leq (*) + (**) + \delta \, \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} Y_r^2 \right] . \end{equation*} \paragraph{Approximating $\E[Y_r \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}]$.} Let $\omega_\ell(x) = \ln(1+x) - x + \frac{x^2}{2}$; for every $x\geq 0$ we have $0\leq \omega_\ell(x) \leq x^3$, hence \begin{align*} \E[Y_r \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}] &= \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} - \omega_\ell(w(r-x)) \right) \d \chi(x) \right] . \end{align*} Since $w$ is decreasing, for every $x\leq R$ we have $w(r-x) \leq w(r-R)$. We deduce \begin{multline} \left| \E[Y_r \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}] - \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \right| \\ \leq w(r-R)^3 \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \chi(\R) \right] \leq w(r-R)^3 . \end{multline} Since $w(x)\to 0$ as $x\to\infty$, taking $r_0$ larger if necessary we may assume that $w(x) \leq 1$ for every $x\geq r_0$. Then $0\leq w(r-x)-\frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \leq w(r-x) $ for every $x\leq R$, hence \begin{equation} 0\leq \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \leq \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right] \leq w(r-R) . \end{equation} \paragraph{Approximating $\E[Y_r^2 \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}]$.} On the other hand, using that $0\leq \ln(1+x) \leq x$ and $|\ln(1+x)-x| \leq x^2$ for $x>0$, \begin{align*} \E[Y_r^2 \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}] =& \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int \left( w(r-x) + \ln(1+w(r-x)) - w(r-x) \right) \d \chi(x)\right)^2 \right] \\ =& \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] \\ &+ \E\Bigg[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \Bigg\{ 2\int w(r-x) (\ln(1+w(r-y))-w(r-y)) \d\chi(x)\d\chi(y) \\ &+ \int (\ln(1+w(r-x))-w(r-x)) (\ln(1+w(r-y))-w(r-y)) \d\chi(x)\d\chi(y) \Bigg\} \Bigg] \end{align*} so that \begin{multline} \left| \E[Y_r^2 \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}] - \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] \right| \\ \leq (\sigma^2 +1) (2w(r-R)^3 + w(r-R)^4) \leq 3 (\sigma^2 +1) w(r-R)^3 \end{multline} since $r-R \geq r_0$ hence $w(r-R)\leq 1$. As before, we have \begin{equation} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] \leq (\sigma^2 +1) w(r-R)^2 , \end{equation} and from \eqref{eq:approx-Yr2} and \eqref{eq:bound-Yr2} we deduce (taking $r_0$ larger if necessary) \begin{equation*} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} Y_r^2 \right] \leq 2(\sigma^2 + 1) w(r-R)^2 . \end{equation*} \paragraph{Approximating $w(r)$} Summing our estimates, letting \begin{multline} \mathrm{Rem}(r,R,\delta) = \frac{1}{1+w(r)} - 1 + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] , \end{multline} then \begin{equation} |\mathrm{Rem}(r,R,\delta)| \leq (*) + (**) + (\sigma^2 + 1) w(r-R)^2 \left( 2\delta + 4w(r-R) \right) . \end{equation} Write $\mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta)$ for the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:bound-rem}. Taking $r_0$ larger if needed and taking $\delta^0>0$ smaller if needed, we have \begin{equation} \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) \leq (*) + (**) + w(r-R)^2 . \end{equation} Since \[ w(r) = \frac{1}{\frac{1}{1+w(r)}} -1 \] we apply the fact that for every $|X|\leq \frac 12$ \[ \left|\frac{1}{1-X} - 1 - (X+X^2) \right| \leq 2 |X|^3 \] to \begin{multline*} X := \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] - \mathrm{Rem}(r,R,\delta) . \end{multline*} We first to check, using \eqref{eq:bound-Yr1}, \eqref{eq:bound-Yr2} and \eqref{eq:bound-rem-2}, that \[ |X| \leq (*) + (**) + (\sigma^2+1)^{1/3} w(r-R) \] hence that it is smaller than $1/2$ by taking $r_0$ larger if necessary. Together with the bound $(a+b+c)^3 \leq 9 (a^3 + b^3 + c^3)$ for every $a,b,c\geq 0$ and the fact that $(*)\leq 1$ and $(**)\leq 1$ we deduce \begin{align*} \left| w(r) - (X + X^2) \right| \leq 18((*)^3 + (**)^3 + (\sigma^2+1) w(r-R)^3) \leq 18 \, \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) \end{align*} since $(*)^3 + (**)^3 + (\sigma^2+1)w(r-R)^3 \leq (*) + (**) + 4(\sigma^2+1)w(r-R)^3$. On the other hand, \begin{multline*} \Bigg| -(X + X^2) + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right]^2 \Bigg| \\ \leq \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta)(1+w(r-R)+(\sigma^2+1)w(r-R)^2 + \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta)) \\ + 2 (\sigma^2+1) w(r-R)^3 + (\sigma^2+1)^2 w(r-R)^4 \leq 3 \, \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) , \end{multline*} where the last inequality holds by taking $r_0$ larger if needed, and observing that $3(\sigma^2+1)w(r-R)^3 \leq \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta)$. Finally, we bound \begin{multline*} \left| \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right]^2 - \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right]^2 \right| \\ \leq 2w(r-R)^3 + w(r-R)^4 \leq 3 w(r-R)^3 \leq \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) \end{multline*} to get \begin{multline} \Bigg| - w(r) + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right]^2 \Bigg| \\ \leq 22 \, \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) . \end{multline} \paragraph{Palm measures.} Recall \eqref{eq:def-ZI}, \eqref{eq:def-Palm} and \eqref{eq:def-Palm-mean}. We can rewrite the different terms in \eqref{eq:approx-w-without-exp-pp} as follows: \begin{align*} \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] = \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \left( w(r-Z) - \frac{w(r-Z)^2}{2} \right) \right] \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right] = \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right] . \end{align*} Let us consider the last term more carefully. Because in the definition of $P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,i}$ we work with $\chi - \delta_{X_i}$, we have \begin{align*} &\E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left\{ \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2 - \int w(r-x)^2 \d\chi(x) \right\} \right] \\ &= \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \left( \int w(r-y) \d\chi(y) - w(r-x) \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ &= \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \left( \int w(r-y) \d(\chi-\delta_x)(y) \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ &= \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \int \left(\int w(r-y) \d(\phi-\delta_x)(y) \right) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z,I^{(r,R,\delta)}} (\phi) \right] \\ &= \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \right] . \end{align*} We can finally rewrite \eqref{eq:approx-w-without-exp-pp}: \begin{multline} \Bigg| - w(r) + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \left( w(r-Z) - w(r-Z)^2 \right) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \right] + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right]^2 \Bigg| \\ = \Bigg| - w(r) + \E\Bigg[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \Big\{ 1 - w(r-Z) - \frac{1}{2} \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \\ + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right] \Big\} \Bigg] \Bigg| \leq 22 \, \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) . \end{multline} \paragraph{Introduce an exponential.} Next, write \begin{align*} \xi := - w(r-Z) - \frac{1}{2} \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right] . \end{align*} From the definition of $P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,i}$, using $g(z,i,\phi) = i \max\left( \ind{\phi(\R)> \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}-1} , \ind{\sup\phi > R} \right)$, \begin{align*} \E\left[ \int g\left(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}, \phi \right) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}}(\phi) \right] = \E\left[ \sum_{i=1}^{\chi(\R)} g\left(X_i , \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}, \chi - \delta_{X_i} \right) \right] = 0 , \end{align*} because for every $j\geq 1$ we have \[ \ind{j\leq \chi(\R)} \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \ind{(\chi-\delta_{X_j})(\R) > \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}-1} = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \ind{j\leq \chi(\R)} \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \ind{\sup(\chi - \delta_{X_j}) > R} = 0 . \] Since $g \geq 0$ it means that we can choose $P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,i}$ such that for every $z$, \[ \int g\left(z, 1, \phi \right) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,1}(\phi) = 0 = P_{z,1}^{(r,R,\delta)}\left( \left\{ \phi : \phi(\R) > \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}-1 \text{ or } \sup\phi > R \right\}\right) . \] We deduce from the definition of $M^{(r,R,\delta)}_z$ that for every $z$, \begin{equation} M^{(r,R,\delta)}_z(\R) \leq \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}-1 \quad , \quad M^{(r,R,\delta)}_z((R,\infty)) = 0 . \end{equation} This allows us to bound $\xi$: since $Z \leq R$ on $\{ I^{(r,R,\delta)} = 1\}$, \begin{align} \xi \leq w(r-R) \quad \text{and} \quad |\xi| \leq w(r-R) + \frac{1}{2} w(r-R) \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)} \leq w(r-R) + \frac{\delta}{2} . \end{align} Since $0 \leq e^x -
