(1+x) \leq x^2$ for every $x\leq 1$, \begin{multline*} \left| \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) (1 + \xi) \right] - \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \e^\xi \right] \right| \leq \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \xi^2 \right] \\ \leq \left( w(r-R) + \frac\delta 2\right) \E\Bigg[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \left\{ w(r-Z) + \frac{1}{2} \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right] \right\} \Bigg] \\ \leq \left( w(r-R) + \frac\delta 2\right) \left( \frac{\sigma^2}{2} + 2\right) w(r-R)^2 , \end{multline*} where we used that \[ \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} M^{(r,R,\delta)}_Z(\R) \right] = \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \int \phi(\R) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}}(\phi) \right] = \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int (\chi(\R)-1) \d\chi(x) \right] \leq \sigma^2 . \] Combining the estimates we have established so far gives Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w}, with the remainder bounded by \begin{multline*} |\mathrm{Remainder}(r,R,\delta)| \leq \left(w(r-R)+\frac{\delta}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\sigma^2}{2}+2\right) w(r-R)^2 \\ + 22 \left((*) + (**) + (\sigma^2 + 1) w(r-R)^2 \left( 2\delta + 4w(r-R) \right) \right) \\ \leq 22 \left((*) + (**) \right) + (\sigma^2 + 1) w(r-R)^2 \left( 45\delta + 90 w(r-R) \right) . \end{multline*} Increasing the numerical constants gives the Proposition.
nodes.statement_short: Truncate on E(r,R,delta), Taylor-expand exp and log to second order, rewrite with Palm measures, then reintroduce an exponential; all errors bounded by Bound(r,R,delta).

nodes.name: Fix conventions on r_0, delta^0 and the ranges of r, R, delt
nodes.statement: The rest of this section is devoted to the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w}. Since stating right now the conditions that $r_0$ and $\delta^0$ must satisfy would detract readability, I choose instead to state the conditions at the point where they appear naturally in the process of the proof. I will then state ``by taking $r_0$ larger if necessary we may assume that some new assertion holds'' (resp. by taking $\delta^0>0$ smaller if necessary) to mean that there exists a choice of $r_0$, resp. of $\delta^0>0$ such that the new assertion holds, in addition to all the assertions that have already been stated before. In everything that follows, we assume that $\delta \in (0,\delta^0)$, $r_\bullet \geq r_0$, $r\geq 2r_\bullet$ and that $r_\bullet \leq R \leq r-r_\bullet$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix conventions on r_0, delta^0 and the ranges of r, R, delta.

nodes.name: Introduce Y_r and bound it on E(r,R,delta).
nodes.statement: Let $Y_r = \int -\ln h(r-x)\d\chi(x)$, again using the convention $\ln 0 = -\infty$. Recall \eqref{eq:event-E-rRd} \begin{equation*} E(r,R,\delta) := \left\{\chi(\R)\leq \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)} \right\} \cap \{ \Lambda \leq R \} , \end{equation*} and write $(*) := \P\left( \chi(\R) > \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)} \right)$ and $(**) := \P(\Lambda > R)$. Since $-\ln h$ is decreasing, using that $-\ln h(x) = \ln(1+w(x)) \leq w(x)$ we have on $E(r,R,\delta)$ \[ Y_r \leq (-\ln h(r-R)) \chi(\R) \leq w(r-R) \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)} \leq \delta . \]
nodes.statement_short: Introduce Y_r and bound it on E(r,R,delta).

nodes.name: Apply the convolution equation and a second-order expansion
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-equation} \begin{align} h(r) = \E\left[ \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \e^{-Y_r} \right] = \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \e^{-Y_r} \right] + \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)^c} \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \e^{-Y_r}\right] . \end{align} Let $\omega_\e(x) = \e^{-x} - \left(1-x+\frac{x^2}{2}\right)$. Taking $\delta^0>0$ small enough we can ensure that $|\omega_\e(x)| \leq x^3$ for every $0\leq x \leq \delta^0$. Bounding the second term of \eqref{eq:z1} by $\P(E(r,R,\delta)^c) \leq (*) + (**)$ and writing the expansion of $\e^{-Y_r}$ in the first one, we get \begin{equation*} \left| h(r) - 1 + \E[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} Y_r] - \frac{1}{2}\E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} Y_r^2 \right] \right| \leq (*) + (**) + \delta \, \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} Y_r^2 \right] . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the convolution equation and a second-order expansion of exp.

nodes.name: Equation (17)
nodes.statement: h(r) = \E\left[ \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \e^{-Y_r} \right] = \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \e^{-Y_r} \right] + \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)^c} \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \e^{-Y_r}\right] .
nodes.label: eq:z1

nodes.name: Approximate the first moment of Y_r.
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Approximating $\E[Y_r \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}]$.} Let $\omega_\ell(x) = \ln(1+x) - x + \frac{x^2}{2}$; for every $x\geq 0$ we have $0\leq \omega_\ell(x) \leq x^3$, hence \begin{align*} \E[Y_r \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}] &= \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} - \omega_\ell(w(r-x)) \right) \d \chi(x) \right] . \end{align*} Since $w$ is decreasing, for every $x\leq R$ we have $w(r-x) \leq w(r-R)$. We deduce \begin{multline} \left| \E[Y_r \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}] - \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \right| \\ \leq w(r-R)^3 \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \chi(\R) \right] \leq w(r-R)^3 . \end{multline} Since $w(x)\to 0$ as $x\to\infty$, taking $r_0$ larger if necessary we may assume that $w(x) \leq 1$ for every $x\geq r_0$. Then $0\leq w(r-x)-\frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \leq w(r-x) $ for every $x\leq R$, hence \begin{equation} 0\leq \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \leq \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right] \leq w(r-R) . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Approximate the first moment of Y_r.

nodes.name: Equation (18)
nodes.statement: \left| \E[Y_r \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}] - \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \right| \\ \leq w(r-R)^3 \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \chi(\R) \right] \leq w(r-R)^3 .
nodes.label: eq:approx-Yr1

nodes.name: Equation (19)
nodes.statement: 0\leq \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \leq \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right] \leq w(r-R) .
nodes.label: eq:bound-Yr1

nodes.name: Approximate the second moment of Y_r.
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Approximating $\E[Y_r^2 \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}]$.} On the other hand, using that $0\leq \ln(1+x) \leq x$ and $|\ln(1+x)-x| \leq x^2$ for $x>0$, \begin{align*} \E[Y_r^2 \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}] =& \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int \left( w(r-x) + \ln(1+w(r-x)) - w(r-x) \right) \d \chi(x)\right)^2 \right] \\ =& \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] \\ &+ \E\Bigg[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \Bigg\{ 2\int w(r-x) (\ln(1+w(r-y))-w(r-y)) \d\chi(x)\d\chi(y) \\ &+ \int (\ln(1+w(r-x))-w(r-x)) (\ln(1+w(r-y))-w(r-y)) \d\chi(x)\d\chi(y) \Bigg\} \Bigg] \end{align*} so that \begin{multline} \left| \E[Y_r^2 \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}] - \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] \right| \\ \leq (\sigma^2 +1) (2w(r-R)^3 + w(r-R)^4) \leq 3 (\sigma^2 +1) w(r-R)^3 \end{multline} since $r-R \geq r_0$ hence $w(r-R)\leq 1$. As before, we have \begin{equation} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] \leq (\sigma^2 +1) w(r-R)^2 , \end{equation} and from \eqref{eq:approx-Yr2} and \eqref{eq:bound-Yr2} we deduce (taking $r_0$ larger if necessary) \begin{equation*} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} Y_r^2 \right] \leq 2(\sigma^2 + 1) w(r-R)^2 . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Approximate the second moment of Y_r.

nodes.name: Equation (20)
nodes.statement: \left| \E[Y_r^2 \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}] - \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] \right| \\ \leq (\sigma^2 +1) (2w(r-R)^3 + w(r-R)^4) \leq 3 (\sigma^2 +1) w(r-R)^3
nodes.label: eq:approx-Yr2

nodes.name: Equation (21)
nodes.statement: \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] \leq (\sigma^2 +1) w(r-R)^2 ,
nodes.label: eq:bound-Yr2

nodes.name: Invert 1/(1+w(r)) to second order with error 22 Bound.
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Approximating $w(r)$} Summing our estimates, letting \begin{multline} \mathrm{Rem}(r,R,\delta) = \frac{1}{1+w(r)} - 1 + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] , \end{multline} then \begin{equation} |\mathrm{Rem}(r,R,\delta)| \leq (*) + (**) + (\sigma^2 + 1) w(r-R)^2 \left( 2\delta + 4w(r-R) \right) . \end{equation} Write $\mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta)$ for the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:bound-rem}. Taking $r_0$ larger if needed and taking $\delta^0>0$ smaller if needed, we have \begin{equation} \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) \leq (*) + (**) + w(r-R)^2 . \end{equation} Since \[ w(r) = \frac{1}{\frac{1}{1+w(r)}} -1 \] we apply the fact that for every $|X|\leq \frac 12$ \[ \left|\frac{1}{1-X} - 1 - (X+X^2) \right| \leq 2 |X|^3 \] to \begin{multline*} X := \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] - \mathrm{Rem}(r,R,\delta) . \end{multline*} We first to check, using \eqref{eq:bound-Yr1}, \eqref{eq:bound-Yr2} and \eqref{eq:bound-rem-2}, that \[ |X| \leq (*) + (**) + (\sigma^2+1)^{1/3} w(r-R) \] hence that it is smaller than $1/2$ by taking $r_0$ larger if necessary. Together with the bound $(a+b+c)^3 \leq 9 (a^3 + b^3 + c^3)$ for every $a,b,c\geq 0$ and the fact that $(*)\leq 1$ and $(**)\leq 1$ we deduce \begin{align*} \left| w(r) - (X + X^2) \right| \leq 18((*)^3 + (**)^3 + (\sigma^2+1) w(r-R)^3) \leq 18 \, \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) \end{align*} since $(*)^3 + (**)^3 + (\sigma^2+1)w(r-R)^3 \leq (*) + (**) + 4(\sigma^2+1)w(r-R)^3$. On the other hand, \begin{multline*} \Bigg| -(X + X^2) + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right]^2 \Bigg| \\ \leq \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta)(1+w(r-R)+(\sigma^2+1)w(r-R)^2 + \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta)) \\ + 2 (\sigma^2+1) w(r-R)^3 + (\sigma^2+1)^2 w(r-R)^4 \leq 3 \, \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) , \end{multline*} where the last inequality holds by taking $r_0$ larger if needed, and observing that $3(\sigma^2+1)w(r-R)^3 \leq \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta)$. Finally, we bound \begin{multline*} \left| \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right]^2 - \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right]^2 \right| \\ \leq 2w(r-R)^3 + w(r-R)^4 \leq 3 w(r-R)^3 \leq \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) \end{multline*} to get \begin{multline} \Bigg| - w(r) + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right]^2 \Bigg| \\ \leq 22 \, \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) . \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Invert 1/(1+w(r)) to second order with error 22 Bound.

nodes.name: Equation (22)
nodes.statement: \mathrm{Rem}(r,R,\delta) = \frac{1}{1+w(r)} - 1 + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] ,
nodes.label: eq:expansion-1-over-1-plus-w(r)

nodes.name: Equation (23)
nodes.statement: |\mathrm{Rem}(r,R,\delta)| \leq (*) + (**) + (\sigma^2 + 1) w(r-R)^2 \left( 2\delta + 4w(r-R) \right) .
nodes.label: eq:bound-rem

nodes.name: Equation (24)
nodes.statement: \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) \leq (*) + (**) + w(r-R)^2 .
nodes.label: eq:bound-rem-2

nodes.name: Equation (25)
nodes.statement: \Bigg| - w(r) + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2\right] + \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right]^2 \Bigg| \\ \leq 22 \, \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) .
nodes.label: eq:approx-w-without-exp-pp

nodes.name: Rewrite the terms through the size-biased pair (Z,I) and Pal
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Palm measures.} Recall \eqref{eq:def-ZI}, \eqref{eq:def-Palm} and \eqref{eq:def-Palm-mean}. We can rewrite the different terms in \eqref{eq:approx-w-without-exp-pp} as follows: \begin{align*} \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left( w(r-x) - \frac{w(r-x)^2}{2} \right) \d\chi(x) \right] = \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \left( w(r-Z) - \frac{w(r-Z)^2}{2} \right) \right] \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right] = \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right] . \end{align*} Let us consider the last term more carefully. Because in the definition of $P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,i}$ we work with $\chi - \delta_{X_i}$, we have \begin{align*} &\E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \left\{ \left(\int w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right)^2 - \int w(r-x)^2 \d\chi(x) \right\} \right] \\ &= \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \left( \int w(r-y) \d\chi(y) - w(r-x) \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ &= \E\left[\ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-x) \left( \int w(r-y) \d(\chi-\delta_x)(y) \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ &= \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \int \left(\int w(r-y) \d(\phi-\delta_x)(y) \right) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z,I^{(r,R,\delta)}} (\phi) \right] \\ &= \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \right] . \end{align*} We can finally rewrite \eqref{eq:approx-w-without-exp-pp}: \begin{multline} \Bigg| - w(r) + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \left( w(r-Z) - w(r-Z)^2 \right) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \right] + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right]^2 \Bigg| \\ = \Bigg| - w(r) + \E\Bigg[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \Big\{ 1 - w(r-Z) - \frac{1}{2} \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \\ + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right] \Big\} \Bigg] \Bigg| \leq 22 \, \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) . \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the terms through the size-biased pair (Z,I) and Palm mean measures.

nodes.name: Equation (26)
nodes.statement: \Bigg| - w(r) + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \left( w(r-Z) - w(r-Z)^2 \right) \right] \\ - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \right] + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right]^2 \Bigg| \\ = \Bigg| - w(r) + \E\Bigg[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \Big\{ 1 - w(r-Z) - \frac{1}{2} \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \\ + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right] \Big\} \Bigg] \Bigg| \leq 22 \, \mathrm{Bound}(r,R,\delta) .
nodes.label: eq:approx-w-without-exp-rw

nodes.name: Replace 1+xi by exp(xi), controlling xi via the Palm mean me
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Introduce an exponential.} Next, write \begin{align*} \xi := - w(r-Z) - \frac{1}{2} \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right] . \end{align*} From the definition of $P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,i}$, using $g(z,i,\phi) = i \max\left( \ind{\phi(\R)> \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}-1} , \ind{\sup\phi > R} \right)$, \begin{align*} \E\left[ \int g\left(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}, \phi \right) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}}(\phi) \right] = \E\left[ \sum_{i=1}^{\chi(\R)} g\left(X_i , \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}, \chi - \delta_{X_i} \right) \right] = 0 , \end{align*} because for every $j\geq 1$ we have \[ \ind{j\leq \chi(\R)} \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \ind{(\chi-\delta_{X_j})(\R) > \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}-1} = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \ind{j\leq \chi(\R)} \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \ind{\sup(\chi - \delta_{X_j}) > R} = 0 . \] Since $g \geq 0$ it means that we can choose $P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,i}$ such that for every $z$, \[ \int g\left(z, 1, \phi \right) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,1}(\phi) = 0 = P_{z,1}^{(r,R,\delta)}\left( \left\{ \phi : \phi(\R) > \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}-1 \text{ or } \sup\phi > R \right\}\right) . \] We deduce from the definition of $M^{(r,R,\delta)}_z$ that for every $z$, \begin{equation} M^{(r,R,\delta)}_z(\R) \leq \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}-1 \quad , \quad M^{(r,R,\delta)}_z((R,\infty)) = 0 . \end{equation} This allows us to bound $\xi$: since $Z \leq R$ on $\{ I^{(r,R,\delta)} = 1\}$, \begin{align} \xi \leq w(r-R) \quad \text{and} \quad |\xi| \leq w(r-R) + \frac{1}{2} w(r-R) \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)} \leq w(r-R) + \frac{\delta}{2} . \end{align} Since $0 \leq e^x - (1+x) \leq x^2$ for every $x\leq 1$, \begin{multline*} \left| \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) (1 + \xi) \right] - \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \e^\xi \right] \right| \leq \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \xi^2 \right] \\ \leq \left( w(r-R) + \frac\delta 2\right) \E\Bigg[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \left\{ w(r-Z) + \frac{1}{2} \int w(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) + \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) \right] \right\} \Bigg] \\ \leq \left( w(r-R) + \frac\delta 2\right) \left( \frac{\sigma^2}{2} + 2\right) w(r-R)^2 , \end{multline*} where we used that \[ \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} M^{(r,R,\delta)}_Z(\R) \right] = \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \int \phi(\R) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}}(\phi) \right] = \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int (\chi(\R)-1) \d\chi(x) \right] \leq \sigma^2 . \]
nodes.statement_short: Replace 1+xi by exp(xi), controlling xi via the Palm mean measure bounds.

nodes.name: Equation (27)
nodes.statement: M^{(r,R,\delta)}_z(\R) \leq \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}-1 \quad , \quad M^{(r,R,\delta)}_z((R,\infty)) = 0 .
nodes.label: eq:Palm-controle-M

nodes.name: Equation (28)
nodes.statement: \xi \leq w(r-R) \quad \text{and} \quad |\xi| \leq w(r-R) + \frac{1}{2} w(r-R) \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)} \leq w(r-R) + \frac{\delta}{2} .
nodes.label: eq:bound-xi

nodes.name: Collect the error terms into the stated remainder bound.
nodes.statement: Combining the estimates we have established so far gives Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w}, with the remainder bounded by \begin{multline*} |\mathrm{Remainder}(r,R,\delta)| \leq \left(w(r-R)+\frac{\delta}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\sigma^2}{2}+2\right) w(r-R)^2 \\ + 22 \left((*) + (**) + (\sigma^2 + 1) w(r-R)^2 \left( 2\delta + 4w(r-R) \right) \right) \\ \leq 22 \left((*) + (**) \right) + (\sigma^2 + 1) w(r-R)^2 \left( 45\delta + 90 w(r-R) \right) . \end{multline*} Increasing the numerical constants gives the Proposition.
nodes.statement_short: Collect the error terms into the stated remainder bound.

nodes.name: Random walk S_n with truncation indicators
nodes.statement: Fix $r_\bullet \geq r_0$ and $r \geq 2 r_\bullet$, and let $(S_n)_{n\geq 0}$, $(R_n)_{n\geq 0}$, $(\delta_n)_{n\geq 0}$ and $(I_n)_{n\geq 1}$ such that $S_0 = r$ and for every $n\geq 0$, writing $\FF_n = \sigma\left( S_k, R_k, \delta_k, I_k : k\leq n\right)$, then conditionally on $\FF_n$ \begin{equation} (S_{n+1} - S_n , I_{n+1}) \eqdistr (- Z, I^{(S_n,R_n, \delta_n)}) . \end{equation} In particular, $(S_n)_{n\geq 0}$ is a random walk started at $S_0 = r$ with i.i.d. steps, such that $S_n-S_{n+1}$ has distribution $M$ for every $n$.

nodes.name: Equation (29)
nodes.statement: (S_{n+1} - S_n , I_{n+1}) \eqdistr (- Z, I^{(S_n,R_n, \delta_n)}) .

nodes.name: Almost-martingale (discount process)
nodes.statement: For every $n\geq 0$, define the ``discount process'' \begin{multline} \kW^{(r)}_n := \left(\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} I_{k+1}\right) \exp\Bigg(- \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \left( w(S_{k+1}) - \E\left[ I_{k+1} w(S_{k+1}) \, | \, \FF_k \right] \right) \\ - \frac 12 \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \int w(S_k-y) \d M^{(S_k,R_k,\delta_k)}_{S_k-S_{k+1}}(y) \Bigg) . \end{multline} Define the stopping time \[ T = \inf\{n\geq 0 : S_n < 2r_\bullet \text{ or } R_n \notin [r_\bullet, S_n - r_\bullet] \text{ or } \delta_n \notin (0,\delta^0) \} . \] Define the processes \begin{equation} W^{(r)}_n = \kW^{(r)}_n w(S_n) \quad , \quad Y_n := W^{(r)}_n - \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \kW^{(r)}_k \mathrm{Remainder}(S_k, R_k, \delta_k) . \end{equation} Then $(Y_{n\wedge T})_{n\geq 0}$ is a martingale, i.e. on the event $\{T > n\}$, \begin{equation} \E\left[ W^{(r)}_{n+1} | \FF_n\right] - W^{(r)}_n = \kW^{(r)}_n \mathrm{Remainder}(S_n, R_n, \delta_n) , \end{equation} where the remainder is given by Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w}.
nodes.statement_short: The discounted process W_n = calW_n w(S_n) is a martingale up to accumulated remainders, until the stopping time T.
nodes.label: prop:almost-martingale

nodes.name: Equation (30)
nodes.statement: \kW^{(r)}_n := \left(\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} I_{k+1}\right) \exp\Bigg(- \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \left( w(S_{k+1}) - \E\left[ I_{k+1} w(S_{k+1}) \, | \, \FF_k \right] \right) \\ - \frac 12 \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \int w(S_k-y) \d M^{(S_k,R_k,\delta_k)}_{S_k-S_{k+1}}(y) \Bigg) .
nodes.label: eq:def-Z

nodes.name: Equation (31)
nodes.statement: W^{(r)}_n = \kW^{(r)}_n w(S_n) \quad , \quad Y_n := W^{(r)}_n - \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \kW^{(r)}_k \mathrm{Remainder}(S_k, R_k, \delta_k) .

nodes.name: Equation (32)
nodes.statement: \E\left[ W^{(r)}_{n+1} | \FF_n\right] - W^{(r)}_n = \kW^{(r)}_n \mathrm{Remainder}(S_n, R_n, \delta_n) ,
nodes.label: eq:almost-mg-ppty

nodes.name: Proof of the almost-martingale property
nodes.statement: It is a straightforward consequence of the Markov property with Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w}.
nodes.statement_short: Markov property combined with the approximate convolution equation.

nodes.name: Equivalent form of the discount process
nodes.statement: Equivalently, we can add some $I_{k+1}$ in the expression: \begin{multline*} \kW^{(r)}_n = \left(\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} I_{k+1}\right) \exp\Bigg(- \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \left( I_{k+1} w(S_{k+1}) - \E\left[ I_{k+1} w(S_{k+1}) \, | \, \FF_k \right] \right) \\ - \frac 12 \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} I_{k+1} \int w(S_k-y) \d M^{(S_k,R_k,\delta_k)}_{S_k-S_{k+1}}(y) \Bigg) . \end{multline*}

nodes.name: Uniform integrability of the discount process
nodes.statement: Up to taking $r_0$ larger, there exists $a_0>0$ such that for every $a \in (0,a_0)$, for every $r_\bullet \geq r_0$ and for every $r\geq 2r_\bullet$, writing $T_a = T \wedge \inf \{ n\geq 0 : R_n > a/\sqrt{w(S_n)} \}$, the stopped process $(\kW^{(r)}_{n\wedge T_a})_{n\geq 0}$ is a uniformly integrable supermartingale.
nodes.statement_short: Stopped at T_a, the discount process is a uniformly integrable supermartingale.
nodes.label: lem:discount-UI

nodes.name: Proof of uniform integrability
nodes.statement: Recall Lemma \ref{lem:lower-bound-w}: writing $C = \liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2 w(r)$ and taking $r_0$ larger if needed we have $r^2 w(r) \geq C/2$ for every $r\geq r_0$. Set $a_0 = \sqrt{C/8}$, then for every $a\in(0,a_0)$ and every $r\geq r_0$ we have $a/\sqrt{w(r)} \leq r/2$, hence for every $r_\bullet \geq r_0$, every $r\geq 2r_\bullet$ and every $R \leq a/\sqrt{w(r)}$ we have $r-R \geq r_\bullet \geq r_0$. In particular, $T_a$ is the same as $T$ with the condition on $R_n$ replaced by $R_n \notin [r_\bullet, a/\sqrt{w(S_n)}]$. Just as in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w}, write \[ \xi := -w(r-Z) + \E\left[I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z)\right] - \frac{1}{2} \int w(r-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y). \] We first prove that for every $\delta \in (0,\delta^0)$, every $r\geq r_\bullet$ and every $r_\bullet \leq R \leq a/\sqrt{w(r)}$ we have $\E[I^{(r,R,\delta)} \e^{2\xi}] \leq 1$. Let us show how the lemma follows. Let $\xi_n$ be obtained from $\xi$ by replacing $r$ by $S_n$, $R$ by $R_n$ and $\delta$ by $\delta_n$: on $\{T_a>n\}$ it satisfies $\delta_n \in (0,\delta^0)$, $S_n\geq 2r_\bullet$ and $r_\bullet \leq R_n \leq a/\sqrt{w(r)}$, hence on $\{ T_a > n \}$, \begin{equation*} \E\left[ \left(\kW^{(r)}_{n+1}\right)^2 \, | \, \FF_n\right] = \left(\kW^{(r)}_n\right)^2 \E\left[I^{(S_n, R_n, \delta_n)} \e^{2\xi_n} \ | \ \FF_n\right] \leq \left(\kW^{(r)}_n\right)^2 . \end{equation*} Together with $\kW^{(r)}_0=1$ we conclude that $\E[ (\kW^{(r)}_{n \wedge T_a})^2 ] \leq 1$ for every $n$, which by De La Vallée Poussin's theorem implies that $(\kW^{(r)}_{n \wedge T_a})_{n\geq 0}$ is uniformly integrable. On the other hand, on $\{T_a>n\}$ \[ \E\left[\kW^{(r)}_{n+1} \, | \, \FF_n \right] = \kW^{(r)}_{n} \E\left[I^{(S_n, R_n, \delta_n)} \e^{\xi_n} \, | \, \FF_n \right] . \] Since $\E[I^{(S_n,R_n,\delta_n)} \e^{\xi_n} \, | \, \FF_n ] \leq (\E[I^{(S_n,R_n,\delta_n)}\e^{2\xi_n} \, | \, \FF_n ])^{1/2}\leq 1$ on $\{T_a>n\}$, the second half of the Lemma follows by induction. Let us now check that $\E[I^{(r,R,\delta)} \e^{2\xi}] \leq 1$. Write $I^{(r,R,\delta)}\xi = A + B$, with $A = -I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) + \E\left[I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z)\right] $ and $B = - \frac{1}{2} I^{(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y)$. Almost surely $|A| \leq w(r-R)$, and $\E[A]=0$. On the other hand, by \eqref{eq:Palm-controle-M} we have $M_z^{(r,R,\delta)}(\R) \leq \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}-1$ for every $z, r, R, \delta$, hence $-\frac\delta 2 \leq B\leq 0$. In addition, \begin{align*} \E[B] &= -\frac{1}{2}\E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y) \right] \\ &= - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left(\int w(r-y) \d(\chi-\delta_x)(y)\right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ &= - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int (\chi(\R)-1) w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ &\geq -\frac{\sigma^2}{2}w(r-R) . \end{align*} Because for every $K\in\R$ \[ \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} (\chi(\R)-1) \chi([K, \infty)) \right] \to \E\left[ (\chi(\R)-1) \chi([K,\infty)) \right] \] as $r_0\to\infty$ uniformly on every $\delta \in (0,\delta^0)$, $r\geq 2r_0$ and $r_0 \leq R \leq r-r_0$, and because this limit converges to $\sigma^2>0$ as $K\to-\infty$, we can find $c>0$ and $K\in\R$ such that, taking $r_0$ larger if necessary, for every $r_\bullet \geq r_0$, $r\geq 2r_\bullet$ and $r_\bullet \leq R \leq a/\sqrt{w(r)}$, \[ \E[B] \leq - c w(r-K) . \] We then use that $\e^{x} \leq 1 + x + x^2$ for every $|x|\leq 1$ and taking $r_0$ larger if necessary so that $2w(r-R) \leq 1$, to get \begin{align*} \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \e^{2(A+B)} \right] \leq \E\left[\e^{2B}\right] + \E\left[2A \e^{2B}\right] + \E\left[4A^2 \e^{2B} \right] . \end{align*} Since $B\leq 0$ a.s. the last term is bounded by $4\E[A^2] \leq 4 w(r-R)^2$. Taking $\delta^0$ smaller if necessary so that $\frac{1-e^{-\delta}}{\delta} \geq \frac 12$, we use that $\e^{x} \leq 1 + \frac{1-e^{-\delta}}{\delta} x \leq 1 + \frac{x}{2}$ for every $-\delta \leq x \leq 0$ to bound the first term by \[ \E[\e^{2B}] \leq 1 + \frac{1}{2} \E[2B] \leq 1 - c w(r-K) . \] For the middle term, write \[ \E[A\e^{2B}] = \E[A] + \E[A(\e^{2B}-1)] \leq w(r-R) \E[1-\e^{2B}] \leq 2w(r-R) \E[|B|] \leq \sigma^2 w(r-R)^2 \] since $\E[|B|] = \E[-B] \leq \frac{\sigma^2}{2}w(r-R)$. We deduce that \begin{equation} \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \e^{2(A+B)} \right] \leq 1 - c w(r-K) + (2\sigma^2 + 4) w(r-R)^2 . \end{equation} By Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad} and up to taking $a_0$ smaller, for every $a \in (0,a_0)$ we have $\sup_{r\geq 2r_0} \sup_{r_0\leq R \leq \frac{a}{\sqrt{w(r)}}} \frac{w(r-R)^2}{w(r-K)} \to 0$ as $r_0\to\infty$, hence up to taking $r_0$ larger if necessary the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:smaller-one} is smaller than $1$. This finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Show E[I e^{2 xi}] <= 1 so the stopped discount process is bounded in L^2 (de la Vallée Poussin) and a supermartingale. Key step: E[B] <= -c w(r-K) dominates the w(r-R)^2 errors.

nodes.name: Choose a_0 from the lower bound on w so that r - R >= r_bull
nodes.statement: Recall Lemma \ref{lem:lower-bound-w}: writing $C = \liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2 w(r)$ and taking $r_0$ larger if needed we have $r^2 w(r) \geq C/2$ for every $r\geq r_0$. Set $a_0 = \sqrt{C/8}$, then for every $a\in(0,a_0)$ and every $r\geq r_0$ we have $a/\sqrt{w(r)} \leq r/2$, hence for every $r_\bullet \geq r_0$, every $r\geq 2r_\bullet$ and every $R \leq a/\sqrt{w(r)}$ we have $r-R \geq r_\bullet \geq r_0$. In particular, $T_a$ is the same as $T$ with the condition on $R_n$ replaced by $R_n \notin [r_\bullet, a/\sqrt{w(S_n)}]$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a_0 from the lower bound on w so that r - R >= r_bullet.

nodes.name: Reduce the lemma to E[I e^{2 xi}] <= 1.
nodes.statement: Just as in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w}, write \[ \xi := -w(r-Z) + \E\left[I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z)\right] - \frac{1}{2} \int w(r-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y). \] We first prove that for every $\delta \in (0,\delta^0)$, every $r\geq r_\bullet$ and every $r_\bullet \leq R \leq a/\sqrt{w(r)}$ we have $\E[I^{(r,R,\delta)} \e^{2\xi}] \leq 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the lemma to E[I e^{2 xi}] <= 1.

nodes.name: Show how the key bound implies the lemma.
nodes.statement: Let us show how the lemma follows. Let $\xi_n$ be obtained from $\xi$ by replacing $r$ by $S_n$, $R$ by $R_n$ and $\delta$ by $\delta_n$: on $\{T_a>n\}$ it satisfies $\delta_n \in (0,\delta^0)$, $S_n\geq 2r_\bullet$ and $r_\bullet \leq R_n \leq a/\sqrt{w(r)}$, hence on $\{ T_a > n \}$, \begin{equation*} \E\left[ \left(\kW^{(r)}_{n+1}\right)^2 \, | \, \FF_n\right] = \left(\kW^{(r)}_n\right)^2 \E\left[I^{(S_n, R_n, \delta_n)} \e^{2\xi_n} \ | \ \FF_n\right] \leq \left(\kW^{(r)}_n\right)^2 . \end{equation*} Together with $\kW^{(r)}_0=1$ we conclude that $\E[ (\kW^{(r)}_{n \wedge T_a})^2 ] \leq 1$ for every $n$, which by De La Vallée Poussin's theorem implies that $(\kW^{(r)}_{n \wedge T_a})_{n\geq 0}$ is uniformly integrable. On the other hand, on $\{T_a>n\}$ \[ \E\left[\kW^{(r)}_{n+1} \, | \, \FF_n \right] = \kW^{(r)}_{n} \E\left[I^{(S_n, R_n, \delta_n)} \e^{\xi_n} \, | \, \FF_n \right] . \] Since $\E[I^{(S_n,R_n,\delta_n)} \e^{\xi_n} \, | \, \FF_n ] \leq (\E[I^{(S_n,R_n,\delta_n)}\e^{2\xi_n} \, | \, \FF_n ])^{1/2}\leq 1$ on $\{T_a>n\}$, the second half of the Lemma follows by induction.
nodes.statement_short: Show how the key bound implies the lemma.

nodes.name: Second moment step
nodes.statement: Let $\xi_n$ be obtained from $\xi$ by replacing $r$ by $S_n$, $R$ by $R_n$ and $\delta$ by $\delta_n$: on $\{T_a>n\}$ it satisfies $\delta_n \in (0,\delta^0)$, $S_n\geq 2r_\bullet$ and $r_\bullet \leq R_n \leq a/\sqrt{w(r)}$, hence on $\{ T_a > n \}$, \begin{equation*} \E\left[ \left(\kW^{(r)}_{n+1}\right)^2 \, | \, \FF_n\right] = \left(\kW^{(r)}_n\right)^2 \E\left[I^{(S_n, R_n, \delta_n)} \e^{2\xi_n} \ | \ \FF_n\right] \leq \left(\kW^{(r)}_n\right)^2 .
nodes.statement_short: Conditional second moment of the discount process does not increase.

nodes.name: L^2 bound gives uniform integrability; Cauchy–Schwarz gives
nodes.statement: Together with $\kW^{(r)}_0=1$ we conclude that $\E[ (\kW^{(r)}_{n \wedge T_a})^2 ] \leq 1$ for every $n$, which by De La Vallée Poussin's theorem implies that $(\kW^{(r)}_{n \wedge T_a})_{n\geq 0}$ is uniformly integrable. On the other hand, on $\{T_a>n\}$ \[ \E\left[\kW^{(r)}_{n+1} \, | \, \FF_n \right] = \kW^{(r)}_{n} \E\left[I^{(S_n, R_n, \delta_n)} \e^{\xi_n} \, | \, \FF_n \right] . \] Since $\E[I^{(S_n,R_n,\delta_n)} \e^{\xi_n} \, | \, \FF_n ] \leq (\E[I^{(S_n,R_n,\delta_n)}\e^{2\xi_n} \, | \, \FF_n ])^{1/2}\leq 1$ on $\{T_a>n\}$, the second half of the Lemma follows by induction.
nodes.statement_short: L^2 bound gives uniform integrability; Cauchy–Schwarz gives the supermartingale property.

nodes.name: Split I xi = A + B and bound A and B.
nodes.statement: Let us now check that $\E[I^{(r,R,\delta)} \e^{2\xi}] \leq 1$. Write $I^{(r,R,\delta)}\xi = A + B$, with $A = -I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z) + \E\left[I^{(r,R,\delta)} w(r-Z)\right] $ and $B = - \frac{1}{2} I^{(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y)$. Almost surely $|A| \leq w(r-R)$, and $\E[A]=0$. On the other hand, by \eqref{eq:Palm-controle-M} we have $M_z^{(r,R,\delta)}(\R) \leq \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}-1$ for every $z, r, R, \delta$, hence $-\frac\delta 2 \leq B\leq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Split I xi = A + B and bound A and B.

nodes.name: Two-sided bounds on E[B].
nodes.statement: In addition, \begin{align*} \E[B] &= -\frac{1}{2}\E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \int w(r-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y) \right] \\ &= - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int \left(\int w(r-y) \d(\chi-\delta_x)(y)\right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ &= - \frac{1}{2} \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int (\chi(\R)-1) w(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ &\geq -\frac{\sigma^2}{2}w(r-R) . \end{align*} Because for every $K\in\R$ \[ \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} (\chi(\R)-1) \chi([K, \infty)) \right] \to \E\left[ (\chi(\R)-1) \chi([K,\infty)) \right] \] as $r_0\to\infty$ uniformly on every $\delta \in (0,\delta^0)$, $r\geq 2r_0$ and $r_0 \leq R \leq r-r_0$, and because this limit converges to $\sigma^2>0$ as $K\to-\infty$, we can find $c>0$ and $K\in\R$ such that, taking $r_0$ larger if necessary, for every $r_\bullet \geq r_0$, $r\geq 2r_\bullet$ and $r_\bullet \leq R \leq a/\sqrt{w(r)}$, \[ \E[B] \leq - c w(r-K) . \]
nodes.statement_short: Two-sided bounds on E[B].

nodes.name: Expand e^{2(A+B)} to second order.
nodes.statement: We then use that $\e^{x} \leq 1 + x + x^2$ for every $|x|\leq 1$ and taking $r_0$ larger if necessary so that $2w(r-R) \leq 1$, to get \begin{align*} \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \e^{2(A+B)} \right] \leq \E\left[\e^{2B}\right] + \E\left[2A \e^{2B}\right] + \E\left[4A^2 \e^{2B} \right] . \end{align*} Since $B\leq 0$ a.s. the last term is bounded by $4\E[A^2] \leq 4 w(r-R)^2$. Taking $\delta^0$ smaller if necessary so that $\frac{1-e^{-\delta}}{\delta} \geq \frac 12$, we use that $\e^{x} \leq 1 + \frac{1-e^{-\delta}}{\delta} x \leq 1 + \frac{x}{2}$ for every $-\delta \leq x \leq 0$ to bound the first term by \[ \E[\e^{2B}] \leq 1 + \frac{1}{2} \E[2B] \leq 1 - c w(r-K) . \] For the middle term, write \[ \E[A\e^{2B}] = \E[A] + \E[A(\e^{2B}-1)] \leq w(r-R) \E[1-\e^{2B}] \leq 2w(r-R) \E[|B|] \leq \sigma^2 w(r-R)^2 \] since $\E[|B|] = \E[-B] \leq \frac{\sigma^2}{2}w(r-R)$. We deduce that \begin{equation} \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \e^{2(A+B)} \right] \leq 1 - c w(r-K) + (2\sigma^2 + 4) w(r-R)^2 . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Expand e^{2(A+B)} to second order.

nodes.name: Equation (33)
nodes.statement: \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} \e^{2(A+B)} \right] \leq 1 - c w(r-K) + (2\sigma^2 + 4) w(r-R)^2 .
nodes.label: eq:smaller-one

nodes.name: Continuity of w makes the right-hand side smaller than 1.
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad} and up to taking $a_0$ smaller, for every $a \in (0,a_0)$ we have $\sup_{r\geq 2r_0} \sup_{r_0\leq R \leq \frac{a}{\sqrt{w(r)}}} \frac{w(r-R)^2}{w(r-K)} \to 0$ as $r_0\to\infty$, hence up to taking $r_0$ larger if necessary the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:smaller-one} is smaller than $1$. This finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Continuity of w makes the right-hand side smaller than 1.

nodes.name: Feynman–Kac representation of w
nodes.statement: There exists a function $\underline{\delta} : [0,\infty) \to (0,\delta^0)$ decreasing with $\underline{\delta}(y) \to 0$ as $y\to\infty$ and a function $g:(0,1] \to [0,\infty)$ increasing with $g(x)\to 0$ as $x\to 0$ such that the following holds. For every $a\in (0,a_0)$, $A>0$, $y>0$, $\RR>0$, and $r \geq x \geq r_0$ where $a_0, r_0$ is given by Lemma \ref{lem:discount-UI}, setting $\delta_n = \underline{\delta}(y)$ for every $n$ and writing \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} \tau_x = \inf\{ n\geq 0 : S_n \leq x \} \\ \rho = \inf\{n\geq 0 : S_n-R_n < y \text{ or } R_n < \RR\} \\ T' = \inf(\tau_x, T_a, \rho, A/w(x) \} \end{cases} \end{equation*} then \begin{equation} \left| w(r) - \E\left[ W^{(r)}_{T'}\right] \right| \leq \frac{100 A}{w(x)} \left( \P(\Lambda > \RR) + w(y)^2 g(w(y))\right) . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: w(r) equals E[W_{T'}] at a suitable bounded stopping time up to an error 100A/w(x) (P(Lambda>R) + w(y)^2 g(w(y))).
nodes.label: cor:Feynman-Kac

nodes.name: Equation (34)
nodes.statement: \left| w(r) - \E\left[ W^{(r)}_{T'}\right] \right| \leq \frac{100 A}{w(x)} \left( \P(\Lambda > \RR) + w(y)^2 g(w(y))\right) .
nodes.label: eq:FK

nodes.name: Proof of the Feynman–Kac representation
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:almost-martingale} the process \[ Y_n := W_n^{(r)} - \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \kW^{(r)}_k \mathrm{Remainder}(S_k, R_k, \delta_k) , \] is such that $(Y_{n\wedge T})_{n\geq 0}$ is a $(\FF_n)_{n\geq 0}$-martingale. Apply the stopping theorem with the bounded stopping time $T'$: \begin{align} w(r) = \E\left[ W^{(r)}_0 \right] = \E\left[ W_{T'}^{(r)} \right] - \E\left[ \sum_{k=0}^{T'-1} \kW^{(r)}_k \mathrm{Remainder}(S_k, R_k, \delta_k) \right] . \end{align} By Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w} \[ \frac{1}{90} |\mathrm{Remainder}(r, R, \delta)| \leq \P(\Lambda>R) + \P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}\right) + (\sigma^2+1) w(r-R)^2(w(r-R)+\delta) , \] thus on $\{ k < T'\}$ we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{90} |\mathrm{Remainder}(S_k, R_k, \delta_k)| \leq \P(\Lambda>\RR) + \P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\underline{\delta}(y)}{w(y)}\right) + (\sigma^2+1) w(y)^2(w(y)+\underline{\delta}(y)) . \end{align*} We can then find a function $\underline{\delta}(y)\to 0$ as $y\to\infty$ decreasing and positive, together with a function $g(x) \to 0$ as $x\to 0$ increasing and positive, such that \begin{align*} \P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\underline{\delta}(y)}{w(y)}\right) + (\sigma^2+1) w(y)^2(w(y)+ \underline{\delta}(y)) \leq \frac{1}{100} w(y)^2 g(w(y)) . \end{align*} Since by Lemma \ref{lem:discount-UI} the process $(\kW^{(r)}_{n\wedge T_a})_{n\geq 0}$ is a supermartingale we have \[ \E\left[ \kW^{(r)}_{n\wedge T'} \right] \leq 1 , \] and given that $T'\leq A/w(x)$ we bound the sum in the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:sum-for-FK} by $A/w(x)$ times the upper bound for the remainder. This finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Optional stopping for the almost-martingale at the bounded time T', with remainders summed over at most A/w(x) steps.

nodes.name: The compensated process is a martingale.
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:almost-martingale} the process \[ Y_n := W_n^{(r)} - \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \kW^{(r)}_k \mathrm{Remainder}(S_k, R_k, \delta_k) , \] is such that $(Y_{n\wedge T})_{n\geq 0}$ is a $(\FF_n)_{n\geq 0}$-martingale.
nodes.statement_short: The compensated process is a martingale.

nodes.name: Optional stopping at T'.
nodes.statement: Apply the stopping theorem with the bounded stopping time $T'$: \begin{align} w(r) = \E\left[ W^{(r)}_0 \right] = \E\left[ W_{T'}^{(r)} \right] - \E\left[ \sum_{k=0}^{T'-1} \kW^{(r)}_k \mathrm{Remainder}(S_k, R_k, \delta_k) \right] . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Optional stopping at T'.

nodes.name: Equation (35)
nodes.statement: w(r) = \E\left[ W^{(r)}_0 \right] = \E\left[ W_{T'}^{(r)} \right] - \E\left[ \sum_{k=0}^{T'-1} \kW^{(r)}_k \mathrm{Remainder}(S_k, R_k, \delta_k) \right] .
nodes.label: eq:sum-for-FK

nodes.name: Bound each remainder before T'.
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w} \[ \frac{1}{90} |\mathrm{Remainder}(r, R, \delta)| \leq \P(\Lambda>R) + \P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}\right) + (\sigma^2+1) w(r-R)^2(w(r-R)+\delta) , \] thus on $\{ k < T'\}$ we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{90} |\mathrm{Remainder}(S_k, R_k, \delta_k)| \leq \P(\Lambda>\RR) + \P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\underline{\delta}(y)}{w(y)}\right) + (\sigma^2+1) w(y)^2(w(y)+\underline{\delta}(y)) . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound each remainder before T'.

nodes.name: Choose delta(y) and g so the remainder is o(w(y)^2).
nodes.statement: We can then find a function $\underline{\delta}(y)\to 0$ as $y\to\infty$ decreasing and positive, together with a function $g(x) \to 0$ as $x\to 0$ increasing and positive, such that \begin{align*} \P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\underline{\delta}(y)}{w(y)}\right) + (\sigma^2+1) w(y)^2(w(y)+ \underline{\delta}(y)) \leq \frac{1}{100} w(y)^2 g(w(y)) . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Choose delta(y) and g so the remainder is o(w(y)^2).

nodes.statement: Since by Lemma \ref{lem:discount-UI} the process $(\kW^{(r)}_{n\wedge T_a})_{n\geq 0}$ is a supermartingale we have \[ \E\left[ \kW^{(r)}_{n\wedge T'} \right] \leq 1 , \] and given that $T'\leq A/w(x)$ we bound the sum in the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:sum-for-FK} by $A/w(x)$ times the upper bound for the remainder. This finishes the proof.

nodes.name: Ratio limit phi
nodes.statement: Given a sequence $r_k \to \infty$ as $k\to\infty$, up to extracting a subsequence we can make sense of the limit \begin{equation} \phi(y) = \lim_{k\to\infty} \frac{w\left( r_k + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r_k)}}\right)}{w(r_k)} \end{equation} for every fixed $y\geq 0$, and thus by a diagonal argument, jointly for every rational $y\geq 0$.

nodes.name: Equation (36)
nodes.statement: \phi(y) = \lim_{k\to\infty} \frac{w\left( r_k + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w(r_k)}}\right)}{w(r_k)}
nodes.label: eq:phi

nodes.name: Continuity of the ratio limit phi
nodes.statement: Any limit $\phi$ in \eqref{eq:phi} extends to a continuous, non-increasing, positive function of $[0,\infty)$. Hence, the convergence \eqref{eq:phi} holds uniformly over every compact of $[0,\infty)$.
conclusions: Any limit $\phi$ in \eqref{eq:phi} extends to a continuous, non-increasing, positive function of $[0,\infty)$.
the convergence \eqref{eq:phi} holds uniformly over every compact of $[0,\infty)$.
nodes.label: prop:continuity-phi

nodes.name: Proof of continuity of phi
nodes.statement: The fact that $\phi$ is decreasing and its continuity at $0$ follow from Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad}, while its positivity follows from Lemma \ref{lem:lower-bound-w}. We thus only need to check the continuity of $\phi$. Fix $y_1, y_2>0$, both rational, and let $r'_k = r_k + \frac{y_1}{\sqrt{w(r_k)}}$. First, \[ \lim_{k\to\infty} \frac{w(r'_k)}{w(r_k)} = \phi(y_1) . \] By Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad}, \[ \liminf_{k\to\infty} \frac{w\left(r'_k + \frac{y_2}{\sqrt{w(r'_k)}}\right)}{w(r'_k)} \geq 1 - \frac{2\sigma}{\eta} y_2 . \] Since $r'_k \geq r_k$ we have $\frac{y_2}{\sqrt{w(r'_k)}} \geq \frac{y_2}{\sqrt{w(r_k)}}$, thus \[ \phi(y_1) \geq \phi(y_1+y_2) \geq \liminf_{k\to\infty} \frac{w\left(r_k + \frac{y_1+y_2}{\sqrt{w(r_k)}}\right)}{w(r_k)} \geq \phi(y_1) \left(1 - \frac{2\sigma}{\eta} y_2\right) \to \phi(y_1) \] as $y_2\to 0$, proving the continuity of $\phi$.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity and positivity from the continuity and lower-bound lemmas; continuity by applying the continuity lemma at shifted points.

nodes.name: Monotonicity, continuity at 0 and positivity follow from ear

nodes.name: Shift the sequence to r'_k.
nodes.statement: Fix $y_1, y_2>0$, both rational, and let $r'_k = r_k + \frac{y_1}{\sqrt{w(r_k)}}$. First, \[ \lim_{k\to\infty} \frac{w(r'_k)}{w(r_k)} = \phi(y_1) . \]

nodes.name: Apply the continuity lemma at r'_k.
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad}, \[ \liminf_{k\to\infty} \frac{w\left(r'_k + \frac{y_2}{\sqrt{w(r'_k)}}\right)}{w(r'_k)} \geq 1 - \frac{2\sigma}{\eta} y_2 . \]

nodes.name: Sandwich phi(y_1+y_2) and let y_2 -> 0.
nodes.statement: Since $r'_k \geq r_k$ we have $\frac{y_2}{\sqrt{w(r'_k)}} \geq \frac{y_2}{\sqrt{w(r_k)}}$, thus \[ \phi(y_1) \geq \phi(y_1+y_2) \geq \liminf_{k\to\infty} \frac{w\left(r_k + \frac{y_1+y_2}{\sqrt{w(r_k)}}\right)}{w(r_k)} \geq \phi(y_1) \left(1 - \frac{2\sigma}{\eta} y_2\right) \to \phi(y_1) \] as $y_2\to 0$, proving the continuity of $\phi$.
nodes.statement_short: Sandwich phi(y_1+y_2) and let y_2 -> 0.

nodes.name: Brownian motion under E^x and exit time
nodes.statement: Let $(B_u)_{u\geq 0}$ and $\E^x$ such that under $\E^x$, $(B_u)_{u\geq 0}$ is a standard Brownian motion with $B_0 = x$ a.s., and let $\tau_0^{B} = \inf\{t\geq 0 : B_t\leq 0\}$.

nodes.name: Functional equation for phi
nodes.statement: Any limit $\phi$ in \eqref{eq:phi} satisfies \begin{equation} \phi(y) = \E^{y/\eta}\left[ \exp\left(-\frac{\sigma^2}{2} \int_0^{\tau_0^B} \phi\left(\eta B_u\right) \d u \right) \right] \quad \text{ for every } y\geq 0 . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Recall the decomposition of the discount process into M_n an
nodes.statement: We now aim to control \[ \E\left[ W^{(r)}_{T'}\right] = \E\left[ w(S_{T'}) \kW^{(r)}_{T'} \right] . \] Recall the expression from $\kW^{(r)}_n$ in \eqref{eq:def-Z}: \begin{multline*} \kW^{(r)}_n = \left(\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} I_{k+1} \right) \exp\Bigg( - \underbrace{\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \left( I_{k+1} w(S_{k+1}) - \E\left[I^{(S_k, \RR, \delta)} w(S_k - Z) \, | \, \FF_k\right] \right)}_{M_n} \\ -\frac{1}{2} \underbrace{ \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} I_{k+1} \int w(S_{k}-y) \d M_{S_k - S_{k+1}}^{(S_k, \RR, \delta)}(y)}_{Y_n} \Bigg) . \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Recall the decomposition of the discount process into M_n and Y_n.

nodes.name: Doob's inequality makes M_n negligible.
nodes.statement: The process $(M_{n\wedge T'})_{n\geq 0}$ is a martingale with increments bounded in absolute value by $w(x-\RR)$, and we have almost surely $w(x-\RR) T' \leq w(x-\RR) \frac{A}{w(x)} \leq A(1+\nu)$. By Doob's maximal inequality, since $\E[M_{T'}^2] \leq (A/w(x)) (1+\nu)^2 w(x)^2 \to 0$ as $x\to 0$, there exists $c_x\to 0$ as $x\to\infty$ such that \begin{equation} \P\left( \sup_{0\leq k \leq A/w(x)} |M_{k\wedge T'}| \geq c_x \right) \leq c_x . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Doob's inequality makes M_n negligible.

nodes.name: Equation (38)
nodes.statement: \P\left( \sup_{0\leq k \leq A/w(x)} |M_{k\wedge T'}| \geq c_x \right) \leq c_x .
nodes.label: eq:controle-Z-1

nodes.name: Doob's inequality makes the martingale part of Y_n negligibl
nodes.statement: On the other hand, writing \[ X_k := I_{k+1} \int w(S_{k}-z) \d M_{S_{k}-S_{k+1}}^{(S_k, \RR, \delta)}(z) \quad , \quad \tilde Y_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \E\left[ X_k \ | \ \FF_k \right] \] then $\tilde Y_n$ is a predictable process such that $\tilde M_n := (Y_{n\wedge T'} - \tilde Y_{n\wedge T'})_{n\geq 0}$ is a martingale. By \eqref{eq:Palm-controle-M}, $0\leq X_k \leq \delta$ on $\{T'>k\}$, meaning that $(\tilde M_n)_{n\geq 0}$ is a martingale with increments bounded in absolute value by $\delta$. Hence $\E[\tilde M_n^2] \leq \delta \E[Y_{n\wedge T'}]$. By Doob's maximal inequality, since $\delta\to 0$ as $x\to\infty$ it thus suffices to show that $\E[Y_{n\wedge T'}]$ remains bounded as $x\to\infty$ to conclude that there exists $c'_x\to 0$ as $x\to\infty$ such that \begin{equation} \P\left( \sup_{0\leq k \leq A/w(x)} |\tilde M_{k\wedge T'}| \geq c'_x \right) \leq c'_x . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Doob's inequality makes the martingale part of Y_n negligible.

nodes.name: Equation (39)
nodes.statement: \P\left( \sup_{0\leq k \leq A/w(x)} |\tilde M_{k\wedge T'}| \geq c'_x \right) \leq c'_x .
nodes.label: eq:controle-Z-2

nodes.name: The conditional Palm term is asymptotically sigma^2 w(u).
nodes.statement: Let us compute $\E[X_k \, | \, \FF_{k}]$: for every $u$ large enough, \begin{align*} \E\left[ I^{(u,\RR,\delta)} \int w(u-z) \d M_{Z}^{(u, \RR, \delta)}(z) \right] &= \E\left[ \ind{E(u,\RR,\delta)} \int \left(\int w(u-\ell) \d(\chi-\delta_z)(\ell)\right) \d\chi(z) \right] \\ &= \E\left[ \ind{E(u,\RR,\delta)} (\chi(\R)-1)\int w(u-z)\d\chi(z) \right] . \end{align*} Using again Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad}, for every large enough $x$ we have $w(u) \leq w(u-\RR) \leq (1+\nu)w(u)$ for every $u\geq x$. As $u\to\infty$ we have in addition that $\inf_{u\geq x} \P(E(u,\RR,\delta)) = \P(E(x,\RR,\delta)) \to 1$ as $x\to\infty$ --- recall that $\underline{\delta}$ was chosen in the proof of Corollary \ref{cor:Feynman-Kac} in such a way that $\underline{\delta}(y)/w(y) \to \infty$ as $y\to\infty$. Then since $w(u-j)/w(u) \to 1$ for every fixed $j$ as $u\to\infty$ by Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad}, and by \eqref{eq:Palm-controle-M} and the dominated convergence theorem, we have as $u\to\infty$ \begin{align*} \frac{1}{w(u)} \E\left[ I^{(u,\RR,\delta)} \int w(u-z) \d M_{Z}^{(u, \RR, \delta)}(z) \right] \to \E\left[ \chi(\R)(\chi(\R)-1)\right] = \sigma^2 . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The conditional Palm term is asymptotically sigma^2 w(u).

nodes.name: Uniform control d_x of the compensator.
nodes.statement: Writing $d_v = \sup_{u\geq v} \left|\frac{1}{\sigma^2 w(u)} \E\left[ I^{(u,\RR,\delta)} \int w(u-z) \d M_{Z}^{(u, \RR, \delta)}(z) \right] - 1\right|$, we have $d_v \to 0$ as $v\to \infty$. The first consequence is that $\E[Y_{T'}] \leq (1+d_x) (A/w(x)) \sigma^2 w(x)$ which remains bounded as $x\to\infty$, thus finishing the proof of \eqref{eq:controle-Z-2}. In addition, as $x\to\infty$, for every $n$ \begin{equation} \left| \frac{\tilde Y_{n\wedge T'}}{\sigma^2 \sum_{k=0}^{n\wedge T'-1} w(S_k)} - 1 \right| \leq d_x \to 0 . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Uniform control d_x of the compensator.

nodes.name: Equation (40)
nodes.statement: \left| \frac{\tilde Y_{n\wedge T'}}{\sigma^2 \sum_{k=0}^{n\wedge T'-1} w(S_k)} - 1 \right| \leq d_x \to 0 .
nodes.label: eq:controle-Z-3

nodes.name: On the good event the discount factor is close to exp(-sigma
nodes.statement: Write $\AA$ for the intersection of the complement of the events in \eqref{eq:controle-Z-1} and \eqref{eq:controle-Z-2}; on $\AA$, for $x$ large enough we have for every $n$ \[ \left| \kW^{(r)}_{n\wedge T'} - \exp\left(-\frac{\sigma^2}{2} \sum_{k=0}^{n\wedge T'-1} w(S_k) \right) \right| \leq 2(c_x + c'_x + d_x) . \]
nodes.statement_short: On the good event the discount factor is close to exp(-sigma^2/2 sum w(S_k)).

Since $w$ is decreasing, $\left( rac{S_{\lfloor Nufloor}-x}{\sqrt{\lfloor Nu floor}}ight)_{0\leq u\leq A} 	o (\eta B_u)_{0\leq u\leq A}$ as $N	o\infty$ in distribution, where $(B_u)_{u\geq 0}$ is a standard Brownian motion with $B_0=y/\eta$ a.s., and $w(x) 	au_x 	o 	au^B_0$, taking $N = 1/w(x)$ and by the locally uniform convergence to $\phi$ continuous using Proposition ef{prop:continuity-phi}, taking $x$ along the sequence used to define $\phi$ \[ \sum_{k=0}^{T'-1} w(S_k) = w(x) \sum_{k=0}^{T'-1}  rac{w(S_k)}{w(x)} 	o \int_0^{	au_0^B \wedge A} \phi(\eta (r-x+B_u)) \d u \] in distribution as $x	o\infty$, hence  egin{align*} \left| \phi(y) - \E^{y/\eta}\left[ \exp\left( -  rac{\sigma^2}{2} \int_0^{	au_0^B \wedge A} \phi(\eta B_u) \d u ight) ight] ight| \leq

nodes.name: Proof of the tail theorem (conclusion)
nodes.statement: We can use the rest of the proof of \cite{lalley2015maximal} directly: their Corollary 12 gives the limit form \[ \phi(y) = \left( \frac{\sigma y}{\eta\sqrt{6}} +1 \right)^{-2} \] and their Lemma 13 follows from our observation at the end of Section \ref{sec:lower-bound-ratio}. The proof of their Theorem 1 adapts in a straightforward manner, giving our Theorem \ref{th:main-tail}.
nodes.statement_short: Solve the functional equation as in Lalley–Shao (Corollary 12) to get phi(y) = (sigma y/(eta sqrt 6) + 1)^{-2}, then adapt their Theorem 1.

nodes.name: Proof sketch of the point-probability theorem
nodes.statement: The idea is to show that $g(r) := \P(\sup_{v\in T} \Lambda_v = r)$ is sufficiently regular, namely that \[ \lim_{\varepsilon\to 0} \limsup_{r\to\infty} \sup_{(1-\varepsilon)r \leq y \leq (1+\varepsilon)r} \left| \frac{g(y)}{g(r)} - 1 \right| = 0 . \] We then use the fact that $ w(r) \sim \sum_{y>r} g(y) $ as $r\to\infty$, and thus that \[ \sum_{(1-\varepsilon)r < y \leq (1+\varepsilon)r} g(y) \sim w(r(1-\varepsilon)) - w(r(1+\varepsilon)) \] to deduce Theorem \ref{th:main-condition}.

nodes.statement_short: Show g(r)=P(max=r) is regularly varying-like, then difference the tail w.

nodes.name: A recurrent walk visits a fixed point
nodes.statement: Let $(U_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a random walk on $\Z$ with $U_0 = 0$ a.s. and i.i.d. steps with $\E[U_1]=0$ and $\E[U_1^2]=\eta^2<\infty$. The random walk is recurrent, so that writing $\tau_k$ for the $k$-th visit of $0$, we have $\tau_1 < \infty$ a.s. In particular, $ \P(\tau_k \leq n/2) \to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$. Then for every fixed $y\in\Z$, since by the strong Markov property $\P(\exists\, \tau_k \leq u < \tau_{k+1} : U_u = y) = \P(\exists\, 0 \leq u < \tau_{1} : U_u = y)>0$, we have \begin{equation} \P(\exists \, 0 \leq u \leq n/2 : U_u = y) \ulim n \infty 1 . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4.1 Probability that a random walk visits a point

nodes.name: Equation (41)
nodes.statement: \P(\exists \, 0 \leq u \leq n/2 : U_u = y) \ulim n \infty 1 .
nodes.section: 4.1 Probability that a random walk visits a point
nodes.label: eq:limit-P-being-at-a-point

nodes.name: Probability that a random walk visits a point
nodes.statement: For every $y<0$, write $T_{y} = \inf\{n\geq 0, U_n \leq y\}$. Following \cite[Section 5.1.1]{lawler2010random}, by Theorem 5.1.7 therein, there exists a constant such that for every $n\geq 1$ \[ \P(T_y > n/2) \leq \cste \frac{1-y}{\sqrt{n}} , \] and by Lemma 5.1.9, for every $m\geq 0$ \[ \P(U_{T_y} \leq y - m) \leq \cste \E\left[ U_1^2 \ind{|U_1| \geq m} \right] \ulim m \infty 0 . \] For every $\varepsilon>0$, taking $m$ large enough that the right-hand side is smaller than $\varepsilon/2$, and using \eqref{eq:limit-P-being-at-a-point} to choose $n_\varepsilon$ such that for every $n\geq n_\varepsilon$ \[ \inf_{0\leq k \leq m} \P\left(\exists \, 0\leq u \leq \frac{n}{2}: U_u = k\right) \geq 1-\frac{\varepsilon}{2} , \] we obtain that for every $y<0$ and every $n \geq n_\varepsilon$, by the strong Markov property \begin{equation} \P\left(\exists \, 0 \leq u \leq n, U_u = y\right) \geq 1-\varepsilon-\cste \frac{1-y}{\sqrt{n}} . \end{equation} We easily see that the same holds for $y>0$, up to a change in the constants involved.
nodes.section: 4.1 Probability that a random walk visits a point
nodes.statement_short: For n large, a centered finite-variance Z-walk visits y within n steps with probability at least 1 - eps - C(1-y)/sqrt(n).

nodes.name: Equation (42)
nodes.statement: \P\left(\exists \, 0 \leq u \leq n, U_u = y\right) \geq 1-\varepsilon-\cste \frac{1-y}{\sqrt{n}} .

nodes.name: Lower bound g(r) by a size-biased expectation of g(r-Z).
nodes.statement: Bound the first term inside the expectation from below by $0$. Since $h$ is increasing, $\e^{-x} \geq 1-x$, $\ln(1+x)\leq x$ hence $-\ln h(x) \leq w(x)$, and recalling $E(r,R,\delta)$ from \eqref{eq:event-E-rRd}, \begin{align} g(r) &\geq \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int g(r-x) \left(1 + \int \ln h(r-1-y) \d(\chi-\delta_x)(y) \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ &\geq \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} g(r-Z) \left(1 - \int w(r-1-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y) \right) \right] . \end{align}
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound g(r) by a size-biased expectation of g(r-Z).

nodes.name: Equation (44)
nodes.statement: g(r) &\geq \E\left[ \ind{E(r,R,\delta)} \int g(r-x) \left(1 + \int \ln h(r-1-y) \d(\chi-\delta_x)(y) \right) \d\chi(x) \right] \\ &\geq \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} g(r-Z) \left(1 - \int w(r-1-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y) \right) \right] .
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum

nodes.name: Bound the Palm integral and pass to an exponential form.
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:Palm-controle-M} we know that a.s. $M^{(r,R,\delta)}_Z(\R)\leq \frac{\delta}{w(r-R)}$ and $M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}((r,\infty)=0)$. Taking $r>2r_0+1$ and $r_0+1\leq R \leq r/2$, on $\{I^{(r,R,\delta)}\neq 0\}$, for $M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}$-a.e. $y$ we have $w(r-1-y) \leq w(r-R-1)$. This means that \begin{equation} \int w(r-1-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y) \leq \delta \frac{w(r-R-1)}{w(r-R)} . \end{equation} Since $w(x-1)/w(x)\to 1$ as $x\to\infty$, we can assume that the right-hand side is smaller than $2\delta$ for every $x\geq r_0$ (up to taking $r_0$ larger). Taking $\delta\leq 1/4$, and using that $1 - x \geq \e^{- (2 \ln 2) x}$ for every $x\in (0,1/2)$, we obtain \begin{align} g(r) &\geq \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} g(r-Z) \exp\left(- (4\ln 2) \int w(r-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y) \right) \right] . \end{align}
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.statement_short: Bound the Palm integral and pass to an exponential form.

nodes.name: Equation (46)
nodes.statement: \int w(r-1-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y) \leq \delta \frac{w(r-R-1)}{w(r-R)} .
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.label: eq:bound-integral-M

nodes.name: Equation (47)
nodes.statement: g(r) &\geq \E\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} g(r-Z) \exp\left(- (4\ln 2) \int w(r-y) \d M_Z^{(r,R,\delta)}(y) \right) \right] .
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.label: eq:supermg-g

nodes.name: Hitting times T_y of nearby points are at most n with high p
nodes.statement:
Let $
u>0$ and $\varepsilon>0$. For every $y$ with $|y-r|\leq 
u r$, define $T_y := \inf\{n \geq 0 : S_n = y\}$. By \eqref{eq:proba-visit-RW}, there exists $c<\infty$ such that for every $n\geq n_\varepsilon$ \[ \P(T_y > n) \leq \varepsilon + c rac{1+|y-r|}{\sqrt{n}} . \] Assume henceforth that $n =  rac{c^2 
u^2 r^2}{\varepsilon^2}$, so that $\P(T_y > n) \leq 2\varepsilon$ uniformly over every $|y-r|\leq 
u r$.
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.statement_short: Hitting times T_y of nearby points are at most n with high probability.

nodes.name: Fix R, delta and the good event that the walk stays above 3r
nodes.statement: Fix $R_j = R = r/8$ and $\delta_j = \delta$ for every $j$, and define the event $\AA := \{ \inf_{0\leq k \leq n} S_k \geq 3r/4 \}$. Since \[ \P(I_{k+1} = 0 \, | \, \FF_k) \leq \P\left(\Lambda > R\right) + \P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\delta}{w(S_k-R)}\right) , \] we can find $\delta = \delta(r) \to 0$ as $r\to\infty$ such that as $r\to\infty$, \[ \P\left(\AA \cap \left\{\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} I_{k+1} = 0 \right\}\right) \ulim r \infty 0 . \]
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.statement_short: Fix R, delta and the good event that the walk stays above 3r/4.

nodes.name: Optional stopping for a positive supermartingale.
nodes.statement: By the Markov property together with \eqref{eq:supermg-g}, if $T''(\omega) := \inf\{j : S_j < 3r/4\}$ and \begin{align*} W_j := g(S_j) \left(\prod_{k=0}^{j-1} I_{k+1}\right) \exp\left(- (4\ln 2) \sum_{k=0}^{j-1} \int w(S_k-z) \d M_{S_k-S_{k+1}}^{(S_k, R, \delta)}(z) \right) \end{align*} then $(W_{j\wedge T''})_{j\geq 0}$ is a positive $(\FF_j)_{j\geq 0}$-supermartingale. By the optional stopping theorem on the bounded stopping time $n \wedge T_y \wedge T''$, and noting that $\{T''>n\} \supset \AA$, \begin{align} g(r) \geq \E\left[ \ind{\AA} g(S_{n\wedge T_y}) \left(\prod_{k=0}^{n\wedge T_y-1} I_{k+1}\right) \exp\left(- (4\ln 2) \sum_{k=0}^{n\wedge T_y-1} \int w(S_k-z) \d M_{S_k-S_{k+1}}^{(S_k, R, \delta)}(z) \right) \right] . \end{align}
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.statement_short: Optional stopping for a positive supermartingale.

nodes.name: Equation (48)
nodes.statement: g(r) \geq \E\left[ \ind{\AA} g(S_{n\wedge T_y}) \left(\prod_{k=0}^{n\wedge T_y-1} I_{k+1}\right) \exp\left(- (4\ln 2) \sum_{k=0}^{n\wedge T_y-1} \int w(S_k-z) \d M_{S_k-S_{k+1}}^{(S_k, R, \delta)}(z) \right) \right] .
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.label: eq:g-supermg

nodes.name: Doob's inequality bounds the probability of leaving the good
nodes.statement: Clearly $g(S_{T_y}) = g(y)$. We aim to bound the other factors in \eqref{eq:g-supermg}. By Doob's maximal inequality, \[ \P(\AA^c) = \P\left( \sup_{0\leq j \leq n} -(S_j-r) > r/4\right) \leq \frac{\E[(S_n-r)^2]}{(r/4)^2} \leq 16 \eta^2 \frac{c^2 \nu^2}{\varepsilon^2} \ulim \nu 0 0 . \]
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.statement_short: Doob's inequality bounds the probability of leaving the good event.

nodes.name: Markov's inequality controls the discount factor.
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, recalling $d_r$ from the proof of Proposition ef{prop:func-equation-phi}, \[ \E\left[ \ind{\AA} I_{k+1} \int w(S_k-z) \d M_{S_k-S_{k+1}}^{(S_k, R, \delta)}(z) \ | \ \FF_k ight] \leq w(r/2) \sigma^2 (1+d_{r/2}) \] hence, assuming that $r$ is large enough that $d_{r/2}\leq 1$ and $w(r/2)\leq C r^{-2} / 2$ for some $C<\infty$ \[ \E\left[ \ind{\AA} \left(\prod_{k=0}^{j-1} I_{k+1}ight) \sum_{k=0}^{j-1} \int w(S_k-z) \d M_{S_k-S_{k+1}}^{(S_k, R, \delta)}(z) ight] \leq n w(r/2)\sigma^2 (1+d_{r/2}) \leq C  rac{\sigma^2 c^2 
u^2}{\varepsilon^2} . \] By Markov’s inequality, writing \[ \EE := \left\{ \ind{\AA} \left(\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} I_{k+1}ight) \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \int w(S_k-y) \d M_{S_k-S_{k+1}}^{(S_k, R, \delta)}(y) \ > \ C  rac{\sigma^2 c^2 
u^2}{\varepsilon^3} ight\} \] we have $\P(\EE)\leq \varepsilon$ for every $r$ large enough, and outside of $\EE$, for every $0\leq j \leq n$  egin{align*} & \ind{\AA} \left(\prod_{k=0}^{j-1} I_{k+1}ight) \exp\left( - (4\ln 2) \sum_{k=0}^{j-1} \int w(S_k-y) \d M_{S_k-S_{k+1}}^{(S_k, R, \delta)}(y) ight) \ &\geq \ind{\AA}\left(\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} I_{k+1}ight) \exp\left( - (4\ln 2) C  rac{c^2 
u^2 \sigma^2}{\varepsilon^3} ight) . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.statement_short: Markov's inequality controls the discount factor.

nodes.name: Combine to get g(r) >= (1-6 eps) g(y).
nodes.statement: Take $\nu>0$ small enough and $r$ large enough that \[ \exp\left( - (4\ln 2) C\frac{c^2 \nu^2 \sigma^2}{\varepsilon^3} \right) \geq 1-\varepsilon \quad \text{and} \quad \P\left(\AA \cap \left\{\prod_{j=1}^{n} I_j = 0 \right\}\right) \leq \varepsilon \quad \text{and} \quad \P(\AA^c) \leq \varepsilon, \] and we get that on the event $\EE^c \cap \AA \cap \left\{\prod_{j=1}^{n} I_j = 0 \right\} \cap \{T_y\leq n\}$ of probability at least $1-5\varepsilon$, the content of the expectation in \eqref{eq:g-supermg} is larger than $g(y)(1-\varepsilon) $, hence \[ g(r) \geq (1-6\varepsilon) g(y) . \]
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.statement_short: Combine to get g(r) >= (1-6 eps) g(y).

nodes.name: Sum g over a window and use the tail asymptotic of w.
nodes.section: 4.2 Lower bound on the probability distribution function of the supremum
nodes.statement_short: Sum g over a window and use the tail asymptotic of w.

nodes.name: Weighted distribution function h_t
nodes.statement: We control the Laplace transform of the weight of $T$ conditionally on $\sup_{v\in T} \Lambda_v$ by considering for every $t\geq 0$ \[h_t(r) = \E\left[ \e^{-t \sum_{v\in T} D_v} \ind{\sup_{v\in T} \Lambda_v \leq r}\right] \quad , \quad h_t(\infty) = \E\left[ \e^{-t \sum_{v\in T} D_v}\right] . \]

nodes.name: Equation (49)
nodes.statement: h_t(r) = \E\left[ \e^{-t D} \prod_{i=1}^{\chi(\R)} h_t(r-X_i) \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \right] .
nodes.label: eq:2convolution-equation-1

nodes.name: Generating function Phi_t
nodes.statement: When $r=\infty$, and writing $\Phi_t(x) = \E\left[\e^{-tD} x^{\chi(\R)}\right]$, this becomes \begin{align} h_t(\infty) = \Phi_t(h_t(\infty)) . \end{align}

nodes.name: Equation (50)
nodes.statement: h_t(\infty) = \Phi_t(h_t(\infty)) .
nodes.label: eq:2htinf-point-fixe

nodes.name: h_t(infinity) is the unique fixed point of Phi_t
nodes.statement: For every $t\geq 0$, the function $\Phi_t$ is convex, $\Phi_t(0)>0$ and $\Phi_t(1)\leq 1$, so $h_t(\infty)$ is the unique solution of the equation $x = \Phi_t(x)$ in $[0,1]$.

nodes.name: Taylor expansion of Phi_t and asymptotics of 1 - h_t(infinity)
nodes.statement: For every $p \in (1,\infty)$ and every random variable $W\in L^p$, \[ \E\left[W \left(1 - \e^{-tD}\right)\right] = o\left(t^{\frac{p-1}{p}}\right) . \] For every $t\geq 0$ define \[ f(t) := \E\left[\chi(\R) \e^{-tD}\right] -1 . \] Then $f(t) = o(t^{1/2})$, \begin{equation} \Phi_t(x) = x + \E\left[ \e^{-tD}-1 \right] + (x-1)f(t) + \frac{(x-1)^2}{2} \E\left[ (\chi(\R)^2 - \chi(\R))\e^{-t D} \right] + o((x-1)^2) \end{equation} with a $o((x-1)^2)$ that is uniform over all $t\geq 0$, and as $t\to 0$ with $t\geq 0$ \begin{equation} 1-h_t(\infty) \sim \sqrt{\frac{2 t}{\sigma^2}} \ . \end{equation}
assumptions: For every $p \in (1,\infty)$ and every random variable $W\in L^p$
nodes.statement_short: Second-order expansion of Phi_t near 1 uniform in t, giving 1 - h_t(inf) ~ sqrt(2t/sigma^2).
nodes.label: lem:phit-taylor-expansion

nodes.name: Equation (51)
nodes.statement: \Phi_t(x) = x + \E\left[ \e^{-tD}-1 \right] + (x-1)f(t) + \frac{(x-1)^2}{2} \E\left[ (\chi(\R)^2 - \chi(\R))\e^{-t D} \right] + o((x-1)^2)
nodes.label: eq:phit-taylor-expansion

nodes.name: Equation (52)
nodes.statement: 1-h_t(\infty) \sim \sqrt{\frac{2 t}{\sigma^2}} \ .
nodes.label: eq:htinfty-taylor-expansion

nodes.name: Remark: general weights
nodes.statement: More generally, if $\mu_q(t) = \E[(1-\e^{-tD})^q ]$ then the Lemma holds with $1-h_t(\infty)\sim\sqrt{2\mu_1(t)/\sigma^2}$ as soon as $\mu_2(t) = o(\mu_1(t))$. This is the case if $\E[D]<\infty$, and there are cases where $\E[D]=\infty$ where this does not hold---typically when the tail of $D$ is not regular enough.
nodes.statement_short: If E[D] is infinite, 1-h_t(inf) ~ sqrt(2 mu_1(t)/sigma^2) as long as mu_2 = o(mu_1).

nodes.name: Proof of the Taylor expansion lemma
nodes.statement:
Using Hölder's inequality, letting $q =  rac{p}{p-1}$ \[ \left| \E\left[W \left(1 - \e^{-tD}ight)ight]ight| \leq \E\left[|W|^pight]^{1/p} \E\left[\left(1 - \e^{-tD}ight)^qight]^{1/q} . \] Split the second expectation on $\{ tD>\varepsilon\}$ and $\{tD\leq \varepsilon\}$, and use $|\e^{-x}-1|\leq x$ for $x\geq 0$:  egin{align*} \E\left[\left(1 - \e^{-tD}ight)^qight] &\leq \E\left[\left(1 - \e^{-tD}ight)^q \ind{tD \leq \varepsilon}ight] + \E\left[\left(1 - \e^{-tD}ight)^q \ind{tD>\varepsilon} ight] \ &\leq \varepsilon^{q-1} \E[tD] + \P\left( D >  rac{\varepsilon}{t}ight) \ &\leq \varepsilon^{q-1} t +  rac{2t}{\varepsilon \psi_D(\varepsilon/t)} \end{align*} with $\psi_D$ given by Lemma ef{lem:refined-Markov}: we can take $\varepsilon = \varepsilon(t)$ that goes to zero sufficiently slowly that the above expression is $o(t)$, proving our claim. The bound on $f$ follows from it with $p=2$ and $W = \chi(\R)$. Next is the Taylor expansion of $\Phi_t(x)$ near $x=1$ (with $x\leq 1$): for every $\varepsilon>0$  egin{multline*} \left| \Phi_t(x) - \E\left[ \e^{-tD}\left( 1 + \chi(\R) \ln x +  rac{\chi(\R)^2}{2} (\ln x)^2 ight) ight] ight| \ \leq \E\left[ \left| \e^{\chi(\R)\ln x} - 1 - \chi(\R) \ln x -  rac{\chi(\R)^2}{2} (\ln x)^2 ight| ight] . \end{multline*} Split it on $\{ \chi(\R)\ln x < -\varepsilon\}$ and $\{\chi(\R)\ln x \geq -\varepsilon\}$, using $|\e^{-u} - 1 - u - u^2/2| \leq \omega(u) u^2$ for $u\leq 0$ with $\omega$ increasing and $\omega(u) 	o 0$ as $u	o 0$:  egin{equation} \E\left[ \left| \e^{\chi(\R)\ln x} - 1 - \chi(\R) \ln x -  rac{\chi(\R)^2}{2} (\ln x)^2 ight| \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x > -\varepsilon} ight] \leq \omega(\varepsilon) (\ln x)^2 \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 ight] . \end{equation} On the other hand, using first $|\e^{-x}-1| \leq 1$, then Lemma ef{lem:refined-Markov} to obtain $\psi_\chi$ (increasing to $+\infty$) and $C := \E[\chi(\R)^2 \psi_\chi(\chi(\R))]$,  egin{align} & \E\left[ \left| \e^{\chi(\R)\ln x} - 1 - \chi(\R) \ln x -  rac{\chi(\R)^2}{2} (\ln x)^2 ight| \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\leq \P\left( \chi(\R) \leq  rac{-\varepsilon}{\ln x} ight) - (\ln x) \E\left[ \chi(\R)\ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] +  rac{(\ln x)^2}{2} \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\leq  rac{C}{\varepsilon^2 \psi_\chi(-\varepsilon/\ln x)} (\ln x)^2 +  rac{(\ln x)^2}{\varepsilon \psi_\chi(-\varepsilon/\ln x)} \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 \psi_\chi(\chi(\R)) \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\quad +  rac{(\ln x)^2}{2 \psi_\chi(-\varepsilon/\ln x)} \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 \psi_\chi(\chi(\R)) \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\leq C\left( \varepsilon^{-2} + \varepsilon^{-1} +  rac 1 2 ight)  rac{(\ln x)^2}{\psi_\chi(-\varepsilon / \ln x)} . \end{align} We can find $\varepsilon = \varepsilon(x)$ that goes to $0$ sufficiently slowly as $x	o 1$ such that the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:lem-phit-taylor-exp-1} and \eqref{eq:lem-phit-taylor-exp-2} are both $o((x-1)^2)$, uniformly in $t\geq 0$. To prove \eqref{eq:phit-taylor-expansion} we need to control  egin{align*} &\Bigg| \E\left[ \e^{-tD}\left( 1 + \chi(\R) \ln x +  rac{\chi(\R)^2}{2} (\ln x)^2 ight) ight] \ &\qquad - x - \E\left[ \e^{-tD}-1 ight] - (x-1) \left(\E\left[\chi(\R) \e^{-tD}ight]-1ight) -  rac{(x-1)^2}{2}\E\left[ \e^{-tD}\left( \chi(\R)^2 - \chi(\R)ight)ight] \Bigg| \ &\leq \E\left[ \chi(\R) \left|\ln x - (x-1) +  rac{(x-1)^2}{2}ight| + \chi(\R)^2 \left|\ln(x)^2 - (x-1)^2ight| ight] = o((x-1)^2) \end{align*} uniformly in $t\geq 0$. Let us now prove \eqref{eq:htinfty-taylor-expansion} from the previous estimates. Since $\Phi_t'(x) = \E[\chi(\R) \e^{-t D} x^{\chi(\R)}]$ we have $0\leq \Phi_t'\leq 1$ on $[0,1]$; in addition $\Phi_t(1) 	o 1$ as $t	o 0$, so that $h_t(\infty) 	o 1$ as $t	o 0$. Hence using \eqref{eq:phit-taylor-expansion}, writing for simplicity $x := 1-h_t(\infty)$ in the rest of the proof  egin{align*} 1-x = 1-x + \E\left[\e^{-tD}-1ight] - x f(t) +  rac{\sigma^2 + o(1)}{2} x^2 . \end{align*} Using that $\E[\e^{-tD}-1] \sim t$ as $t	o 0$ with $t\geq 0$, the solution must be  egin{align*} 1-h_t(\infty) =  rac{-f(t) + \sqrt{f(t)^2 + 2 \sigma^2 t + o(t)}}{\sigma^2 + o(1)} \sim \sqrt{ rac{2 t}{\sigma^2}} \ . \end{align*} This finishes the proof of Lemma ef{lem:phit-taylor-expansion}.
nodes.statement_short: Hölder plus the refined Markov inequality, then a split Taylor estimate; solve the quadratic fixed-point equation for 1-h_t(inf).

nodes.name: Hölder and the refined Markov inequality give o(t^{(p-1)/p})
nodes.statement: Using Hölder's inequality, letting $q = \frac{p}{p-1}$ \[ \left| \E\left[W \left(1 - \e^{-tD}\right)\right]\right| \leq \E\left[|W|^p\right]^{1/p} \E\left[\left(1 - \e^{-tD}\right)^q\right]^{1/q} . \] Split the second expectation on $\{ tD>\varepsilon\}$ and $\{tD\leq \varepsilon\}$, and use $|\e^{-x}-1|\leq x$ for $x\geq 0$: \begin{align*} \E\left[\left(1 - \e^{-tD}\right)^q\right] &\leq \E\left[\left(1 - \e^{-tD}\right)^q \ind{tD \leq \varepsilon}\right] + \E\left[\left(1 - \e^{-tD}\right)^q \ind{tD>\varepsilon} \right] \\ &\leq \varepsilon^{q-1} \E[tD] + \P\left( D > \frac{\varepsilon}{t}\right) \\ &\leq \varepsilon^{q-1} t + \frac{2t}{\varepsilon \psi_D(\varepsilon/t)} \end{align*} with $\psi_D$ given by Lemma \ref{lem:refined-Markov}: we can take $\varepsilon = \varepsilon(t)$ that goes to zero sufficiently slowly that the above expression is $o(t)$, proving our claim.
nodes.statement_short: Hölder and the refined Markov inequality give o(t^{(p-1)/p}).

nodes.name: Deduce the bound on f and set up the Taylor expansion of Phi
nodes.statement: The bound on $f$ follows from it with $p=2$ and $W = \chi(\R)$. Next is the Taylor expansion of $\Phi_t(x)$ near $x=1$ (with $x\leq 1$): for every $\varepsilon>0$ \begin{multline*} \left| \Phi_t(x) - \E\left[ \e^{-tD}\left( 1 + \chi(\R) \ln x + \frac{\chi(\R)^2}{2} (\ln x)^2 \right) \right] \right| \\ \leq \E\left[ \left| \e^{\chi(\R)\ln x} - 1 - \chi(\R) \ln x - \frac{\chi(\R)^2}{2} (\ln x)^2 \right| \right] . \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Deduce the bound on f and set up the Taylor expansion of Phi_t.

nodes.name: Small-jump part of the expansion error.
nodes.statement: Split it on $\{ \chi(\R)\ln x < -\varepsilon\}$ and $\{\chi(\R)\ln x \geq -\varepsilon\}$, using $|\e^{-u} - 1 - u - u^2/2| \leq \omega(u) u^2$ for $u\leq 0$ with $\omega$ increasing and $\omega(u) \to 0$ as $u\to 0$: \begin{equation} \E\left[ \left| \e^{\chi(\R)\ln x} - 1 - \chi(\R) \ln x - \frac{\chi(\R)^2}{2} (\ln x)^2 \right| \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x > -\varepsilon} \right] \leq \omega(\varepsilon) (\ln x)^2 \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 \right] . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Small-jump part of the expansion error.

nodes.name: Equation (53)
nodes.statement: \E\left[ \left| \e^{\chi(\R)\ln x} - 1 - \chi(\R) \ln x - \frac{\chi(\R)^2}{2} (\ln x)^2 \right| \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x > -\varepsilon} \right] \leq \omega(\varepsilon) (\ln x)^2 \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 \right] .
nodes.label: eq:lem-phit-taylor-exp-1

nodes.name: Large-jump part via the refined Markov inequality.
nodes.statement:
On the other hand, using first $|\e^{-x}-1| \leq 1$, then Lemma ef{lem:refined-Markov} to obtain $\psi_\chi$ (increasing to $+\infty$) and $C := \E[\chi(\R)^2 \psi_\chi(\chi(\R))]$,  egin{align} & \E\left[ \left| \e^{\chi(\R)\ln x} - 1 - \chi(\R) \ln x -  rac{\chi(\R)^2}{2} (\ln x)^2 ight| \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\leq \P\left( \chi(\R) \leq  rac{-\varepsilon}{\ln x} ight) - (\ln x) \E\left[ \chi(\R)\ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] +  rac{(\ln x)^2}{2} \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\leq  rac{C}{\varepsilon^2 \psi_\chi(-\varepsilon/\ln x)} (\ln x)^2 +  rac{(\ln x)^2}{\varepsilon \psi_\chi(-\varepsilon/\ln x)} \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 \psi_\chi(\chi(\R)) \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\quad +  rac{(\ln x)^2}{2 \psi_\chi(-\varepsilon/\ln x)} \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 \psi_\chi(\chi(\R)) \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\leq C\left( \varepsilon^{-2} + \varepsilon^{-1} +  rac 1 2 ight)  rac{(\ln x)^2}{\psi_\chi(-\varepsilon / \ln x)} . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Large-jump part via the refined Markov inequality.

nodes.name: Equation (54)
nodes.statement:
& \E\left[ \left| \e^{\chi(\R)\ln x} - 1 - \chi(\R) \ln x -  rac{\chi(\R)^2}{2} (\ln x)^2 ight| \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\leq \P\left( \chi(\R) \leq  rac{-\varepsilon}{\ln x} ight) - (\ln x) \E\left[ \chi(\R)\ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] +  rac{(\ln x)^2}{2} \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\leq  rac{C}{\varepsilon^2 \psi_\chi(-\varepsilon/\ln x)} (\ln x)^2 +  rac{(\ln x)^2}{\varepsilon \psi_\chi(-\varepsilon/\ln x)} \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 \psi_\chi(\chi(\R)) \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\quad +  rac{(\ln x)^2}{2 \psi_\chi(-\varepsilon/\ln x)} \E\left[ \chi(\R)^2 \psi_\chi(\chi(\R)) \ind{\chi(\R)\ln x \leq -\varepsilon} ight] 
onumber \ &\leq C\left( \varepsilon^{-2} + \varepsilon^{-1} +  rac 1 2 ight)  rac{(\ln x)^2}{\psi_\chi(-\varepsilon / \ln x)} .
nodes.label: eq:lem-phit-taylor-exp-2

nodes.name: Combine to the uniform o((x-1)^2) expansion.
nodes.statement: We can find $\varepsilon = \varepsilon(x)$ that goes to $0$ sufficiently slowly as $x\to 1$ such that the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:lem-phit-taylor-exp-1} and \eqref{eq:lem-phit-taylor-exp-2} are both $o((x-1)^2)$, uniformly in $t\geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine to the uniform o((x-1)^2) expansion.

nodes.name: Plug x = 1-h_t(inf) into the expansion.
nodes.statement: Let us now prove \eqref{eq:htinfty-taylor-expansion} from the previous estimates. Since $\Phi_t'(x) = \E[\chi(\R) \e^{-t D} x^{\chi(\R)}]$ we have $0\leq \Phi_t'\leq 1$ on $[0,1]$; in addition $\Phi_t(1) \to 1$ as $t\to 0$, so that $h_t(\infty) \to 1$ as $t\to 0$. Hence using \eqref{eq:phit-taylor-expansion}, writing for simplicity $x := 1-h_t(\infty)$ in the rest of the proof \begin{align*} 1-x = 1-x + \E\left[\e^{-tD}-1\right] - x f(t) + \frac{\sigma^2 + o(1)}{2} x^2 . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Plug x = 1-h_t(inf) into the expansion.

nodes.name: Solve the quadratic equation.
nodes.statement: Using that $\E[\e^{-tD}-1] \sim t$ as $t\to 0$ with $t\geq 0$, the solution must be \begin{align*} 1-h_t(\infty) = \frac{-f(t) + \sqrt{f(t)^2 + 2 \sigma^2 t + o(t)}}{\sigma^2 + o(1)} \sim \sqrt{\frac{2 t}{\sigma^2}} \ . \end{align*} This finishes the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:phit-taylor-expansion}.
nodes.statement_short: Solve the quadratic equation.

nodes.name: Speed of convergence of tilted expectations
nodes.statement: Let $W \in L^2$, then as $t\to 0$ \begin{equation} \E[W] - \E\left[ \e^{-tD} h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1} W \right] = \sqrt{\frac{2t}{\sigma^2}} \ \E[ W(\chi(\R)-1) ] + o(t^{1/2}) . \end{equation}
nodes.label: lem:speed-cv-expectation-Et

nodes.name: Equation (55)
nodes.statement: \E[W] - \E\left[ \e^{-tD} h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1} W \right] = \sqrt{\frac{2t}{\sigma^2}} \ \E[ W(\chi(\R)-1) ] + o(t^{1/2}) .

nodes.name: Proof of the speed-of-convergence lemma
nodes.statement: Write \begin{align*} &\E[W] - \E\left[ \e^{-tD} h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1} W \right] - (1-h_t(\infty)) \E[ W(\chi(\R)-1) ] \\ &= \E\left[ W\left( 1 - \e^{-tD}h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1} - (1-h_t(\infty))(\chi(\R)-1) \right)\right] \\ &= \E\left[ W\left(1 + (h_t(\infty)-1)(\chi(\R)-1) - h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1} + h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1}\left( 1-\e^{-tD} \right) \right)\right] . \end{align*} Then the absolute value of the left-hand side is smaller than \begin{align*} \E\left[|W| \left|1 + (h_t(\infty)-1)(\chi(\R)-1) - h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1}\right|\right] + h_t(\infty)^{-1} \E\left[|W| \left( 1-\e^{-tD} \right)\right] . \end{align*} We use Lemma \ref{lem:phit-taylor-expansion} and the fact that $h_t(\infty)\to 1$ to bound the second term by $o(t^{1/2})$ as $t\to 0$. The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and the same kind of control as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:phit-taylor-expansion} can be used to bound the first term by $o(1-h_t(\infty)) = o(t^{1/2})$. We conclude by using the asymptotic of $1-h_t(\infty)$ from Lemma \ref{lem:phit-taylor-expansion}.
nodes.statement_short: Algebraic rewriting, then Cauchy–Schwarz and the Taylor lemma bound each term by o(t^{1/2}).

nodes.name: Rewrite the difference.
nodes.statement: Write \begin{align*} &\E[W] - \E\left[ \e^{-tD} h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1} W \right] - (1-h_t(\infty)) \E[ W(\chi(\R)-1) ] \\ &= \E\left[ W\left( 1 - \e^{-tD}h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1} - (1-h_t(\infty))(\chi(\R)-1) \right)\right] \\ &= \E\left[ W\left(1 + (h_t(\infty)-1)(\chi(\R)-1) - h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1} + h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1}\left( 1-\e^{-tD} \right) \right)\right] . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the difference.

nodes.name: Bound by two terms.
nodes.statement: Then the absolute value of the left-hand side is smaller than \begin{align*} \E\left[|W| \left|1 + (h_t(\infty)-1)(\chi(\R)-1) - h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1}\right|\right] + h_t(\infty)^{-1} \E\left[|W| \left( 1-\e^{-tD} \right)\right] . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound by two terms.

nodes.name: Both terms are o(t^{1/2}); use the asymptotic of 1-h_t(inf).
nodes.statement: We use Lemma \ref{lem:phit-taylor-expansion} and the fact that $h_t(\infty)\to 1$ to bound the second term by $o(t^{1/2})$ as $t\to 0$. The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and the same kind of control as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:phit-taylor-expansion} can be used to bound the first term by $o(1-h_t(\infty)) = o(t^{1/2})$. We conclude by using the asymptotic of $1-h_t(\infty)$ from Lemma \ref{lem:phit-taylor-expansion}.
nodes.statement_short: Both terms are o(t^{1/2}); use the asymptotic of 1-h_t(inf).

nodes.name: Equation (56)
nodes.statement: h(r) - (1- h_t(\infty)) \leq h_t(r) \leq h(r) .
nodes.label: eq:easy-bounds-htr

nodes.name: Function w_t
nodes.statement: Define $w_t(r) = \frac{h_t(\infty)}{h_t(r)}-1$; this is well-defined for every $r\geq 0$ since $h_t(0)>0$, and it decreases to $0$ as $r\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Equation (57)
nodes.statement: w_t(r) = \frac{h_t(\infty)}{h_t(r)}-1 \geq \frac{h_t(\infty)}{h(r)}-1 = h_t(\infty) w(r) - (1-h_t(\infty))
nodes.label: eq:2lower-bound-wt

nodes.name: Equation (58)
nodes.statement: w_t(r) \leq \frac{h_t(\infty)}{h(r) -(1- h_t(\infty))}-1 = \frac{1-h(r)}{h(r)-(1-h_t(\infty))} \leq \frac{w(r)}{h(r) - (1-h_t(\infty))} .
nodes.label: eq:2upper-bound-wt

nodes.name: Critical time scale t(r, alpha)
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha\geq 0$ and $r>0$ define \begin{equation} t(r, \alpha) := \frac{\alpha^2}{2\sigma^2} \left( \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2 r^2} \right)^2 \ . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (59)
