nodes.statement: t(r, \alpha) := \frac{\alpha^2}{2\sigma^2} \left( \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2 r^2} \right)^2 \ .
nodes.label: eq:def-t-r-alpha

nodes.name: Equation (60)
nodes.statement: \liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2 w_{t(r,\alpha)}(r) \geq -\alpha\frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} + \liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2 w(r) \geq (1-\alpha) \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} .
nodes.label: eq:2bound-w-liminf-1-alpha

nodes.name: Equation (61)
nodes.statement: w_t(r) = \frac{h_t(\infty)}{h_t(r)} - 1 \geq \frac{h_t(\infty)}{h_s(r)}-1 = \frac{h_t(\infty)}{h_s(\infty)} w_s(r) + \frac{h_t(\infty)}{h_s(\infty)} - 1
nodes.label: eq:2lower-bound-wt-strong

nodes.name: Equation (62)
nodes.statement: w_t(r) \leq \frac{h_t(\infty)}{h_s(r) + h_t(\infty) - h_s(\infty)}-1 = \frac{h_s(\infty)-h_s(r)}{h_s(r) + h_t(\infty) - h_s(\infty)} = \frac{1-\frac{h_s(r)}{h_s(\infty)}}{\frac{h_s(r)}{h_s(\infty)} + \frac{h_t(\infty)}{h_s(\infty)} - 1} \\ = \frac{w_s(r)}{-w_s(r) + \frac{h_t(\infty)}{h_s(\infty)}(1+w_s(r))} = \frac{w_s(r)}{\frac{h_t(\infty)}{h_s(\infty)} + w_s(r)\left(\frac{h_t(\infty)}{h_s(\infty)}-1\right)} .
nodes.label: eq:2upper-bound-wt-strong

nodes.name: Remark on regimes of t and r
nodes.statement: A significant complexity is introduced by the need to control the asymptotic as $r\to\infty$ for every fixed $t$, as well as for $t$ and $r\to\infty$ jointly. Here is what we expect: as $t\to 0$ and $r\to\infty$, if $t = o(r^{-4})$ then $w_t(r) \sim w(r)$; on the other hand if $r = o(t^{-1/4})$ then $w_t(r) = o(w(r)) = o(r^{-2})$. Only in the regime where $t r^4$ is of order $1$, for example when $t=t(r,\alpha)$, will we see a limit in $(0,6\eta^2/\sigma^2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Only when t r^4 is of order 1 does w_t(r)/w(r) have a non-trivial limit.

nodes.name: Uniform continuity of r^2 w_{t(r,alpha)}(r) in alpha
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha>0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $r_\varepsilon$ and $f_\varepsilon(r) \to 6 \eta^2 \varepsilon / \sigma^2$ as $r\to\infty$ such that for every $r\geq r_\varepsilon$, \[ \sup_{\gamma, \beta \in [0,\alpha]: |\beta-\gamma|\leq \varepsilon} r^2 \left| w_{t(r,\beta)}(r) - w_{t(r,\gamma)}(r) \right| \leq f_\varepsilon(r) . \]
conclusions: there exists $r_\varepsilon$ and $f_\varepsilon(r) \to 6 \eta^2 \varepsilon / \sigma^2$ as $r\to\infty$ such that for every $r\geq r_\varepsilon$
nodes.label: lem:2uniform-continuity-u

nodes.name: Proof of uniform continuity in alpha
nodes.statement: Since $1-h_t(\infty) \sim_{t\to 0} \sqrt{\frac{2t}{\sigma^2}}$, which implies $1-h_{t(r,\alpha)}(\infty) \sim_{r\to\infty} \alpha \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2 r^2}$, and since $h_{t(r,\alpha)}(\infty)$ is decreasing in $\alpha$, we have that for every $\varepsilon, \varepsilon'>0$ and $\alpha>0$, for every $0\leq \beta \leq \alpha$ \[ \limsup_{r\to\infty} r^2\left(1 - \frac{h_{t(r,\beta+\varepsilon+\varepsilon')}(\infty)}{h_{t(r,\beta)}(\infty)} \right) \leq \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} (\varepsilon+\varepsilon') . \] Taking the supremum over the finitely many $\beta \in [0,\alpha] \cap \varepsilon' \Z$ and by monotonicity of $\beta \mapsto h_{t(r,\beta)}(\infty)$, then taking $\varepsilon'\to 0$, we find $g_\varepsilon(r) \to 6\eta^2/\sigma^2$ as $r\to\infty$ such that \begin{equation*} \sup_{0\leq \beta \leq \alpha} r^2\left(1 - \frac{h_{t(r,\beta+\varepsilon)}(\infty)}{h_{t(r,\beta)}(\infty)} \right) \leq \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) . \end{equation*} Fix $\alpha>0$. By \eqref{eq:2upper-bound-wt}, there exists $f_1(x)$ (that depends on $\alpha$) that converge to $6\eta^2/\sigma^2$ as $x\to\infty$ with $f_1(x)\geq 6\eta^2/\sigma^2$ such that $r^2 w_{t(r,\beta)}(r) \leq \frac{6 \eta^2}{\sigma^2} f_1(r) $ for every $\beta \in [0,\alpha]$. By \eqref{eq:2lower-bound-wt-strong}, for every $\beta \in [0,\alpha]$ \begin{align*} r^2 w_{t(r,\beta+\varepsilon)}(r) &\geq \left( 1 - \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r)\right) r^2 w_{t(r,\beta)}(r) - \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \\ &\geq r^2 w_{t(r,\beta)}(r) - \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left(1+ \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2}\right) . \end{align*} On the other hand, by \eqref{eq:2upper-bound-wt-strong}, taking $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, then $r$ large enough that $r^{-2} \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left( 1 + \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2} \right) \leq 1/2$, using that $|(1-x)^{-1} - 1| \leq 2x$ for $|x|\leq 1/2$, \begin{align*} w_{t(r,\beta+\varepsilon)}(r) &\leq w_{t(r,\beta)}(r) \left( 1 - r^{-2} \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left( 1 + \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2} \right) \right)^{-1} \\ &\leq w_{t(r,\beta)}(r) + 2 w_{t(r,\beta)} r^{-2} \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left( 1 + \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2} \right) . \end{align*} The Lemma follows by taking \[ f_\varepsilon(r) = \max \left( 2f_1(r) r^{-2} \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left( 1 + \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2} \right) , \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left(1+ \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2}\right) \right) , \] and we can check that indeed $f_\varepsilon(r) \to 6\eta^2 \varepsilon/\sigma^2$ as $r\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare h_{t(r,beta)}(inf) across beta, then use the strengthened lower and upper bounds on w_t.

nodes.name: Uniform control of the ratio h_{t(r,beta+eps)}(inf)/h_{t(r,b
nodes.statement: Since $1-h_t(\infty) \sim_{t\to 0} \sqrt{\frac{2t}{\sigma^2}}$, which implies $1-h_{t(r,\alpha)}(\infty) \sim_{r\to\infty} \alpha \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2 r^2}$, and since $h_{t(r,\alpha)}(\infty)$ is decreasing in $\alpha$, we have that for every $\varepsilon, \varepsilon'>0$ and $\alpha>0$, for every $0\leq \beta \leq \alpha$ \[ \limsup_{r\to\infty} r^2\left(1 - \frac{h_{t(r,\beta+\varepsilon+\varepsilon')}(\infty)}{h_{t(r,\beta)}(\infty)} \right) \leq \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} (\varepsilon+\varepsilon') . \] Taking the supremum over the finitely many $\beta \in [0,\alpha] \cap \varepsilon' \Z$ and by monotonicity of $\beta \mapsto h_{t(r,\beta)}(\infty)$, then taking $\varepsilon'\to 0$, we find $g_\varepsilon(r) \to 6\eta^2/\sigma^2$ as $r\to\infty$ such that \begin{equation*} \sup_{0\leq \beta \leq \alpha} r^2\left(1 - \frac{h_{t(r,\beta+\varepsilon)}(\infty)}{h_{t(r,\beta)}(\infty)} \right) \leq \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Uniform control of the ratio h_{t(r,beta+eps)}(inf)/h_{t(r,beta)}(inf).

nodes.name: Upper bound r^2 w_{t(r,beta)}(r) by f_1(r).
nodes.statement: Fix $\alpha>0$. By \eqref{eq:2upper-bound-wt}, there exists $f_1(x)$ (that depends on $\alpha$) that converge to $6\eta^2/\sigma^2$ as $x\to\infty$ with $f_1(x)\geq 6\eta^2/\sigma^2$ such that $r^2 w_{t(r,\beta)}(r) \leq \frac{6 \eta^2}{\sigma^2} f_1(r) $ for every $\beta \in [0,\alpha]$.
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound r^2 w_{t(r,beta)}(r) by f_1(r).

nodes.name: Lower bound on the increment.
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:2lower-bound-wt-strong}, for every $\beta \in [0,\alpha]$ \begin{align*} r^2 w_{t(r,\beta+\varepsilon)}(r) &\geq \left( 1 - \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r)\right) r^2 w_{t(r,\beta)}(r) - \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \\ &\geq r^2 w_{t(r,\beta)}(r) - \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left(1+ \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2}\right) . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound on the increment.

nodes.name: Upper bound on the increment.
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by \eqref{eq:2upper-bound-wt-strong}, taking $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, then $r$ large enough that $r^{-2} \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left( 1 + \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2} \right) \leq 1/2$, using that $|(1-x)^{-1} - 1| \leq 2x$ for $|x|\leq 1/2$, \begin{align*} w_{t(r,\beta+\varepsilon)}(r) &\leq w_{t(r,\beta)}(r) \left( 1 - r^{-2} \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left( 1 + \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2} \right) \right)^{-1} \\ &\leq w_{t(r,\beta)}(r) + 2 w_{t(r,\beta)} r^{-2} \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left( 1 + \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2} \right) . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound on the increment.

nodes.name: Define f_eps and check its limit.
nodes.statement: The Lemma follows by taking \[ f_\varepsilon(r) = \max \left( 2f_1(r) r^{-2} \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left( 1 + \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2} \right) , \varepsilon g_\varepsilon(r) \left(1+ \frac{f_1(r)}{r^2}\right) \right) , \] and we can check that indeed $f_\varepsilon(r) \to 6\eta^2 \varepsilon/\sigma^2$ as $r\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Define f_eps and check its limit.

nodes.name: Tilted expectations E^{(t)}
nodes.statement: Define a family $(\E^{(t)})_{t\geq 0}$ of expectations on the same probability space as $\E$ such that $(k_u, \chi_u, D_u, \Lambda^{(u)}, (X^{(u)}_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi_u(\R)})_{u\in \mathcal U}$ are i.i.d. with the distribution of $(k, \chi, D, \Lambda, (X_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)})$ such that for every nonnegative and measurable $f$ \begin{equation} \E^{(t)}\left[ f\left( k, \chi, D, \Lambda, (X_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)} \right) \right] \\ = \E\left[ \e^{-tD} h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1} f\left( k, \chi, D, \Lambda, (X_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)} \right) \right] . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (63)
nodes.statement: \E^{(t)}\left[ f\left( k, \chi, D, \Lambda, (X_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)} \right) \right] \\ = \E\left[ \e^{-tD} h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1} f\left( k, \chi, D, \Lambda, (X_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)} \right) \right] .

nodes.name: Tilted BRW law
nodes.statement: We can then check that for every nonnegative and measurable $f$ \begin{equation} \E^{(t)}\left[ f\left( T, (X_v)_{v\in T}, (D_v)_{v\in T}, (\Lambda_v)_{v\in T} \right) \right] = \frac{\E\left[ \e^{-t\sum_{v\in T} D_v} f\left( T, (X_v)_{v\in T}, (D_v)_{v\in T}, (\Lambda_v)_{v\in T} \right) \right]}{\E\left[ \e^{-t\sum_{v\in T} D_v} \right]} \ , \end{equation} noting that $h_t(\infty) = \E[ \e^{-t\sum_{v\in T} D_v} ]$.

nodes.name: Equation (64)
nodes.statement: \E^{(t)}\left[ f\left( T, (X_v)_{v\in T}, (D_v)_{v\in T}, (\Lambda_v)_{v\in T} \right) \right] = \frac{\E\left[ \e^{-t\sum_{v\in T} D_v} f\left( T, (X_v)_{v\in T}, (D_v)_{v\in T}, (\Lambda_v)_{v\in T} \right) \right]}{\E\left[ \e^{-t\sum_{v\in T} D_v} \right]} \ ,

nodes.name: The tilted BRW is subcritical
nodes.statement: Differentiating $\Phi_t$ gives \begin{equation} \E^{(t)}\left[ \chi(\R) \right] = \Phi_t'(h_t(\infty)) \leq 1 \end{equation} with a strict inequality when $t>0$. In other words, the \textsc{brw}\xspace becomes subcritical under $\E^{(t)}$.

nodes.name: Equation (65)
nodes.statement: \E^{(t)}\left[ \chi(\R) \right] = \Phi_t'(h_t(\infty)) \leq 1
nodes.label: eq:2expectation-chi-vol

nodes.name: Asymptotic of the tilted mean offspring
nodes.statement: We can be more precise: by Lemma \ref{lem:speed-cv-expectation-Et} \begin{equation} 1- \E^{(t)}[ \chi(\R) ] \sim \sqrt{2t\sigma^2} . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (66)
nodes.statement: 1- \E^{(t)}[ \chi(\R) ] \sim \sqrt{2t\sigma^2} .
nodes.label: eq:asymptotic-expectation-chi-vol

nodes.name: Continuity of tilted expectations at t = 0
nodes.statement: Because $\e^{-tD} h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1} \leq h_t(\infty)^{-1}$ a.s. we have by the dominated convergence theorem $\E^{(t)}[W] \to \E[W]$ as $t\to 0$ as soon as $W$ is integrable, in particular \begin{equation} \E^{(t)}\left[ \chi(\R)(\chi(\R)-1) \right] \ulim t 0 \sigma^2 , \end{equation} and there exists $t_0>0$ such that for every $t\in[0,t_0]$ and every $W\geq 0$ integrable \begin{equation} \E^{(t)}[W] \leq 2\E[W] . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (67)
nodes.statement: \E^{(t)}\left[ \chi(\R)(\chi(\R)-1) \right] \ulim t 0 \sigma^2 ,
nodes.label: eq:2variance-chi-vol

nodes.name: Normalized function tilde h_t and its convolution equation
nodes.statement: We can rewrite \eqref{eq:2convolution-equation-1} as an equation on \[ \tilde h_t(r) := \P^{(t)}\left( \sup_n \sup G_n \leq r \right) = \frac{h_t(r)}{h_t(\infty)} = \frac{1}{1+w_t(r)} \ , \] namely \begin{equation} \tilde{h}_t(r) = \E^{(t)}\left[ \prod_{i=1}^{\chi(\R)} \tilde h_t(r-X_i) \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \right] = \E^{(t)}\left[ \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \exp\left( \int \ln\tilde h_t(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right) \right] . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (69)
nodes.statement: \tilde{h}_t(r) = \E^{(t)}\left[ \prod_{i=1}^{\chi(\R)} \tilde h_t(r-X_i) \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \right] = \E^{(t)}\left[ \ind{\Lambda\leq r} \exp\left( \int \ln\tilde h_t(r-x) \d\chi(x) \right) \right] .
nodes.label: eq:2convolution-equation-vol

nodes.name: Size-biased displacement Z_t
nodes.statement: For every $t\geq 0$, there exists a random variable $Z_t$ such that for every positive and measurable $f$ \begin{equation} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] \cdot \E[f(Z_t)] = \E^{(t)}\left[ \int f(x) \d\chi(x) \right] . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (70)
nodes.statement: \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] \cdot \E[f(Z_t)] = \E^{(t)}\left[ \int f(x) \d\chi(x) \right] .
nodes.label: eq:2def-Zt

nodes.name: Likelihood ratio V_t
nodes.statement: For every $t\geq 0$ let \[ V_t := \frac{\e^{-tD} h_t(\infty)^{\chi(\R)-1}}{\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]} . \] Clearly $\E[V_t \chi(\R)]=1$.

nodes.name: Coupling variables U and J_t
nodes.statement: Let $U$ be uniform on $[0,1]$ and independent from the reproduction scheme\xspace, in particular of $(D,\chi)$, and for every $t\geq 0$ let $J_t$ be a random variable such that for every nonnegative and measurable $f$ \[ \E[f(Z, J_t)] = \E\left[ \int f\left( x, \ind{U < V_t}\right) \d\chi(x) \right] . \]

nodes.name: Coupled Z_t
nodes.statement: Finally, let $\tilde{Z_t}$ independent from $(Z, J_t)$ such that for every nonnegative and measurable $f$ \[ \E[f(\tilde Z_t)] = \E\left[ \frac{(V_t-1) \ind{V_t\geq 1}}{\E[(V_t-1) \ind{V_t\geq 1} \chi(\R)]} \int f(x) \d\chi(x) \right] . \] Finally, define \begin{equation} Z_t := Z \ind{J_t=1} + \tilde Z_t \ind{J_t=0} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (71)
nodes.statement: Z_t := Z \ind{J_t=1} + \tilde Z_t \ind{J_t=0}
nodes.label: eq:def-Zt-coupling

nodes.name: Explicit coupling of Z_t and Z
nodes.statement: The random variables $(Z_t)_{t\geq 0}$ from \eqref{eq:def-Zt-coupling} satisfy \eqref{eq:2def-Zt}, and in addition \begin{equation} \limsup_{t\to 0} \ (2\sigma^2 t)^{-1/2} \P(Z_t \neq Z) \leq 1 . \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \E[(Z_t - Z_0)^2] \ulim t 0 0 . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The coupled Z_t has the tilted size-biased law, differs from Z with probability O(sqrt t), and converges to Z in L^2.
nodes.label: lem:coupling-explicit

nodes.name: Equation (72)
nodes.statement: \limsup_{t\to 0} \ (2\sigma^2 t)^{-1/2} \P(Z_t \neq Z) \leq 1 .

nodes.name: Proof of the coupling lemma
nodes.statement: Clearly, outside of the event $J_t=0$ we have $Z_t = Z$. This event has probability \begin{equation} \P(J_t=0) = \E[\chi(\R) \ind{U>V_t}] = \E[\chi(\R) (1-V_t)\ind{V_t<1}] = \E[\chi(\R)\ind{V_t<1}] - \E[\chi(\R) V_t \ind{V_t<1}] . \end{equation} Using that $\E[\chi(\R)] = \E[V_t\chi(\R)] = 1$, we can rewrite this as \[ \P(J_t=0) = \E[\chi(\R) V_t \ind{V_t\geq 1}] - \E[\chi(R) \ind{V_t\geq 1}] = \E\left[ (V_t-1) \ind{V_t\geq 1} \chi(\R) \right] . \] Then \begin{align*} \E[f(Z_t)] &= \E[\ind{J_t=1} f(Z)] + \E[\ind{J_t=0} f(\tilde Z_t)] \\ &= \E\left[ \ind{U<V_t} \int f(x)\d\chi(x) \right] + \P(J_t=0) \E\left[ f(\tilde Z_t) \right] \\ &= \E\left[ \min(1, V_t) \int f(x)\d\chi(x) \right] + \E\left[ (V_t-1) \ind{V_t\geq 1} \int f(x)\d\chi(x) \right] \\ &= \E\left[V_t \int f(x) \d\chi(x) \right] , \end{align*} thus proving \eqref{eq:2def-Zt}. On the other hand, by Lemma \ref{lem:speed-cv-expectation-Et} and from $\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]\to 1$ as $t\to 0$ \[ \E[\chi(\R)\ind{V_t<1}] - \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] \E[\chi(\R) V_t \ind{V_t<1}] = \sqrt{\frac{2t}{\sigma^2}} \E[(\chi(\R)-1)\chi(\R) \ind{V_t<1}] + o(t^{1/2}) . \] Plugging this into \eqref{eq:PJt0}, \begin{equation*} \P(Z_t \neq Z) \leq \P(J_t =0) \leq \E[\chi(\R)\ind{V_t<1}] - \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]\E[\chi(\R) V_t \ind{V_t<1}] \end{equation*} is such that \[ \limsup_{t\to 0} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2t \sigma^2}} \P(Z_t \neq Z) \leq \limsup_{t\to 0} \frac{1}{\sigma^2} \E[(\chi(\R)-1)\chi(\R) \ind{V_t<1}] \leq 1 . \] Finally, from $(a-b)^2 \leq 2a^2 + 2b^2$ \begin{align*} \E[ (Z_t-Z)^2] &= \E\left[ \ind{J_t=0} (\tilde Z_t-Z)^2 \right] \\ &\leq 2\P(Z_t=0) \E\left[ (\tilde Z_t)^2 \right] + 2\E[\ind{J_t=0} Z^2] \\ &= 2\E\left[ (V_t-1) \ind{V_t\geq 1} \int x^2 \d\chi(x) \right] + 2\E[\ind{J_t=0} Z^2] \end{align*} and both terms converge to $0$ as $t\to 0$ by dominated convergence.
nodes.statement_short: Compute P(J_t=0) and the law of Z_t directly; the speed lemma bounds P(Z_t != Z); dominated convergence for L^2.

nodes.name: Probability of J_t = 0.
nodes.statement: Clearly, outside of the event $J_t=0$ we have $Z_t = Z$. This event has probability \begin{equation} \P(J_t=0) = \E[\chi(\R) \ind{U>V_t}] = \E[\chi(\R) (1-V_t)\ind{V_t<1}] = \E[\chi(\R)\ind{V_t<1}] - \E[\chi(\R) V_t \ind{V_t<1}] . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Probability of J_t = 0.

nodes.name: Equation (74)
nodes.statement: \P(J_t=0) = \E[\chi(\R) \ind{U>V_t}] = \E[\chi(\R) (1-V_t)\ind{V_t<1}] = \E[\chi(\R)\ind{V_t<1}] - \E[\chi(\R) V_t \ind{V_t<1}] .
nodes.label: eq:PJt0

nodes.name: Verify the law of Z_t.
nodes.statement: Using that $\E[\chi(\R)] = \E[V_t\chi(\R)] = 1$, we can rewrite this as \[ \P(J_t=0) = \E[\chi(\R) V_t \ind{V_t\geq 1}] - \E[\chi(R) \ind{V_t\geq 1}] = \E\left[ (V_t-1) \ind{V_t\geq 1} \chi(\R) \right] . \] Then \begin{align*} \E[f(Z_t)] &= \E[\ind{J_t=1} f(Z)] + \E[\ind{J_t=0} f(\tilde Z_t)] \\ &= \E\left[ \ind{U<V_t} \int f(x)\d\chi(x) \right] + \P(J_t=0) \E\left[ f(\tilde Z_t) \right] \\ &= \E\left[ \min(1, V_t) \int f(x)\d\chi(x) \right] + \E\left[ (V_t-1) \ind{V_t\geq 1} \int f(x)\d\chi(x) \right] \\ &= \E\left[V_t \int f(x) \d\chi(x) \right] , \end{align*} thus proving \eqref{eq:2def-Zt}.
nodes.statement_short: Verify the law of Z_t.

nodes.name: Bound P(Z_t != Z).
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by Lemma \ref{lem:speed-cv-expectation-Et} and from $\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]\to 1$ as $t\to 0$ \[ \E[\chi(\R)\ind{V_t<1}] - \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] \E[\chi(\R) V_t \ind{V_t<1}] = \sqrt{\frac{2t}{\sigma^2}} \E[(\chi(\R)-1)\chi(\R) \ind{V_t<1}] + o(t^{1/2}) . \] Plugging this into \eqref{eq:PJt0}, \begin{equation*} \P(Z_t \neq Z) \leq \P(J_t =0) \leq \E[\chi(\R)\ind{V_t<1}] - \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]\E[\chi(\R) V_t \ind{V_t<1}] \end{equation*} is such that \[ \limsup_{t\to 0} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2t \sigma^2}} \P(Z_t \neq Z) \leq \limsup_{t\to 0} \frac{1}{\sigma^2} \E[(\chi(\R)-1)\chi(\R) \ind{V_t<1}] \leq 1 . \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound P(Z_t != Z).

nodes.name: L^2 convergence by dominated convergence.
nodes.statement: Finally, from $(a-b)^2 \leq 2a^2 + 2b^2$ \begin{align*} \E[ (Z_t-Z)^2] &= \E\left[ \ind{J_t=0} (\tilde Z_t-Z)^2 \right] \\ &\leq 2\P(Z_t=0) \E\left[ (\tilde Z_t)^2 \right] + 2\E[\ind{J_t=0} Z^2] \\ &= 2\E\left[ (V_t-1) \ind{V_t\geq 1} \int x^2 \d\chi(x) \right] + 2\E[\ind{J_t=0} Z^2] \end{align*} and both terms converge to $0$ as $t\to 0$ by dominated convergence.
nodes.statement_short: L^2 convergence by dominated convergence.

nodes.name: Coupled random walks U_n^t
nodes.statement: Let $(Z_n^{t})_{n\geq 1, t\geq 0}$ be i.i.d. copies of $(Z_t)_{t\geq 0}$, and define for every $t\geq 0$ and every $n\geq 0$ \begin{equation} U_n^t = Z_1^t + \dots + Z_n^t \end{equation} where $U_0^t = 0$.

nodes.name: Equation (75)
nodes.statement: U_n^t = Z_1^t + \dots + Z_n^t
nodes.label: eq:def-Unt

nodes.name: Many-to-one formula (tilted)
nodes.statement: The many-to-one formula takes the following form: for every measurable and bounded $g$, for every $n$ \begin{equation} \E^{(t)}\left[\int g \d G_n\right] = \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^n \cdot \E[g(U_n^t)] . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (76)
nodes.statement: \E^{(t)}\left[\int g \d G_n\right] = \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^n \cdot \E[g(U_n^t)] .
nodes.label: eq:many-to-one-chiR

nodes.name: Positivity of c(alpha)
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha\geq 0$, \[ 0 < c(\alpha) := \liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2 \inf_{t\in[0,t(r,\alpha)]} w_t(r) \leq \limsup_{r\to\infty} r^2 \sup_{t\in[0,t(r,\alpha)]} w_t(r) \leq \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} . \]
nodes.label: lem:positivity-c-alpha

nodes.name: Proof of positivity of c(alpha)
nodes.statement: The upper bound follows from \eqref{eq:2upper-bound-wt}. We prove the lower bound by the second moment method. By the many-to-one formula \eqref{eq:many-to-one-chiR}, \[ \E^{(t)}[G_n([r, \infty))] = \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^n \P(U^t_n \geq r) . \] The second moment is \begin{align*} \E^{(t)}[G_n(\R)^2] &= \E^{(t)}\left[ \left(\sum_{x\in G_{n-1}} \chi_x(\R)\right)^2\right] \\ &= \E^{(t)}[G_{n-1}(\R)] \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)^2] + \E^{(t)}[G_{n-1}(\R)(G_{n-1}(\R)-1)] \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^2 \\ &= \E^{(t)}[G_{n-1}(\R)^2] \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^2 + \E^{(t)}[G_{n-1}(\R)] \mathrm{Var}^{(t)}(\chi(\R)) \end{align*} so that \begin{align} \E^{(t)}[G_n(\R)^2] &\leq \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{2n} + n\mathrm{Var}^{(t)}(\chi(\R)) \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{n-1} \\ &\nonumber \leq \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{n-1}\left(1+n\mathrm{Var}^{(t)}(\chi(\R))\right) \\ &\nonumber \leq 2n\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{n}\sigma^2 \end{align} as soon as $t, n$ and $r$ are large enough. Taking $n = r^2/\eta^2$, by the Paley--Zygmund inequality we get \begin{equation*} \frac{r^2 w_t(r)}{1+w_t(r)} = r^2 \P^{(t)}(G_{r^2}([r,\infty))>0) \geq \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{r^2} \frac{\eta^2 \P(U_{r^2}^t \geq r)^2}{2\sigma^2} . \end{equation*} Using \eqref{eq:coupling-first-step} we can check that if we take $t_0>0$ small enough then $\liminf_{r\to\infty} \inf_{t\in [0,t_0]} \P(U_{r^2/\eta^2}^t \geq r) > \P(N\geq 2)$, where $N\sim \NN(0,1)$. Using that $\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] = 1 - \sqrt{2t\sigma^2} + o(t) \geq \exp( - 2\sqrt{t\sigma^2})$ for every $t\in [0,t_0]$ (taking $t_0$ smaller if needed), we finally find \[ \liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2 \inf_{t\in [0, t(r,\alpha)]} w_t(r) \geq \frac{\P(N\geq 2)^2}{2}\frac{\eta^2}{\sigma^2} \exp\left(-\alpha\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{\sigma^2} \right) . \]
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound from the easy bounds; lower bound by the second moment method under the tilted law and the coupling.

nodes.name: Upper bound is immediate; lower bound by second moment metho
nodes.statement: The upper bound follows from \eqref{eq:2upper-bound-wt}. We prove the lower bound by the second moment method.
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound is immediate; lower bound by second moment method.

nodes.name: First moment via many-to-one.
nodes.statement: By the many-to-one formula \eqref{eq:many-to-one-chiR}, \[ \E^{(t)}[G_n([r, \infty))] = \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^n \P(U^t_n \geq r) . \]
nodes.statement_short: First moment via many-to-one.

nodes.name: Recursive second-moment bound.
nodes.statement: The second moment is \begin{align*} \E^{(t)}[G_n(\R)^2] &= \E^{(t)}\left[ \left(\sum_{x\in G_{n-1}} \chi_x(\R)\right)^2\right] \\ &= \E^{(t)}[G_{n-1}(\R)] \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)^2] + \E^{(t)}[G_{n-1}(\R)(G_{n-1}(\R)-1)] \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^2 \\ &= \E^{(t)}[G_{n-1}(\R)^2] \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^2 + \E^{(t)}[G_{n-1}(\R)] \mathrm{Var}^{(t)}(\chi(\R)) \end{align*} so that \begin{align} \E^{(t)}[G_n(\R)^2] &\leq \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{2n} + n\mathrm{Var}^{(t)}(\chi(\R)) \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{n-1} \\ &\nonumber \leq \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{n-1}\left(1+n\mathrm{Var}^{(t)}(\chi(\R))\right) \\ &\nonumber \leq 2n\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{n}\sigma^2 \end{align} as soon as $t, n$ and $r$ are large enough.
nodes.statement_short: Recursive second-moment bound.

nodes.name: Equation (77)
nodes.statement: \E^{(t)}[G_n(\R)^2] &\leq \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{2n} + n\mathrm{Var}^{(t)}(\chi(\R)) \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{n-1} \\ &\nonumber \leq \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{n-1}\left(1+n\mathrm{Var}^{(t)}(\chi(\R))\right) \\ &\nonumber \leq 2n\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{n}\sigma^2
nodes.label: eq:second-moment-Gr2

nodes.name: Paley–Zygmund.
nodes.statement: Taking $n = r^2/\eta^2$, by the Paley--Zygmund inequality we get \begin{equation*} \frac{r^2 w_t(r)}{1+w_t(r)} = r^2 \P^{(t)}(G_{r^2}([r,\infty))>0) \geq \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{r^2} \frac{\eta^2 \P(U_{r^2}^t \geq r)^2}{2\sigma^2} . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Paley–Zygmund.

nodes.name: Coupling and the asymptotic of the tilted mean give the expl
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{eq:coupling-first-step} we can check that if we take $t_0>0$ small enough then $\liminf_{r\to\infty} \inf_{t\in [0,t_0]} \P(U_{r^2/\eta^2}^t \geq r) > \P(N\geq 2)$, where $N\sim \NN(0,1)$. Using that $\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] = 1 - \sqrt{2t\sigma^2} + o(t) \geq \exp( - 2\sqrt{t\sigma^2})$ for every $t\in [0,t_0]$ (taking $t_0$ smaller if needed), we finally find \[ \liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2 \inf_{t\in [0, t(r,\alpha)]} w_t(r) \geq \frac{\P(N\geq 2)^2}{2}\frac{\eta^2}{\sigma^2} \exp\left(-\alpha\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{\sigma^2} \right) . \]
nodes.statement_short: Coupling and the asymptotic of the tilted mean give the explicit lower bound.

nodes.name: Uniform bounds on x^2 w_t(x)
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha>0$ and $b \in (0,1)$, \[ c(\alpha) \leq \liminf_{r\to\infty} \inf_{br \leq x \leq r} x^2 w_{t(r,\alpha)}(x) \leq \limsup_{r\to\infty} \sup_{br \leq x \leq r} x^2 w_{t(r,\alpha)}(x) \leq \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} . \] More generally, \[ c(\alpha) \leq \liminf_{r\to\infty} \inf_{s\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]} \inf_{br \leq x \leq r} x^2 w_{s}(x) \leq \limsup_{r\to\infty} \sup_{s\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]} \sup_{br \leq x \leq r} x^2 w_{s}(x) \leq \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} . \]
nodes.label: cor:2uniform-limit-r2wt

nodes.name: Proof of the uniform bounds
nodes.statement: For the second part, we use the correspondence $t(r,\alpha) = t(br, b^2 \alpha)$. Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and assume that $r_\bullet$ is such that for every $r\geq r_\bullet$ \[ (1-\varepsilon)c(\alpha) \leq \inf_{0\leq t \leq t(r,\alpha)} r^2 w_t(r) \leq \sup_{0\leq t \leq t(r,\alpha)} r^2 w_t(r) \leq (1+\varepsilon) \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} . \] Then for every $r\geq r_\bullet/b$ and every $q \in [b,1]$, because $q^2 \alpha \leq \alpha$, \[ (1-\varepsilon)c(\alpha) \leq (qr)^2 w_{t(qr, q^2 \alpha)}(qr) = (qr)^2 w_{t(r, \alpha)}(qr) \leq (1+\varepsilon) \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} . \] This concludes the proof of the first equation. The second follows from the first and \eqref{eq:2upper-bound-wt-strong} (for the lower bound) and \eqref{eq:2upper-bound-wt} (for the upper bound).
nodes.statement_short: Scaling identity t(r,alpha) = t(br, b^2 alpha) transfers the bounds of the positivity lemma.

nodes.name: Fix eps and r_bullet from the positivity lemma.
nodes.statement: For the second part, we use the correspondence $t(r,\alpha) = t(br, b^2 \alpha)$. Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and assume that $r_\bullet$ is such that for every $r\geq r_\bullet$ \[ (1-\varepsilon)c(\alpha) \leq \inf_{0\leq t \leq t(r,\alpha)} r^2 w_t(r) \leq \sup_{0\leq t \leq t(r,\alpha)} r^2 w_t(r) \leq (1+\varepsilon) \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} . \]
nodes.statement_short: Fix eps and r_bullet from the positivity lemma.

nodes.name: Apply at qr with q in [b,1].
nodes.statement: Then for every $r\geq r_\bullet/b$ and every $q \in [b,1]$, because $q^2 \alpha \leq \alpha$, \[ (1-\varepsilon)c(\alpha) \leq (qr)^2 w_{t(qr, q^2 \alpha)}(qr) = (qr)^2 w_{t(r, \alpha)}(qr) \leq (1+\varepsilon) \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} . \] This concludes the proof of the first equation.
nodes.statement_short: Apply at qr with q in [b,1].

nodes.name: The second statement follows from the monotonicity bounds.
nodes.statement: The second follows from the first and \eqref{eq:2upper-bound-wt-strong} (for the lower bound) and \eqref{eq:2upper-bound-wt} (for the upper bound).
nodes.statement_short: The second statement follows from the monotonicity bounds.

nodes.name: Continuity of the tail w_t (lower bound)
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha\geq 0$, define \[ D(\alpha) = \frac{4}{\eta\sqrt{\pi}} \sqrt{\sigma^2 + \frac{\alpha}{c(\alpha)}} \ . \] For every $y\geq 0$ \begin{equation} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w_{t(r, \alpha)}\left(r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_{t(r, \alpha)}(r)}}\right)}{w_{t(r, \alpha)}(r)} \geq 1 - y D(\alpha) . \end{equation}
nodes.label: lem:2continuity-w-broad-volume

nodes.name: Equation (78)
nodes.statement: \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w_{t(r, \alpha)}\left(r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_{t(r, \alpha)}(r)}}\right)}{w_{t(r, \alpha)}(r)} \geq 1 - y D(\alpha) .
nodes.label: eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right

nodes.name: Proof of the continuity lower bound for w_t
nodes.statement:
In this proof, for conciseness we write $t = t(r,\alpha)$. We follow the proof of Lemma ef{lem:continuity-w-broad}, with adaptations. Let $r_y =  rac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}$. Assume that $r$ is large enough that $u_t(r) \geq c(\alpha)/2$. By \eqref{eq:2convolution-equation-vol}, using that $	ilde h_t(x) \leq 	ilde h_t(r)$ when $x\leq r$, \[ 	ilde h_t(r+r_y) \leq \E^{(t)}\left[ \exp\left( \ln 	ilde h_t(r) G_n([r_y,\infty)) + \int_{(-\infty,r_y]} \ln	ilde h_t(r+r_y-x) \d G_n(x) ight) ight] . \] Write $X$ for the expression inside the exponential. As in Lemma ef{lem:continuity-w-broad}, we bound $\E[\e^{X}] \leq \E[1 + X +  rac{X^2}{2}]$, and do so by bounding the first and second moments of $X$ under $\E^{(t)}$: by the many-to-one formula \eqref{eq:many-to-one-chiR}  egin{align} 
onumber & \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n}  rac{-\E^{(t)}[X]}{w_t(r)} \ 
onumber &= \E\left[  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r))}{w_t(r)} \ind{U_n^t \geq r_y} +  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r+r_y-U_n^t))}{w_t(r)}\ind{U_n^t < r_y} ight] \ 
onumber &\geq  rac{\ln(1+w_r(t))}{w_t(r)}\P(U_n^t \geq r_y) + \E\left[  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r+r_y-U_n^t))}{w_t(r)} \ind{U_n^t<r_y , |U_n^t-U_n^0|\leq \delta\sqrt{n}} ight]\ 
onumber &\geq  rac{\ln(1+w_r(t))}{w_t(r)}\P(U_n^0 \geq r_y-\delta\sqrt{n}) \ 
onumber &\qquad - \underset{(a)}{\underbrace{\P\left(|U_n^t - U_n^0|>\delta\sqrt{n}ight)}} - \underset{(b)}{\underbrace{\P\left( U_n^0 \geq r_y-\delta\sqrt{n}, U_n^t < r_y, |U_n^t-U_n^0|\leq \delta\sqrt{n} ight)}} \ 
onumber &\qquad + \E\left[  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r+r_y-U_n^0 + \delta\sqrt{n}))}{w_t(r)} \ind{U_n^0 < r_y+\delta\sqrt{n}} ight] \ &\qquad - \underset{(c)}{\underbrace{\P\left( |U_n^t - U_n^0| > \delta\sqrt{n} ight)}} - \underset{(d)}{\underbrace{\P\left( |U_n^t-U_n^0|\leq \delta\sqrt{n}, U_n^t\geq r_y, U_n^0<r_y+\delta\sqrt{n} ight)}} \end{align} where we used that $w_t$ is a decreasing function and $0< \ln(1+x)/x \leq 1$ for $x>0$. Terms $(b)$ and $(d)$ are clearly smaller than \[ \P(U_n^0 \in [r_y - \delta\sqrt{n}, r_y+\delta\sqrt{n}) ) . \] The central limit theorem gives us a sequence $\omega_1(n) 	o 0$ as $n	o\infty$ and a constant $c$ such that this probability is smaller than $c\delta + \omega_1(n)$. On the other hand, by Bienaymé--Chebyshev's inequality \[ \P(|U_n^t-U_n^0|>\delta\sqrt{n}) \leq  rac{\E[(U_1^t - U_1^0)^2]}{\delta^2} , \] which goes to zero as $t	o 0$ by \eqref{eq:coupling-first-step}. Let $(B_u)_{u\geq 0}$ be a centered standard Brownian motion. Fix some $s>0$, and from now on set $n = n(r) = \lfloor \eta^{-2} s w_t(r)^{-1}floor$. The sequence $U_n^0 (\eta^2 n)^{-1/2}$ converges to $B_1$ in distribution as $r	o\infty$, so that $U_n^0/r_y$ converges to $y^{-1} B_s$. Assume that \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right} holds with the right-hand side being replaced by some bounded, non-increasing function $f(y)$. Then  egin{multline*} \liminf_{r	o\infty} \E\left[  rac{\ln\left(1+w_t\left(r+r_y+\delta\sqrt{n} - U_n^0ight)ight)}{w_t(r)} \ind{U_n^0 < r_y\left(1 +  rac{\delta \sqrt{s}}{\eta}ight)} ight] \ \geq \E\left[ f\left( y\left[ 1 +  rac{\delta\sqrt{s}}{\eta} ight] - B_s ight) \ind{y\left[ 1 +  rac{\delta\sqrt{s}}{\eta} ight] - B_s > 0} ight] . \end{multline*} We can check this by taking a coupling of the sequence $U_n^0 (\eta^2 n)^{-1/2}$ that converges a.s. towards $B_1$ by the Skorokhod representation theorem, then using the monotonicity of $f$ with Fatou's Lemma. Clearly $f(y) = \ind{y\leq 0}$ works. Since $w_t(r)	o 0$ as $r	o\infty$, taking the liminf of \eqref{eq:discounted-expectation-X} as $r	o\infty$,  egin{multline*} \liminf_{r	o\infty} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n}  rac{-\E^{(t)}[X]}{w_t(r)} \ \geq \P\left(B_s \geq y- rac{\delta\sqrt{s}}{\eta} ight) + \E\left[ f\left( y\left[ 1 +  rac{\delta\sqrt{s}}{\eta} ight] - B_s ight) \ind{y\left[ 1 +  rac{\delta\sqrt{s}}{\eta} ight] > B_s} ight] - 2c\delta . \end{multline*} Take $\delta	o 0$:  egin{equation} \liminf_{r	o\infty} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n}  rac{-\E^{(t)}[X]}{w_t(r)} \geq \P(B_s\geq y) + \E\left[\ind{B_s < y} f\left(y-B_sight)ight] . \end{equation} On the other hand, by \eqref{eq:second-moment-Gr2} and taking $t_0>0$ small enough that $\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-1} \mathrm{Var}^{(t)}(\chi(\R))\leq 2\sigma^2$ for every $t\leq t_0$, we get uniformly in $t\in[0,t_0]$,  egin{align*} \E^{(t)}[X^2] \leq (\ln 	ilde h_t(r))^2 \E^{(t)}[G_n(\R)^2] \leq (\ln 	ilde h_t(r))^2 \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^n (1+2n\sigma^2) , \end{align*} Since $n \ln 	ilde h_t(r) \ulim r \infty s \eta^{-2}$ as $r	o\infty$ from the definition of $n$,  egin{equation} \limsup_{r	o\infty} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n}  rac{\E^{(t)}[X^2]}{w_t(r)} \leq  rac{2 s \sigma^2}{\eta^2} . \end{equation} Combining \eqref{eq:liminf-EX} and \eqref{eq:liminf-EX2},  egin{equation} \liminf_{r	o\infty}  rac{w_t(r+r_y)}{w_t(r)} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n} \geq \E\left[ \ind{B_s\geq y} + \ind{B_s<y} f\left(y-B_sight)ight] - s  rac{\sigma^2}{\eta^2} . \end{equation} Recall from \eqref{eq:asymptotic-expectation-chi-vol} that $1-\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] \sim \sqrt{2t\sigma^2}$ as $t	o 0$. Since $\liminf_{r	o\infty} r^2 w_t(r) \geq c(\alpha)  rac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} > 0$ by Lemma ef{lem:positivity-c-alpha} and since $t = t(r,\alpha)$ we get  egin{align*} \liminf_{r	o\infty}  rac{w_t(r+r_y)}{w_t(r)} &\geq \exp\left(-  rac{s}{w_t(r) \eta^2} rac{\alpha}{r^2} ight) \left\{ \E\left[ \ind{B_s\geq 1} + \ind{B_s<1} f\left(y-yB_sight)ight] - s  rac{\sigma^2}{\eta^2} ight \} \ &\geq \E\left[ \ind{B_s\geq 1} + \ind{B_s<1} f\left(y-yB_sight)ight] -  rac{s}{\eta^2}\left(\sigma^2 +  rac{\alpha}{c(\alpha)}ight) . \end{align*} The rest of the proof follows that of Lemma ef{lem:continuity-w-broad}:  egin{align*} \liminf_{r	o\infty}  rac{w_t(r+r_y)}{w_t(r)} &\geq \P(	au_y \leq x) - \left(  rac{\sigma^2}{\eta^2} +  rac{\alpha}{\eta^2 c(\alpha)} ight) \E\left[	au_y \ind{	au_y\leq x}ight] \ &\geq 1 -  rac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \inf_{x>0} \left(  rac{1}{\sqrt{x}} + y^2 \sqrt{x}  rac{2}{\eta^2}\left(\sigma^2 +  rac{\alpha}{c(\alpha)}ight) ight) \ &= 1 -  rac{4y}{\eta\sqrt{\pi}} \sqrt{\sigma^2 +  rac{\alpha}{c(\alpha)}} \ . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Adapt the continuity lemma proof under the tilted law, using the coupling of U^t and U^0. Key step: the subcritical factor E^{(t)}[chi(R)]^{-n} contributes alpha/c(alpha).

nodes.name: Follow the continuity lemma proof.
nodes.statement: In this proof, for conciseness we write $t = t(r,\alpha)$. We follow the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad}, with adaptations.
nodes.statement_short: Follow the continuity lemma proof.

nodes.name: Introduce r_y.
nodes.statement: Let $r_y = \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}$. Assume that $r$ is large enough that $u_t(r) \geq c(\alpha)/2$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce r_y.

nodes.name: Iterate the tilted convolution equation.
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:2convolution-equation-vol}, using that $\tilde h_t(x) \leq \tilde h_t(r)$ when $x\leq r$, \[ \tilde h_t(r+r_y) \leq \E^{(t)}\left[ \exp\left( \ln \tilde h_t(r) G_n([r_y,\infty)) + \int_{(-\infty,r_y]} \ln\tilde h_t(r+r_y-x) \d G_n(x) \right) \right] . \]
nodes.statement_short: Iterate the tilted convolution equation.

nodes.name: First-moment bound with error terms (a)-(d).
nodes.statement:
Write $X$ for the expression inside the exponential. As in Lemma ef{lem:continuity-w-broad}, we bound $\E[\e^{X}] \leq \E[1 + X +  rac{X^2}{2}]$, and do so by bounding the first and second moments of $X$ under $\E^{(t)}$: by the many-to-one formula \eqref{eq:many-to-one-chiR}  egin{align} 
onumber & \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n}  rac{-\E^{(t)}[X]}{w_t(r)} \ 
onumber &= \E\left[  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r))}{w_t(r)} \ind{U_n^t \geq r_y} +  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r+r_y-U_n^t))}{w_t(r)}\ind{U_n^t < r_y} ight] \ 
onumber &\geq  rac{\ln(1+w_r(t))}{w_t(r)}\P(U_n^t \geq r_y) + \E\left[  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r+r_y-U_n^t))}{w_t(r)} \ind{U_n^t<r_y , |U_n^t-U_n^0|\leq \delta\sqrt{n}} ight]\ 
onumber &\geq  rac{\ln(1+w_r(t))}{w_t(r)}\P(U_n^0 \geq r_y-\delta\sqrt{n}) \ 
onumber &\qquad - \underset{(a)}{\underbrace{\P\left(|U_n^t - U_n^0|>\delta\sqrt{n}ight)}} - \underset{(b)}{\underbrace{\P\left( U_n^0 \geq r_y-\delta\sqrt{n}, U_n^t < r_y, |U_n^t-U_n^0|\leq \delta\sqrt{n} ight)}} \ 
onumber &\qquad + \E\left[  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r+r_y-U_n^0 + \delta\sqrt{n}))}{w_t(r)} \ind{U_n^0 < r_y+\delta\sqrt{n}} ight] \ &\qquad - \underset{(c)}{\underbrace{\P\left( |U_n^t - U_n^0| > \delta\sqrt{n} ight)}} - \underset{(d)}{\underbrace{\P\left( |U_n^t-U_n^0|\leq \delta\sqrt{n}, U_n^t\geq r_y, U_n^0<r_y+\delta\sqrt{n} ight)}} \end{align} where we used that $w_t$ is a decreasing function and $0< \ln(1+x)/x \leq 1$ for $x>0$.
nodes.statement_short: First-moment bound with error terms (a)-(d).

nodes.name: Equation (79)
nodes.statement:
onumber & \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n}  rac{-\E^{(t)}[X]}{w_t(r)} \ 
onumber &= \E\left[  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r))}{w_t(r)} \ind{U_n^t \geq r_y} +  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r+r_y-U_n^t))}{w_t(r)}\ind{U_n^t < r_y} ight] \ 
onumber &\geq  rac{\ln(1+w_r(t))}{w_t(r)}\P(U_n^t \geq r_y) + \E\left[  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r+r_y-U_n^t))}{w_t(r)} \ind{U_n^t<r_y , |U_n^t-U_n^0|\leq \delta\sqrt{n}} ight]\ 
onumber &\geq  rac{\ln(1+w_r(t))}{w_t(r)}\P(U_n^0 \geq r_y-\delta\sqrt{n}) \ 
onumber &\qquad - \underset{(a)}{\underbrace{\P\left(|U_n^t - U_n^0|>\delta\sqrt{n}ight)}} - \underset{(b)}{\underbrace{\P\left( U_n^0 \geq r_y-\delta\sqrt{n}, U_n^t < r_y, |U_n^t-U_n^0|\leq \delta\sqrt{n} ight)}} \ 
onumber &\qquad + \E\left[  rac{\ln(1+w_t(r+r_y-U_n^0 + \delta\sqrt{n}))}{w_t(r)} \ind{U_n^0 < r_y+\delta\sqrt{n}} ight] \ &\qquad - \underset{(c)}{\underbrace{\P\left( |U_n^t - U_n^0| > \delta\sqrt{n} ight)}} - \underset{(d)}{\underbrace{\P\left( |U_n^t-U_n^0|\leq \delta\sqrt{n}, U_n^t\geq r_y, U_n^0<r_y+\delta\sqrt{n} ight)}}
nodes.label: eq:discounted-expectation-X

nodes.name: CLT and Chebyshev control the error terms.
nodes.statement: Terms $(b)$ and $(d)$ are clearly smaller than \[ \P(U_n^0 \in [r_y - \delta\sqrt{n}, r_y+\delta\sqrt{n}) ) . \] The central limit theorem gives us a sequence $\omega_1(n) \to 0$ as $n\to\infty$ and a constant $c$ such that this probability is smaller than $c\delta + \omega_1(n)$. On the other hand, by Bienaymé--Chebyshev's inequality \[ \P(|U_n^t-U_n^0|>\delta\sqrt{n}) \leq \frac{\E[(U_1^t - U_1^0)^2]}{\delta^2} , \] which goes to zero as $t\to 0$ by \eqref{eq:coupling-first-step}.
nodes.statement_short: CLT and Chebyshev control the error terms.

nodes.name: Choose n of order s/w_t(r) and pass to Brownian motion.
nodes.statement: Let $(B_u)_{u\geq 0}$ be a centered standard Brownian motion. Fix some $s>0$, and from now on set $n = n(r) = \lfloor \eta^{-2} s w_t(r)^{-1}\rfloor$. The sequence $U_n^0 (\eta^2 n)^{-1/2}$ converges to $B_1$ in distribution as $r\to\infty$, so that $U_n^0/r_y$ converges to $y^{-1} B_s$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose n of order s/w_t(r) and pass to Brownian motion.

nodes.name: Provisional lower bound f and Fatou.
nodes.statement: Assume that \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right} holds with the right-hand side being replaced by some bounded, non-increasing function $f(y)$. Then \begin{multline*} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \E\left[ \frac{\ln\left(1+w_t\left(r+r_y+\delta\sqrt{n} - U_n^0\right)\right)}{w_t(r)} \ind{U_n^0 < r_y\left(1 + \frac{\delta \sqrt{s}}{\eta}\right)} \right] \\ \geq \E\left[ f\left( y\left[ 1 + \frac{\delta\sqrt{s}}{\eta} \right] - B_s \right) \ind{y\left[ 1 + \frac{\delta\sqrt{s}}{\eta} \right] - B_s > 0} \right] . \end{multline*} We can check this by taking a coupling of the sequence $U_n^0 (\eta^2 n)^{-1/2}$ that converges a.s. towards $B_1$ by the Skorokhod representation theorem, then using the monotonicity of $f$ with Fatou's Lemma. Clearly $f(y) = \ind{y\leq 0}$ works.
nodes.statement_short: Provisional lower bound f and Fatou.

nodes.name: Liminf of the first moment.
nodes.statement: Since $w_t(r)\to 0$ as $r\to\infty$, taking the liminf of \eqref{eq:discounted-expectation-X} as $r\to\infty$, \begin{multline*} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n} \frac{-\E^{(t)}[X]}{w_t(r)} \\ \geq \P\left(B_s \geq y-\frac{\delta\sqrt{s}}{\eta} \right) + \E\left[ f\left( y\left[ 1 + \frac{\delta\sqrt{s}}{\eta} \right] - B_s \right) \ind{y\left[ 1 + \frac{\delta\sqrt{s}}{\eta} \right] > B_s} \right] - 2c\delta . \end{multline*} Take $\delta\to 0$: \begin{equation} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n} \frac{-\E^{(t)}[X]}{w_t(r)} \geq \P(B_s\geq y) + \E\left[\ind{B_s < y} f\left(y-B_s\right)\right] . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Liminf of the first moment.

nodes.name: Equation (80)
nodes.statement: \liminf_{r\to\infty} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n} \frac{-\E^{(t)}[X]}{w_t(r)} \geq \P(B_s\geq y) + \E\left[\ind{B_s < y} f\left(y-B_s\right)\right] .
nodes.label: eq:liminf-EX

nodes.name: Second moment bound.
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by \eqref{eq:second-moment-Gr2} and taking $t_0>0$ small enough that $\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-1} \mathrm{Var}^{(t)}(\chi(\R))\leq 2\sigma^2$ for every $t\leq t_0$, we get uniformly in $t\in[0,t_0]$, \begin{align*} \E^{(t)}[X^2] \leq (\ln \tilde h_t(r))^2 \E^{(t)}[G_n(\R)^2] \leq (\ln \tilde h_t(r))^2 \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^n (1+2n\sigma^2) , \end{align*} Since $n \ln \tilde h_t(r) \ulim r \infty s \eta^{-2}$ as $r\to\infty$ from the definition of $n$, \begin{equation} \limsup_{r\to\infty} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n} \frac{\E^{(t)}[X^2]}{w_t(r)} \leq \frac{2 s \sigma^2}{\eta^2} . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Second moment bound.

nodes.name: Equation (81)
nodes.statement: \limsup_{r\to\infty} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n} \frac{\E^{(t)}[X^2]}{w_t(r)} \leq \frac{2 s \sigma^2}{\eta^2} .
nodes.label: eq:liminf-EX2

nodes.name: Combine and absorb the subcritical factor.
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:liminf-EX} and \eqref{eq:liminf-EX2}, \begin{equation} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w_t(r+r_y)}{w_t(r)} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n} \geq \E\left[ \ind{B_s\geq y} + \ind{B_s<y} f\left(y-B_s\right)\right] - s \frac{\sigma^2}{\eta^2} . \end{equation} Recall from \eqref{eq:asymptotic-expectation-chi-vol} that $1-\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] \sim \sqrt{2t\sigma^2}$ as $t\to 0$. Since $\liminf_{r\to\infty} r^2 w_t(r) \geq c(\alpha) \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2} > 0$ by Lemma \ref{lem:positivity-c-alpha} and since $t = t(r,\alpha)$ we get \begin{align*} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w_t(r+r_y)}{w_t(r)} &\geq \exp\left(- \frac{s}{w_t(r) \eta^2}\frac{\alpha}{r^2} \right) \left\{ \E\left[ \ind{B_s\geq 1} + \ind{B_s<1} f\left(y-yB_s\right)\right] - s \frac{\sigma^2}{\eta^2} \right \} \\ &\geq \E\left[ \ind{B_s\geq 1} + \ind{B_s<1} f\left(y-yB_s\right)\right] - \frac{s}{\eta^2}\left(\sigma^2 + \frac{\alpha}{c(\alpha)}\right) . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Combine and absorb the subcritical factor.

nodes.name: Equation (82)
nodes.statement: \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w_t(r+r_y)}{w_t(r)} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]^{-n} \geq \E\left[ \ind{B_s\geq y} + \ind{B_s<y} f\left(y-B_s\right)\right] - s \frac{\sigma^2}{\eta^2} .
nodes.label: eq:2why-t-must-vary

nodes.name: Optimize the Brownian hitting-time bound.
nodes.statement: The rest of the proof follows that of Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad}: \begin{align*} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac{w_t(r+r_y)}{w_t(r)} &\geq \P(\tau_y \leq x) - \left( \frac{\sigma^2}{\eta^2} + \frac{\alpha}{\eta^2 c(\alpha)} \right) \E\left[\tau_y \ind{\tau_y\leq x}\right] \\ &\geq 1 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \inf_{x>0} \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} + y^2 \sqrt{x} \frac{2}{\eta^2}\left(\sigma^2 + \frac{\alpha}{c(\alpha)}\right) \right) \\ &= 1 - \frac{4y}{\eta\sqrt{\pi}} \sqrt{\sigma^2 + \frac{\alpha}{c(\alpha)}} \ . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Optimize the Brownian hitting-time bound.

nodes.name: Continuity of the tail w_t (strong, uniform in t)
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha>0$ and $y\geq 0$, recalling $D(\alpha)$ from Lemma \ref{lem:2continuity-w-broad-volume}, \begin{equation} \liminf_{r\to\infty} \inf_{0\leq t \leq t(r,\alpha)} \frac{w_t\left(r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}\right)}{w_t(r)} \geq \begin{cases} 1 - y D(\alpha) &\text{ if } y\geq 0, \\ 1 &\text{ if } y\leq 0 , \end{cases} \end{equation} and for every $y > - \frac{2}{\e D(\alpha)}$, \begin{equation} \limsup_{r\to\infty} \sup_{0\leq t \leq t(r,\alpha)} \frac{w_t\left(r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}\right)}{w_t(r)} \leq \begin{cases} f_\alpha^{-1}(-y) &\text{ if } y\leq 0 , \\ 1 &\text{ if } y\geq 0 , \end{cases} \end{equation} where $f_\alpha^{-1}$ is the inverse of the function $f_\alpha : [1,3] \to [0, \frac{2}{D(\alpha) 3\sqrt{3}} ] , x \mapsto \frac{1-x^{-1}}{D(\alpha)\sqrt{x}} $.
nodes.label: lem:2continuity-w-broad-volume-strong

nodes.name: Equation (83)
nodes.statement: \liminf_{r\to\infty} \inf_{0\leq t \leq t(r,\alpha)} \frac{w_t\left(r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}\right)}{w_t(r)} \geq \begin{cases} 1 - y D(\alpha) &\text{ if } y\geq 0, \\ 1 &\text{ if } y\leq 0 , \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right-strong

nodes.name: Equation (84)
nodes.statement: \limsup_{r\to\infty} \sup_{0\leq t \leq t(r,\alpha)} \frac{w_t\left(r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}\right)}{w_t(r)} \leq \begin{cases} f_\alpha^{-1}(-y) &\text{ if } y\leq 0 , \\ 1 &\text{ if } y\geq 0 , \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-left-strong

nodes.name: Ratio at a fixed offset tends to 1
nodes.statement: A consequence of \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right-strong} is that for every fixed $z\in\R$, \begin{equation} \frac{w_{t(r,\alpha)}(r+z)}{w_{t(r,\alpha)}(r)} \ulim r \infty 1 . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (85)
nodes.statement: \frac{w_{t(r,\alpha)}(r+z)}{w_{t(r,\alpha)}(r)} \ulim r \infty 1 .
nodes.label: eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-constant-offset

nodes.name: Proof of the fixed-offset ratio
nodes.statement: It follows directly when $z\geq 0$. For $z<0$, taking $\beta>\alpha$ we find that $t(r+z,\beta) \geq t(r,\alpha)$ for every large enough $r$, and using \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right-strong} with $r+z$ instead of $r$ and $\beta$ instead of $\alpha$ gives the desired bound.
nodes.statement_short: Direct for z >= 0; for z < 0 apply the strong bound at r+z with a larger alpha.

nodes.name: Proof of the strong continuity lemma
nodes.statement: Fix $\alpha>0$, $\varepsilon>0$ and $r_\varepsilon$ such that for every $r\geq r_\varepsilon$, by Lemma \ref{lem:2uniform-continuity-u}, for every $\beta,\gamma \in [0,\alpha]$ with $|\beta-\gamma|\leq \varepsilon$ we have $\left| \frac{w_{t(r,\beta)}(r)}{w_{t(r,\gamma)}(r)} - 1 \right| \leq \varepsilon$. Writing $s = t(r,\gamma)$ and $t=t(r,\beta)$, \begin{align*} \frac{w_t\left(r+\frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}\right)}{w_t(r)} &\geq (1-\varepsilon)^2 \frac{w_s\left( r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}\right)}{w_s(r)} \geq (1-\varepsilon)^2 \frac{w_s\left( r + \frac{\frac{y}{1-\varepsilon}}{\sqrt{w_s(r)}}\right)}{w_s(r)} . \end{align*} Taking $r_\varepsilon$ larger if necessary, by Lemma \ref{lem:2continuity-w-broad-volume} we can assume that for every $\gamma \in \varepsilon\Z \cap [0,\alpha]$ \[ \frac{w_{t(r,\gamma)}\left( r + \frac{\frac{y}{1-\varepsilon}}{\sqrt{w_{t(r,\gamma)}(r)}}\right)}{w_{t(r,\gamma)}(r)} \geq (1-\varepsilon) \left(1 - D(\gamma) \frac{y}{1-\varepsilon} \right) \geq 1-\varepsilon - D(\alpha) y . \] Here we used that $c$ is a nonincreasing function. It follows that for every $r\geq r_\varepsilon$ \[ \inf_{0\leq t \leq t(r,\alpha)} \frac{w_t\left(r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}\right)}{w_t(r)} \geq (1-\varepsilon)^2 (1 - \varepsilon - D(\alpha) y) .\] Taking the liminf as $r\to\infty$, then $\varepsilon\to 0$ gives \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right-strong}. We first prove \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-left-strong} without the supremum; \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-left-strong} will follow by the same reasoning as that we used above to deduce \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right-strong} from \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right}. Consider as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad} the quantity $r_{x} = \inf\{ r \geq 0, w_{t(r,\alpha)}(r) \leq x\}$. Let $B\geq 1$ and $t=t(r,\alpha)$; by \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right-strong}, \[ \liminf_{r\to\infty} \inf_{A \in[1,B]} \frac{w_t\left(r_{Aw_t(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)})}}\right)}{w_t(r_{Aw(r)})} \geq 1 - y D(\alpha) . \] For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $r_\varepsilon$ such that for every $A\in [1,B]$ and every $r\geq r_\varepsilon$, the ratio inside the $\inf$ is larger than $(1-\varepsilon) (1-y D(\alpha))$. Since $w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)}-1)>Aw_t(r)$, using \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-constant-offset} with $z=-1$ and taking $r_\varepsilon$ larger if necessary, we have $w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)}) \geq (1-\varepsilon) Aw_t(r)$ for every $r\geq r_\varepsilon$, thus \[ \frac{w_t\left(r_{Aw_t(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)})}}\right)}{w_t(r)} \geq A(1-\varepsilon) \frac{w_t\left(r_{Aw_t(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)})}}\right)}{w_t(r_{Aw(r)})} \geq A (1-y D(\alpha)) (1-\varepsilon)^2 , \] so that for every $y\leq D(\alpha)^{-1}(1 - (A(1-\varepsilon)^2)^{-1})$, the right-hand side is larger than $1$, hence since $w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)}) \leq A w_t(r)$ \[ r > r_{Aw_t(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)})}} \geq r_{Aw_t(r)} + \frac{y/\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}} \implies r_{Aw_r(t)} \leq r - \frac{y/\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}} \ , \] whence \[ \frac{w_t\left( r - \frac{y/\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}} \right)}{w_t(r)} \leq \frac{w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)})}{w_t(r)} \leq A . \] We conclude with the same reasoning as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad}. Finally, we can use the same reasoning as in the proof of Corollary \ref{cor:2uniform-limit-r2wt} to prove the final statement of the Lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Discretize alpha using uniform continuity in alpha and apply the weak lemma; the upper bound follows by inversion through r_x as before.

nodes.name: Compare w_t with w_s for nearby alpha.
nodes.statement: Fix $\alpha>0$, $\varepsilon>0$ and $r_\varepsilon$ such that for every $r\geq r_\varepsilon$, by Lemma \ref{lem:2uniform-continuity-u}, for every $\beta,\gamma \in [0,\alpha]$ with $|\beta-\gamma|\leq \varepsilon$ we have $\left| \frac{w_{t(r,\beta)}(r)}{w_{t(r,\gamma)}(r)} - 1 \right| \leq \varepsilon$. Writing $s = t(r,\gamma)$ and $t=t(r,\beta)$, \begin{align*} \frac{w_t\left(r+\frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}\right)}{w_t(r)} &\geq (1-\varepsilon)^2 \frac{w_s\left( r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}\right)}{w_s(r)} \geq (1-\varepsilon)^2 \frac{w_s\left( r + \frac{\frac{y}{1-\varepsilon}}{\sqrt{w_s(r)}}\right)}{w_s(r)} . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Compare w_t with w_s for nearby alpha.

nodes.name: Apply the weak continuity lemma on a finite grid of alphas.
nodes.statement: Taking $r_\varepsilon$ larger if necessary, by Lemma \ref{lem:2continuity-w-broad-volume} we can assume that for every $\gamma \in \varepsilon\Z \cap [0,\alpha]$ \[ \frac{w_{t(r,\gamma)}\left( r + \frac{\frac{y}{1-\varepsilon}}{\sqrt{w_{t(r,\gamma)}(r)}}\right)}{w_{t(r,\gamma)}(r)} \geq (1-\varepsilon) \left(1 - D(\gamma) \frac{y}{1-\varepsilon} \right) \geq 1-\varepsilon - D(\alpha) y . \] Here we used that $c$ is a nonincreasing function.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the weak continuity lemma on a finite grid of alphas.

nodes.name: Obtain the uniform lower bound.
nodes.statement: It follows that for every $r\geq r_\varepsilon$ \[ \inf_{0\leq t \leq t(r,\alpha)} \frac{w_t\left(r + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}}\right)}{w_t(r)} \geq (1-\varepsilon)^2 (1 - \varepsilon - D(\alpha) y) .\] Taking the liminf as $r\to\infty$, then $\varepsilon\to 0$ gives \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right-strong}.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain the uniform lower bound.

nodes.name: Reduce the upper bound to fixed t.
nodes.statement: We first prove \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-left-strong} without the supremum; \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-left-strong} will follow by the same reasoning as that we used above to deduce \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right-strong} from \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the upper bound to fixed t.

nodes.name: Introduce r_x and apply the lower bound there.
nodes.statement: Consider as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad} the quantity $r_{x} = \inf\{ r \geq 0, w_{t(r,\alpha)}(r) \leq x\}$. Let $B\geq 1$ and $t=t(r,\alpha)$; by \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-right-strong}, \[ \liminf_{r\to\infty} \inf_{A \in[1,B]} \frac{w_t\left(r_{Aw_t(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)})}}\right)}{w_t(r_{Aw(r)})} \geq 1 - y D(\alpha) . \]
nodes.statement_short: Introduce r_x and apply the lower bound there.

nodes.name: Invert as in the continuity lemma.
nodes.statement: For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $r_\varepsilon$ such that for every $A\in [1,B]$ and every $r\geq r_\varepsilon$, the ratio inside the $\inf$ is larger than $(1-\varepsilon) (1-y D(\alpha))$. Since $w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)}-1)>Aw_t(r)$, using \eqref{eq:2continuity-ratio-vol-constant-offset} with $z=-1$ and taking $r_\varepsilon$ larger if necessary, we have $w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)}) \geq (1-\varepsilon) Aw_t(r)$ for every $r\geq r_\varepsilon$, thus \[ \frac{w_t\left(r_{Aw_t(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)})}}\right)}{w_t(r)} \geq A(1-\varepsilon) \frac{w_t\left(r_{Aw_t(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)})}}\right)}{w_t(r_{Aw(r)})} \geq A (1-y D(\alpha)) (1-\varepsilon)^2 , \] so that for every $y\leq D(\alpha)^{-1}(1 - (A(1-\varepsilon)^2)^{-1})$, the right-hand side is larger than $1$, hence since $w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)}) \leq A w_t(r)$ \[ r > r_{Aw_t(r)} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)})}} \geq r_{Aw_t(r)} + \frac{y/\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}} \implies r_{Aw_r(t)} \leq r - \frac{y/\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}} \ , \] whence \[ \frac{w_t\left( r - \frac{y/\sqrt{A}}{\sqrt{w_t(r)}} \right)}{w_t(r)} \leq \frac{w_t(r_{Aw_t(r)})}{w_t(r)} \leq A . \] We conclude with the same reasoning as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad}.
nodes.statement_short: Invert as in the continuity lemma.

nodes.name: Uniformity in t as in the corollary.
nodes.statement: Finally, we can use the same reasoning as in the proof of Corollary \ref{cor:2uniform-limit-r2wt} to prove the final statement of the Lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Uniformity in t as in the corollary.

nodes.name: Tilted size-biased pair (Z, I)
nodes.statement: Define the distribution of $(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)})$ under $\E^{(t)}$ to be such that for every positive and measurable $f$, \begin{equation} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] \cdot \E^{(t)}\left[ f(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}) \right] = \E^{(t)}\left[ \int f(x,\ind{E(r,R,\delta)}) \d\chi(x) \right] . \end{equation} Note that $\E^{(t)}[f(Z)] = \E[f(Z_t)]$ for every $t$.

nodes.name: Equation (86)
nodes.statement: \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] \cdot \E^{(t)}\left[ f(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}) \right] = \E^{(t)}\left[ \int f(x,\ind{E(r,R,\delta)}) \d\chi(x) \right] .
nodes.label: eq:2def-ZI-vol

nodes.name: Tilted Palm kernel
nodes.statement: Define the Markov kernel $((z,i), \Gamma) \mapsto P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,i}(\Gamma)$ (that implicitely depend on $t$), where $\Gamma$ is a measurable subset of the set of point measures, $i\in\{0,1\}$ and $z\in\R$, such that for every positive and measurable $g$, if $(X_i)_{1\leq i \leq \chi(\R)}$ is a measurable numbering of the atoms of $\chi$, \begin{equation} \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] \cdot \E^{(t)}\left[ \int g\left(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}, \phi \right) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}}(\phi) \right] = \E^{(t)}\left[ \sum_{i=1}^{\chi(\R)} g\left(X_i , \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}, \chi - \delta_{X_i} \right) \right] . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (87)
nodes.statement: \E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] \cdot \E^{(t)}\left[ \int g\left(Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}, \phi \right) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z, I^{(r,R,\delta)}}(\phi) \right] = \E^{(t)}\left[ \sum_{i=1}^{\chi(\R)} g\left(X_i , \ind{E(r,R,\delta)}, \chi - \delta_{X_i} \right) \right] .
nodes.label: eq:2def-Palm-vol

nodes.name: Tilted mean measure function
nodes.statement: This Markov kernel defines a ``mean measure function'' $M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z}$ (that implicitely depend on $t$) such that for every measurable subset $A$ of $\R$, \begin{equation} M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z}(A) = \int \phi(A) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,1}(\phi) . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (88)
nodes.statement: M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z}(A) = \int \phi(A) \d P^{(r,R,\delta)}_{z,1}(\phi) .
nodes.label: eq:2def-Palm-mean-vol

nodes.name: Approximate convolution equation for w_t
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{assum} 1. to 4., there exists $\delta^0, t_0, r_0>0$ and $C>0$ such that for every $\delta \in (0,\delta^0)$, $t\in [0,t_0)$, $r_\bullet \geq r_0$, $r\geq 2r_\bullet$ and every $r_\bullet \leq R \leq r-r_\bullet$, \begin{multline} w_t(r) = \E^{(t)}\Bigg[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w_t(r-Z) \exp\Big( \ln\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] - w_t(r-Z) - \frac{1}{2} \int w_t(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \\ + \E^{(t)}\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w_t(r-Z) \right] \Big) \Bigg] + \mathrm{Remainder}_t(r,R,\delta) , \end{multline} where \begin{equation*} C_\mathrm{rem} |\mathrm{Remainder}_t(r,R,\delta)| \leq \P(\Lambda>R) + \P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\delta}{w_t(r-R)}\right) + (\sigma^2 + 1) w_t(r-R)^2 \left( w_t(r-R) + \delta \right) . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Tilted analogue of the approximate convolution equation, with an extra ln E^{(t)}[chi(R)] in the exponential.
nodes.label: prop:2convolution-w-vol

nodes.name: Equation (89)
nodes.statement: w_t(r) = \E^{(t)}\Bigg[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w_t(r-Z) \exp\Big( \ln\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] - w_t(r-Z) - \frac{1}{2} \int w_t(r-y) \d M^{(r,R,\delta)}_{Z} (y) \\ + \E^{(t)}\left[ I^{(r,R,\delta)} w_t(r-Z) \right] \Big) \Bigg] + \mathrm{Remainder}_t(r,R,\delta) ,
nodes.label: eq:2convolution-w-vol

nodes.name: Proof of the tilted approximate convolution equation
nodes.statement: The proof of this Proposition is identical to that of Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w} with $\E$ replaced by $\E^{(t)}$, $h$ replaced by $\tilde h_t$ and $w$ replaced by $w_t$, since most of the estimates therein are deterministic and the rest have been controlled in Section \ref{sec:2Laplace-volume-without-displacement}. Note the additional $\ln\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]$ in the exponential which comes from \eqref{eq:2def-ZI-vol}, \eqref{eq:2def-Palm-vol} and \eqref{eq:2def-Palm-mean-vol}. A useful observation to bound the remainder with expressions in $\P$ and not in $\P^{(t)}$ is \eqref{eq:bound-Et-by-2E}. More precisely, we use the following substitutions.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the untilted proof with E, h, w replaced by E^{(t)}, tilde h_t, w_t, using E^{(t)} <= 2E.

nodes.name: Same proof with tilted quantities.
nodes.statement: The proof of this Proposition is identical to that of Proposition \ref{prop:convolution-w} with $\E$ replaced by $\E^{(t)}$, $h$ replaced by $\tilde h_t$ and $w$ replaced by $w_t$, since most of the estimates therein are deterministic and the rest have been controlled in Section \ref{sec:2Laplace-volume-without-displacement}.
nodes.statement_short: Same proof with tilted quantities.

nodes.name: Account for the extra logarithmic term and the change of mea
nodes.statement: Note the additional $\ln\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]$ in the exponential which comes from \eqref{eq:2def-ZI-vol}, \eqref{eq:2def-Palm-vol} and \eqref{eq:2def-Palm-mean-vol}. A useful observation to bound the remainder with expressions in $\P$ and not in $\P^{(t)}$ is \eqref{eq:bound-Et-by-2E}. More precisely, we use the following substitutions.
nodes.statement_short: Account for the extra logarithmic term and the change of measure.

nodes.name: Tilted almost-martingale
nodes.statement: Fix $r_\bullet \geq r_0$ and $r\geq 2r_\bullet$. Define $S_n$, $R_n$, $\delta_n$ and $\FF_n$ as in Section \ref{sec:the-martingale}, and \[ T = \inf\{n\geq 0: S_n < 2r_\bullet \text{ or } R_n\notin [r_\bullet, S_n-r_\bullet] \text{ or } \delta_n \notin (0,\delta^0)\}. \] Proposition \ref{prop:almost-martingale} also holds, with an extra $n\ln\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)]$ in the exponential in $\kW^{(r)}_n$ \begin{multline} \kW^{(r)}_n = \left(\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} I_{k+1}\right) \exp\Bigg( n \ln\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] - \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \left(w_t(S_{k+1}) - \E^{(t)}\left[I^{(S_{k}, R_{k}, \delta_{k})} w_t(S_{k}-Z) \, | \, \FF_{k} \right] \right) \\ -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \int w_t(S_{k}-y) \d M_{S_k-S_{k+1}}^{(S_k, R_k, \delta_k)}(y) \Bigg) \end{multline} and replacing $\E$ by $\E^{(t)}$, $w$ by $w_t$ and $\mathrm{Remainder}$ by $\mathrm{Remainder}_t$.
nodes.statement_short: The almost-martingale property holds for the tilted walk with an extra n ln E^{(t)}[chi(R)] in the discount process.

nodes.name: Equation (90)
nodes.statement: \kW^{(r)}_n = \left(\prod_{k=0}^{n-1} I_{k+1}\right) \exp\Bigg( n \ln\E^{(t)}[\chi(\R)] - \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \left(w_t(S_{k+1}) - \E^{(t)}\left[I^{(S_{k}, R_{k}, \delta_{k})} w_t(S_{k}-Z) \, | \, \FF_{k} \right] \right) \\ -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \int w_t(S_{k}-y) \d M_{S_k-S_{k+1}}^{(S_k, R_k, \delta_k)}(y) \Bigg)
nodes.label: eq:2def-Z-vol

nodes.name: Uniform integrability of the tilted discount process
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha>0$ and $0<C_-<1<C_+<\infty$, there exists $a_\alpha$ and $r_\alpha$ such that for every $a\in (0,a_\alpha)$, every $r_\bullet \geq r_\alpha$, $r\geq 2 r_\bullet$ and every $t\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]$, letting $R_n = \RR := a / \sqrt{w_t(C_- r)}$ for every $n$ and $T_a = T \wedge \inf \{ n\geq 0 : S_n \notin [C_-r, C_+r] \}$, the stopped process $(\kW^{(r)}_{n\wedge T_a})_{n\geq 0}$ is a uniformly integrable supermartingale under $\E^{(t)}$.
nodes.statement_short: For t <= t(r,alpha) and S_n kept in [C_- r, C_+ r], the stopped tilted discount process is a uniformly integrable supermartingale.
nodes.label: lem:2discount-UI-vol

nodes.name: Proof of tilted uniform integrability
nodes.statement: The majority of the proof is a straightforward adaptation of that of Lemma \ref{lem:discount-UI} with the modifications described before Lemma \ref{lem:2discount-UI-vol}. Instead of Lemma \ref{lem:lower-bound-w} we use Corollary \ref{cor:2uniform-limit-r2wt} with $(2C_+)^2\alpha$ instead of $\alpha$, $2C_+ r$ instead of $r$, and $b=C_- / C_+ / 4$. Recalling $t(r,\alpha) = t(2C_+ r, (2C_+)^2 \alpha)$, we find $r_\alpha\geq r_0$ such that that for every $r\geq 2r_\alpha$, \[ \frac{1}{2}c((2C_+)^2\alpha) \leq \inf_{t\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]} \inf_{C_-r/2 \leq y \leq 2C_+r} y^2 w_{t}(y) \leq \sup_{t\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]} \sup_{C_-r/2 \leq y \leq 2C_+r} y^2 w_{t)}(y) \leq \frac{12 \eta^2}{\sigma^2} . \] Take $a_\alpha = \sqrt{c((2C_+)^2\alpha)/8}$, then for every $a \in (0,a_\alpha)$ and for every $C_- r \leq x \leq C_+ r$ we have $\RR \leq \frac{x}{2}$ hence $C_- r/2 \leq x/2 \leq x-\RR \leq C_+ r$, thus \begin{equation} \sup_{t\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]} \sup_{r\geq 2r_\alpha} \sup_{a\in (0,a_\alpha)} \sup_{x\in [C_-r, C_+r]} \frac{w_{t}(x-\RR)^2}{w_{t}(x-K)} \ulim {r_\alpha} \infty 0 . \end{equation} Call $(\delta, r_\bullet, r, x)$ ``admissible’’ if $\delta\in (0,\delta^0)$, $r_\bullet \geq r_\alpha$, $r\geq 2r_\bullet$ and $x \in [C_-r, C_+r] \cap [2r_\bullet, \infty)$. We point out that \begin{equation} T_a = \inf \{ n\geq 0 \ : \ (\delta_n, r_\bullet, r, S_n) \text{ is not admissible} \} . \end{equation} A key step of the proof is to show that for every admissible $(\delta, r_\bullet, r, x)$, letting \[ A = - I^{(x,\RR,\delta)}w_t(x-Z) + \E^{(t)}\left[I^{(x,\RR,\delta)} w_t(x-Z)\right] \quad , \quad B = - \frac{I^{(x,\RR,\delta)}} 2 \int w_t(x-y) \d M_Z^{(x,\RR,\delta)}(y) \] then $\E^{(t)}[I^{(x, \RR, \delta)} \e^{2(A+B)}] \leq 1$; let us prove it. Obviously $|A|\leq w_t(x-\RR)$ from \eqref{eq:2def-ZI-vol}. By the analogue of \eqref{eq:Palm-controle-M} (using \eqref{eq:2def-Palm-vol} and \eqref{eq:2def-Palm-mean-vol}) applied to the new $M_z^{(r,\RR,\delta)}$ we have $M_z^{(x,\RR,\delta)}(\R) \leq \frac{\delta}{w_t(x-\RR)}-1$ on $E(r,\RR,\delta)$ for every $z, x, \RR, \delta$, hence $-\frac\delta 2 \leq B\leq 0$. Then \begin{equation*} \E^{(t)}[B] \geq -\frac{w_t(x-\RR)}{2} \E^{(t)}\left[\ind{E(x,\RR,\delta)} (\chi(\R)-1)\chi(\R)) \right] \geq -\sigma^2 w_t(x-\RR) \end{equation*} as soon as $t\in [0,t_0)$ by \eqref{eq:2variance-chi-vol}, where we take $t_0>0$ smaller than in Proposition \ref{prop:2convolution-w-vol} if necessary. On the other hand, by \eqref{eq:bound-Et-by-2E} and dominated convergence \begin{align*} \sup_{t\in [0,t_0)} \E^{(t)}\left[(1-\ind{E(x,\RR,\delta)}) \chi(\R) (\chi(\R)-1) \right] \leq 2\E\left[(1-\ind{E(x,\RR,\delta)}) \chi(\R) (\chi(\R)-1) \right] \ulim {r_0} \infty 0 \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \sup_{t\in [0,t_0)} \E^{(t)}\left[ \chi((-\infty, K)) (\chi(\R)-1) \right] \leq 2 \E\left[ \chi((-\infty, K)) (\chi(\R)-1) \right] \ulim K {-\infty} 0 , \end{align*} which together with \eqref{eq:2variance-chi-vol} means that we can find $K\in\R$ that only depends on $t_0$ such that, taking $r_\alpha$ larger if necessary, \begin{align*} \inf_{t\in[0,t_0)} \inf_{r\geq 2r_\alpha} \inf_{\delta \in (0,\delta^0)} \E^{(t)}\left[ \ind{E(x,\RR,\delta)} \chi([K,\infty)) (\chi(\R)-1) \right] \geq \frac{\sigma^2}{2} , \end{align*} hence $\E^{(t)}[B] \leq - c w_t(x-K)$ for every $x\in [C_-r, C_+r]$, where $c=\sigma^2/4$. We deduce \[ \E^{(t)}\left[ I^{(x,\RR,\delta)} \e^{2(A+B)} \right] \leq 1 - c w_t(x-K) + 4(\sigma^2+1) w_t(x-\RR)^2 . \] By \eqref{eq:wt2-over-wt-goes-to-zero}, taking $r_\alpha$ larger if necessary, we can thus ensure that for every admissible $(\delta, r_\bullet, r, x)$ we have $t(r,\alpha)<t_0$ and $\E^{(t)}\left[ I^{(x,\RR,\delta)} \e^{2(A+B)} \right] \leq 1$. The uniform integrability and the bound on the conditional expectation follows as in Lemma \ref{lem:discount-UI}.
nodes.statement_short: Adapt the untilted proof, replacing the lower bound on w by the uniform corollary and showing E^{(t)}[I e^{2(A+B)}] <= 1.

nodes.name: Adapt the untilted proof.
nodes.statement: The majority of the proof is a straightforward adaptation of that of Lemma \ref{lem:discount-UI} with the modifications described before Lemma \ref{lem:2discount-UI-vol}.
nodes.statement_short: Adapt the untilted proof.

nodes.name: Uniform bounds on w_t choose a_alpha.
nodes.statement: Instead of Lemma \ref{lem:lower-bound-w} we use Corollary \ref{cor:2uniform-limit-r2wt} with $(2C_+)^2\alpha$ instead of $\alpha$, $2C_+ r$ instead of $r$, and $b=C_- / C_+ / 4$. Recalling $t(r,\alpha) = t(2C_+ r, (2C_+)^2 \alpha)$, we find $r_\alpha\geq r_0$ such that that for every $r\geq 2r_\alpha$, \[ \frac{1}{2}c((2C_+)^2\alpha) \leq \inf_{t\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]} \inf_{C_-r/2 \leq y \leq 2C_+r} y^2 w_{t}(y) \leq \sup_{t\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]} \sup_{C_-r/2 \leq y \leq 2C_+r} y^2 w_{t)}(y) \leq \frac{12 \eta^2}{\sigma^2} . \] Take $a_\alpha = \sqrt{c((2C_+)^2\alpha)/8}$, then for every $a \in (0,a_\alpha)$ and for every $C_- r \leq x \leq C_+ r$ we have $\RR \leq \frac{x}{2}$ hence $C_- r/2 \leq x/2 \leq x-\RR \leq C_+ r$, thus \begin{equation} \sup_{t\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]} \sup_{r\geq 2r_\alpha} \sup_{a\in (0,a_\alpha)} \sup_{x\in [C_-r, C_+r]} \frac{w_{t}(x-\RR)^2}{w_{t}(x-K)} \ulim {r_\alpha} \infty 0 . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Uniform bounds on w_t choose a_alpha.

nodes.name: Equation (91)
nodes.statement: \sup_{t\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]} \sup_{r\geq 2r_\alpha} \sup_{a\in (0,a_\alpha)} \sup_{x\in [C_-r, C_+r]} \frac{w_{t}(x-\RR)^2}{w_{t}(x-K)} \ulim {r_\alpha} \infty 0 .
nodes.label: eq:wt2-over-wt-goes-to-zero

nodes.name: Admissible parameters and T_a.
nodes.statement: Call $(\delta, r_\bullet, r, x)$ ``admissible’’ if $\delta\in (0,\delta^0)$, $r_\bullet \geq r_\alpha$, $r\geq 2r_\bullet$ and $x \in [C_-r, C_+r] \cap [2r_\bullet, \infty)$. We point out that \begin{equation} T_a = \inf \{ n\geq 0 \ : \ (\delta_n, r_\bullet, r, S_n) \text{ is not admissible} \} . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Admissible parameters and T_a.

nodes.name: Equation (92)
nodes.statement: T_a = \inf \{ n\geq 0 \ : \ (\delta_n, r_\bullet, r, S_n) \text{ is not admissible} \} .
nodes.label: eq:Ta-is-admissible

nodes.name: Reduce to E^{(t)}[I e^{2(A+B)}] <= 1.
nodes.statement: A key step of the proof is to show that for every admissible $(\delta, r_\bullet, r, x)$, letting \[ A = - I^{(x,\RR,\delta)}w_t(x-Z) + \E^{(t)}\left[I^{(x,\RR,\delta)} w_t(x-Z)\right] \quad , \quad B = - \frac{I^{(x,\RR,\delta)}} 2 \int w_t(x-y) \d M_Z^{(x,\RR,\delta)}(y) \] then $\E^{(t)}[I^{(x, \RR, \delta)} \e^{2(A+B)}] \leq 1$; let us prove it.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to E^{(t)}[I e^{2(A+B)}] <= 1.

nodes.name: Bounds on A and B.
nodes.statement: Obviously $|A|\leq w_t(x-\RR)$ from \eqref{eq:2def-ZI-vol}. By the analogue of \eqref{eq:Palm-controle-M} (using \eqref{eq:2def-Palm-vol} and \eqref{eq:2def-Palm-mean-vol}) applied to the new $M_z^{(r,\RR,\delta)}$ we have $M_z^{(x,\RR,\delta)}(\R) \leq \frac{\delta}{w_t(x-\RR)}-1$ on $E(r,\RR,\delta)$ for every $z, x, \RR, \delta$, hence $-\frac\delta 2 \leq B\leq 0$. Then \begin{equation*} \E^{(t)}[B] \geq -\frac{w_t(x-\RR)}{2} \E^{(t)}\left[\ind{E(x,\RR,\delta)} (\chi(\R)-1)\chi(\R)) \right] \geq -\sigma^2 w_t(x-\RR) \end{equation*} as soon as $t\in [0,t_0)$ by \eqref{eq:2variance-chi-vol}, where we take $t_0>0$ smaller than in Proposition \ref{prop:2convolution-w-vol} if necessary.
nodes.statement_short: Bounds on A and B.

nodes.name: Upper bound E[B] <= -c w_t(x-K).
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by \eqref{eq:bound-Et-by-2E} and dominated convergence \begin{align*} \sup_{t\in [0,t_0)} \E^{(t)}\left[(1-\ind{E(x,\RR,\delta)}) \chi(\R) (\chi(\R)-1) \right] \leq 2\E\left[(1-\ind{E(x,\RR,\delta)}) \chi(\R) (\chi(\R)-1) \right] \ulim {r_0} \infty 0 \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \sup_{t\in [0,t_0)} \E^{(t)}\left[ \chi((-\infty, K)) (\chi(\R)-1) \right] \leq 2 \E\left[ \chi((-\infty, K)) (\chi(\R)-1) \right] \ulim K {-\infty} 0 , \end{align*} which together with \eqref{eq:2variance-chi-vol} means that we can find $K\in\R$ that only depends on $t_0$ such that, taking $r_\alpha$ larger if necessary, \begin{align*} \inf_{t\in[0,t_0)} \inf_{r\geq 2r_\alpha} \inf_{\delta \in (0,\delta^0)} \E^{(t)}\left[ \ind{E(x,\RR,\delta)} \chi([K,\infty)) (\chi(\R)-1) \right] \geq \frac{\sigma^2}{2} , \end{align*} hence $\E^{(t)}[B] \leq - c w_t(x-K)$ for every $x\in [C_-r, C_+r]$, where $c=\sigma^2/4$.
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound E[B] <= -c w_t(x-K).

nodes.name: Conclude as before.
nodes.statement: We deduce \[ \E^{(t)}\left[ I^{(x,\RR,\delta)} \e^{2(A+B)} \right] \leq 1 - c w_t(x-K) + 4(\sigma^2+1) w_t(x-\RR)^2 . \] By \eqref{eq:wt2-over-wt-goes-to-zero}, taking $r_\alpha$ larger if necessary, we can thus ensure that for every admissible $(\delta, r_\bullet, r, x)$ we have $t(r,\alpha)<t_0$ and $\E^{(t)}\left[ I^{(x,\RR,\delta)} \e^{2(A+B)} \right] \leq 1$. The uniform integrability and the bound on the conditional expectation follows as in Lemma \ref{lem:discount-UI}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude as before.

nodes.name: Feynman–Kac representation of w_t
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha>0$, $0<C_-<1<C_+<\infty$ and $a\in (0,a_\alpha)$, recalling $a_\alpha$, $r_\alpha$ and $T_a$ from Lemma \ref{lem:2discount-UI-vol}, there exist two functions $\underline{\delta}(y)\ulim y \infty 0$ with values in $(0,\delta^0)$ and $g(y) \ulim y \infty 0$ such that for every $A>0$, $r\geq 2r_\alpha$, $x \in [C_- r, C_+ r]$ and every $t\in[0,t(r,\alpha)] $, letting $\delta_n = \underline{\delta}(r)$ for every $n$, $R_n = \RR := a/\sqrt{w_t(C_- r)}$ for every $n$, and $S_0 = r$ a.s., writing $\tau_x = \inf\{ n\geq 0 : S_n \leq x \}$ and $T' = \inf(\tau_x, A/w(x), T_a)$, \begin{equation} \left| w_t(r) - \E^{(t)}\left[ W^{(r)}_{T'}\right] \right| \leq A w_t(x) g(x) . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Tilted Feynman–Kac representation: |w_t(r) - E^{(t)}[W_{T'}]| <= A w_t(x) g(x).
nodes.label: cor:2Feynman-Kac-vol

nodes.name: Equation (93)
nodes.statement: \left| w_t(r) - \E^{(t)}\left[ W^{(r)}_{T'}\right] \right| \leq A w_t(x) g(x) .
nodes.label: eq:2FK-vol

nodes.name: Proof of the tilted Feynman–Kac representation
nodes.statement: By Corollary \ref{cor:2uniform-limit-r2wt}, up to taking $r_\alpha$ larger, using that $t(r,\alpha) = t(C_+ r, C_+^2 \alpha)$, we have for every $z\in [C_- r/2, C_+ r]$ and every $t\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]$ \[ \frac{c((C_-/2)^2 \alpha)}{2 z^2} \leq w_t(z) \leq \frac{12 \eta^2}{\sigma^2 z^2} . \] Let $m = C_- r/2$. Recall from \eqref{eq:Ta-is-admissible} that on $\{T' > n\}$, $m \leq S_n-R_n \leq C_+r$. Together with Lemma \ref{lem:refined-Markov}, we get a function $g_1(z)\ulim z 0 0$ (that only depends on the law of $\Lambda$ and $\chi$ under $\P$) such that on $\{T'>n\}$, for $c_1 = \frac{48 \eta^2}{\sigma^2 C_-^2}$, \begin{align*} &C_\mathrm{rem} |\mathrm{Remainder}_t(S_n, R_n, \delta_n)| \\ \leq& \ \P(\Lambda>R_n) + \P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\delta_n}{w_t(S_n-R_n)}\right) + (\sigma^2+1) w_t(S_n-R_n)^2(w(S_n-R_n)+\delta_n) \\ \leq& \ \frac{w_t(m)^2}{a^2} g_1\left(\frac{w_t(m)}{a^2}\right) + \frac{w_t(m)^2}{\delta_n^2} g_1\left(\frac{w_t(m)}{\delta_n}\right) + (\sigma^2+1) w_t(m)^2 (w_t(m)+\delta_n) \\ \leq& \ \frac{c_1^2}{r^4} g_1\left(\frac{c_1}{a^2 r^2}\right) + \frac{c_1^2}{r^4 \underline{\delta}(r)^2} g_1\left(\frac{c_1}{\underline{\delta}(r) r^2}\right) + \frac{c_1 (\sigma^2+1)}{r^4}\left( \frac{c_1}{r^2} + \underline{\delta}(r)\right) \end{align*} and we see that we can find $\underline{\delta}(r)$ that goes to zero sufficiently slowly as $r\to\infty$ that this expression is $o(r^{-4})$ uniformly in $t$. Use the analogue of Proposition \ref{prop:almost-martingale} and the stopping theorem as in the proof of Corollary \ref{cor:Feynman-Kac}: \begin{align*} w_t(r) = \E^{(t)}\left[ W_{T'}^{(r)} \right] - \E^{(t)}\left[ \sum_{k=0}^{T'-1} \kW^{(r)}_k \mathrm{Remainder}_t(S_k, R_k, \delta_k) \right] . \end{align*} By Lemma \ref{lem:2discount-UI-vol}, on $\{T_a>n\} \supset \{T'>n\}$ we have $\E^{(t)}\left[\kW^{(r)}_{n+1} \, | \, \FF_n \right] \leq 1$. With this, together with our upper bound on the remainder and our lower bound on $w_t(x)$, and following the same ideas as for Corollary \ref{cor:Feynman-Kac}, we find $g(z) \to 0$ as $z\to \infty$ that makes \eqref{eq:2FK-vol} hold.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the remainder by o(r^{-4}) uniformly in t via the refined Markov inequality, then optional stopping.

nodes.name: Two-sided bounds on w_t on the relevant range.
nodes.statement: By Corollary \ref{cor:2uniform-limit-r2wt}, up to taking $r_\alpha$ larger, using that $t(r,\alpha) = t(C_+ r, C_+^2 \alpha)$, we have for every $z\in [C_- r/2, C_+ r]$ and every $t\in [0,t(r,\alpha)]$ \[ \frac{c((C_-/2)^2 \alpha)}{2 z^2} \leq w_t(z) \leq \frac{12 \eta^2}{\sigma^2 z^2} . \]
nodes.statement_short: Two-sided bounds on w_t on the relevant range.

nodes.name: Remainder is o(r^{-4}) for a suitable delta(r).
nodes.statement: Let $m = C_- r/2$. Recall from \eqref{eq:Ta-is-admissible} that on $\{T' > n\}$, $m \leq S_n-R_n \leq C_+r$. Together with Lemma \ref{lem:refined-Markov}, we get a function $g_1(z)\ulim z 0 0$ (that only depends on the law of $\Lambda$ and $\chi$ under $\P$) such that on $\{T'>n\}$, for $c_1 = \frac{48 \eta^2}{\sigma^2 C_-^2}$, \begin{align*} &C_\mathrm{rem} |\mathrm{Remainder}_t(S_n, R_n, \delta_n)| \\ \leq& \ \P(\Lambda>R_n) + \P\left(\chi(\R)>\frac{\delta_n}{w_t(S_n-R_n)}\right) + (\sigma^2+1) w_t(S_n-R_n)^2(w(S_n-R_n)+\delta_n) \\ \leq& \ \frac{w_t(m)^2}{a^2} g_1\left(\frac{w_t(m)}{a^2}\right) + \frac{w_t(m)^2}{\delta_n^2} g_1\left(\frac{w_t(m)}{\delta_n}\right) + (\sigma^2+1) w_t(m)^2 (w_t(m)+\delta_n) \\ \leq& \ \frac{c_1^2}{r^4} g_1\left(\frac{c_1}{a^2 r^2}\right) + \frac{c_1^2}{r^4 \underline{\delta}(r)^2} g_1\left(\frac{c_1}{\underline{\delta}(r) r^2}\right) + \frac{c_1 (\sigma^2+1)}{r^4}\left( \frac{c_1}{r^2} + \underline{\delta}(r)\right) \end{align*} and we see that we can find $\underline{\delta}(r)$ that goes to zero sufficiently slowly as $r\to\infty$ that this expression is $o(r^{-4})$ uniformly in $t$.
nodes.statement_short: Remainder is o(r^{-4}) for a suitable delta(r).

nodes.name: Optional stopping and supermartingale bound.
nodes.statement: Use the analogue of Proposition \ref{prop:almost-martingale} and the stopping theorem as in the proof of Corollary \ref{cor:Feynman-Kac}: \begin{align*} w_t(r) = \E^{(t)}\left[ W_{T'}^{(r)} \right] - \E^{(t)}\left[ \sum_{k=0}^{T'-1} \kW^{(r)}_k \mathrm{Remainder}_t(S_k, R_k, \delta_k) \right] . \end{align*} By Lemma \ref{lem:2discount-UI-vol}, on $\{T_a>n\} \supset \{T'>n\}$ we have $\E^{(t)}\left[\kW^{(r)}_{n+1} \, | \, \FF_n \right] \leq 1$. With this, together with our upper bound on the remainder and our lower bound on $w_t(x)$, and following the same ideas as for Corollary \ref{cor:Feynman-Kac}, we find $g(z) \to 0$ as $z\to \infty$ that makes \eqref{eq:2FK-vol} hold.
nodes.statement_short: Optional stopping and supermartingale bound.

nodes.name: Subsequential limit L(alpha)
nodes.statement: Along every sequence $(r_k)_{k\geq 1}$, letting $t_k = t(r_k,\alpha)$, we can find some $\LL(\alpha)$ such that, up to extracting a subsequence, we have $r^2 w_t(r) \to \LL(\alpha)$. Clearly $\LL(0) = \frac{6\eta^2}{\sigma^2}$.
nodes.section: 5.7 The functional equation of the limit

nodes.name: Ratio limit phi_alpha
nodes.statement: Like in Section \ref{sec:ratio-limit}, by diagonal extraction we can find $\phi_\alpha$ and a subsequence $(r_{k_n})_n$ such that in addition, for every rational $y\geq 0$ \begin{equation} \frac{w_{t_{k_n}}\left(r_{k_n} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_{t_{k_n}}(r_{k_n})}}\right)}{w_{t_{k_n}}(r_{k_n})} \ulim k \infty \phi_\alpha(y) . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.7 The functional equation of the limit

nodes.name: Equation (94)
nodes.statement: \frac{w_{t_{k_n}}\left(r_{k_n} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{w_{t_{k_n}}(r_{k_n})}}\right)}{w_{t_{k_n}}(r_{k_n})} \ulim k \infty \phi_\alpha(y) .
nodes.section: 5.7 The functional equation of the limit
nodes.label: eq:2cv-phialpha

nodes.name: Continuity of phi_alpha
nodes.statement: By the same reasoning as in Proposition \ref{prop:continuity-phi} with Lemma \ref{lem:continuity-w-broad} replaced by Lemma \ref{lem:2continuity-w-broad-volume}, $\phi_\alpha$ is continuous, non-increasing, positive, $\phi_\alpha(0)=1$, and the convergence in \eqref{eq:2cv-phialpha} holds uniformly (in $y$) over every compact of $[0,\infty)$.
nodes.section: 5.7 The functional equation of the limit

nodes.name: Functional equation for phi_alpha
nodes.statement: Any limit $\phi_\alpha$ in \eqref{eq:2cv-phialpha} satisfies \begin{equation} \phi_\alpha(y) = \E^{y/\eta}\left[\exp\left( -\frac{\sigma^2}{2} \int_0^{\tau_0} \phi_\alpha(\eta B_s) \d s - \frac{\alpha \LL(0)}{\LL(\alpha)} \tau_0 \right)\right] . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.7 The functional equation of the limit
nodes.statement_short: phi_alpha satisfies a Feynman–Kac equation with an extra killing rate alpha L(0)/L(alpha).
nodes.label: prop:2func-equation-phi-vol

nodes.name: Equation (95)
nodes.statement: \phi_\alpha(y) = \E^{y/\eta}\left[\exp\left( -\frac{\sigma^2}{2} \int_0^{\tau_0} \phi_\alpha(\eta B_s) \d s - \frac{\alpha \LL(0)}{\LL(\alpha)} \tau_0 \right)\right] .
nodes.section: 5.7 The functional equation of the limit
